pali_mahasangiti: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; Manasā ce paduṭṭhena, bhāsati vā karoti vā; Tato naṁ dukkhamanveti, cakkaṁva vahato padaṁ.
english_sujato: Intention shapes experiences; intention is first, they’re made by intention. If with corrupt intent you speak or act, suffering follows you, like a wheel, the ox’s foot.
interlinear_pali: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā, manasā ce paduṭṭhena bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṁ dukkham-anveti cakkaṁ va vahato padaṁ.
interlinear_english: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, (their quality is) made by mind, if with a base mind one speaks or acts, through that suffering follows him like a wheel (follows) the ox’s foot.
interlinear_notes: This meaning of this line has to be understood by reference to the whole verse, which is an ethical statement about the quality of mind bringing suitable returns. I believe many mistranslations have occurred by treating it as a descriptive, quasi-Abhidhammic, statement about the relationship between mind and mental objects.

In parallel versions the reading is always given as manojavā, impelled (or driven) by mind, which might seem more congruous with the early teaching. This reading also occurs in Peṭakopadesa, PTS p. 164, which reads in the context of this verse: Manojavā ti yattha mano gacchati tattha ime dhammā gacchantī ti manojavā; impelled by mind means wherever the mind goes there these thoughts go, (therefore) impelled by mind is said.
It is curious that vahatu, an ox, is not found in PED or CPED.
We see here and it many other places that the verb is made to work twice; in Pāḷi the meaning is clear, but in English we have to restate the verb, otherwise it is ambiguous.

This verse evidently belongs with the following one, and must have been composed together, but the commentary assigns very different occasions to their composition. The same could be said about many others pairs of verses, and not only in this Chapter.
narrative_pali: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā, manasā ce paduṭṭhena bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṁ dukkham-anveti cakkaṁ va vahato padaṁ.
narrative_english: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, their quality is made by mind, if with base mind one speaks or acts through that, suffering follows one like a wheel follows ox’s foot.

pali_mahasangiti: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; Manasā ce pasannena, bhāsati vā karoti vā; Tato naṁ sukhamanveti, chāyāva anapāyinī.
english_sujato: Intention shapes experiences; intention is first, they’re made by intention. If with pure intent you speak or act, happiness follows you like a shadow that never leaves.
interlinear_pali: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā, manasā ce pasannena bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṁ sukham-anveti chāyā va anapāyinī.
interlinear_english: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, (their quality is) made by mind, if with pure mind one speaks or acts, through that happiness follows him like a shadow which does not depart.
narrative_pali: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā, manasā ce pasannena bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṁ sukham-anveti chāyā va anapāyinī.
narrative_english: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, their quality is made by mind, if with pure mind one speaks or acts through that happiness follows one like shadow which does not depart.

pali_mahasangiti: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ ahāsi me; Ye ca taṁ upanayhanti, veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati.
english_sujato: “They abused me, they hit me! They beat me, they robbed me!” For those who bear such a grudge, hatred is never laid to rest.
interlinear_pali: “Akkocchi maṁ, avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ, ahāsi me”, ye ca taṁ upanayhanti veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati.
interlinear_english: “He abused me, he struck at me, he overcame me, he robbed me,” those who bear ill-will towards this their hatred is never appeased.
interlinear_notes: Presumably me is ablative, he took from me, he robbed from me.

We might have expected the genitive, not the nominative, form here, yesaṁ, for those..., the line could easily be rewritten to fit the metre: yesañ-ca upanayhanti, and in the next line: yesaṁ na upanayhanti.
narrative_pali: “Akkocchi maṁ, avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ, ahāsi me”, ye ca taṁ upanayhanti, veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati.
narrative_english: “He abused me, he struck at me, he overcame me, he robbed me,” those who bear ill-will towards this, their hatred is never appeased.

pali_mahasangiti: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ ahāsi me; Ye ca taṁ nupanayhanti, veraṁ tesūpasammati.
english_sujato: “They abused me, they hit me! They beat me, they robbed me!” For those who bear no such grudge, hatred is laid to rest.
interlinear_pali: “Akkocchi maṁ, avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ, ahāsi me”, ye taṁ na upanayhanti veraṁ tesūpasammati.
interlinear_english: “He abused me, he struck at me, he overcame me, he robbed me,” those who do not bear ill-will towards this their hatred is appeased.
interlinear_notes: This is an unexpected formation here, we either have tesaṁ + upasammati giving sandhi tesūpa-, or the locative is being used tesu + upasammati; if it is the former, then we might have expected tesañ-ca sammati, to match the verb in the preceding verse.

pali_mahasangiti: Na hi verena verāni, sammantīdha kudācanaṁ; Averena ca sammanti, esa dhammo sanantano.
english_sujato: For never is hatred laid to rest by hate, it’s laid to rest by love: this is an ancient teaching.
interlinear_pali: Na hi verena verāni sammantīdha kudācanaṁ, averena ca sammanti, esa dhammo sanantano.
interlinear_english: For not by hatred do hatreds cease at any time in this place, they only cease with non-hatred, this truth is (surely) eternal.
interlinear_notes: Interestingly an alternative name for what is now known as Hinduism is the sanātana (variant form of sanantana) Dharma; this is the earliest use of the phrase I know of.
This verse and the one that follows do not form a pair, but seem to have been attracted into the collection at this point by word collocation on vera.
narrative_pali: Na hi verena verāni sammantīdha kudācanaṁ, averena ca sammanti, esa dhammo sanantano.
narrative_english: For not by hatred do hatreds cease at any time in this place, they only cease with non-hatred, this truth is surely eternal.

pali_mahasangiti: Pare ca na vijānanti, mayamettha yamāmase; Ye ca tattha vijānanti, tato sammanti medhagā.
english_sujato: When others do not understand, let us, who do understand this, restrain ourselves in this regard; for that is how conflicts are laid to rest.
interlinear_pali: Pare ca na vijānanti mayam-ettha yamāmase, ye ca tattha vijānanti tato sammanti medhagā.
interlinear_english: The others do not understand that we should restrain ourselves here, but (for) those here who do understand, through that, (their) dissensions will cease.
interlinear_notes: As in verse three the genitive would have made more sense here: yesaṁ tattha vijānanti..., for those who do understand...

pali_mahasangiti: Subhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ; Bhojanamhi cāmattaññuṁ, kusītaṁ hīnavīriyaṁ; Taṁ ve pasahati māro, vāto rukkhaṁva dubbalaṁ.
english_sujato: Those who contemplate the beautiful, their faculties unrestrained, immoderate in eating, lazy, lacking energy: Māra strikes them down like the wind, a feeble tree.
interlinear_pali: Subhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ, bhojanamhi amattaññuṁ, kusītaṁ hīnavīriyaṁ – taṁ ve pasahati Māro vāto rukkhaṁ va dubbalaṁ.
interlinear_english: Living contemplating what is pleasant, uncontrolled in sense faculties, not knowing the limit in food, indolent, low in energy – Māra surely overthrows that one, like wind (overthrows) a weak tree.
interlinear_notes: In the commentary it is clear that viharantaṁ belongs with subhānupassiṁ, not with indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ, as many translations have it. Cf. kāye kāyānupassī viharati, etc. from Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasuttaṁ (DN 22), see elsewhere on this website.
narrative_pali: Subhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ, bhojanamhi amattaññuṁ, kusītaṁ hīnavīriyaṁ – taṁ ve pasahati Māro vāto rukkhaṁ va dubbalaṁ.
narrative_english: Contemplating what is pleasant, with sense faculties uncontrolled,

pali_mahasangiti: Asubhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, Indriyesu susaṁvutaṁ; Bhojanamhi ca mattaññuṁ, Saddhaṁ āraddhavīriyaṁ; Taṁ ve nappasahati māro, Vāto selaṁva pabbataṁ.
english_sujato: Those who contemplate the ugly, their faculties well-restrained, eating in moderation, faithful and energetic: Māra cannot strike them down, like the wind, a rocky mountain.
interlinear_pali: Asubhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu susaṁvutaṁ, bhojanamhi ca mattaññuṁ, saddhaṁ āraddhavīriyaṁ – taṁ ve nappasahati Māro vāto selaṁ va pabbataṁ.
interlinear_english: Living contemplating the unpleasant, well-controlled in sense faculties, and knowing the limit in food, faithful, with energy aroused – Māra does not overthrow that one, just as wind does not (overthrow) a mountain made of rock.
interlinear_notes: The form here does not arise through sandhi; na is so closely associated with the verb it is modifying it becomes part of it, as we see frequently with the negative.

pali_mahasangiti: Anikkasāvo kāsāvaṁ, yo vatthaṁ paridahissati; Apeto damasaccena, na so kāsāvamarahati.
english_sujato: One who, not free of stains themselves, would wear the robe stained in ocher, bereft of self-control and truth: they are not worthy of the ocher robe.
interlinear_pali: Anikkasāvo kāsāvaṁ yo vatthaṁ paridahessati, apeto damasaccena na so kāsāvam-arahati.
interlinear_english: The one who, while still impure, would wear the renunciant’s robe, unendowed with restraint and truth, is not worthy of the renunciant’s robe.
interlinear_notes: The form is a double negative, a + nis + kasāva; the word is related is to the one following, the kāsāva, or discoloured robe.
narrative_pali: Anikkasāvo kāsāvaṁ yo vatthaṁ paridahessati,
narrative_english: apeto damasaccena na so kāsāvam-arahati. The one who, while he’s still impure, would wear the renunciant’s robe, unendowed with restraint and truth, he is not worthy of that robe.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca vantakasāvassa, sīlesu susamāhito; Upeto damasaccena, sa ve kāsāvamarahati.
english_sujato: One who’s purged all their stains, steady in ethics, possessed of self-control and of truth, they are truly worthy of the ocher robe.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca vantakasāvassa, sīlesu susamāhito, upeto damasaccena sa ve kāsāvam-arahati.
interlinear_english: The one who, steady in virtue, throws out (any) impurity, endowed with restraint and truth, is indeed worthy of the renunciant’s robe.
interlinear_notes: It is unexpected that the opposite form, sīlesu asamāhito, unsteady in virtue, is not found in the corresponding line in the previous verse.

pali_mahasangiti: Asāre sāramatino, sāre cāsāradassino; Te sāraṁ nādhigacchanti, micchāsaṅkappagocarā.
english_sujato: Thinking the inessential is essential, seeing the essential as inessential; they don’t realize the essential, for wrong thoughts are their habitat.
interlinear_pali: Asāre sāramatino, sāre cāsāradassino, te sāraṁ nādhigacchanti, micchāsaṅkappagocarā.
interlinear_english: Finding the essential in what is unessential, and seeing the unessential in what is essential, they do not understand what is essential, and resort to wrong intention.
interlinear_notes: This parses as ca + asāra + dassino; it is not clear to me why ca is found here, as it is not needed by the grammar, the meaning or the metre.
narrative_pali: Asāre sāramatino, sāre cāsāradassino, te sāraṁ nādhigacchanti, micchāsaṅkappagocarā.
narrative_english: Finding the essential in the unessential, seeing the unessential in the essential, they do not understand what is the essential, and resort to wrong intention.

pali_mahasangiti: Sārañca sārato ñatvā, asārañca asārato; Te sāraṁ adhigacchanti, sammāsaṅkappagocarā.
english_sujato: Having known the essential as essential, and the inessential as inessential; they realize the essential, for right thoughts are their habitat.
interlinear_pali: Sārañ-ca sārato ñatvā, asārañ-ca asārato, te sāraṁ adhigacchanti, sammāsaṅkappagocarā.
interlinear_english: Knowing the essential in what is essential, and the unessential in what is unessential, they understand what is essential, and resort to right intention.
interlinear_notes: Interesting use of the ablative here, perhaps indicating the starting point.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathā agāraṁ ducchannaṁ, vuṭṭhī samativijjhati; Evaṁ abhāvitaṁ cittaṁ, rāgo samativijjhati.
english_sujato: Just as rain seeps into a poorly roofed house, lust seeps into an undeveloped mind.
interlinear_pali: Yathā agāraṁ ducchannaṁ vuṭṭhī samativijjhati, evaṁ abhāvitaṁ cittaṁ rāgo samativijjhati.
interlinear_english: Just as the rain penetrates a house with thatching that is poor, so passion penetrates a mind that is undeveloped.
narrative_pali: Yathā agāraṁ ducchannaṁ vuṭṭhī samativijjhati, evaṁ abhāvitaṁ cittaṁ rāgo samativijjhati.
narrative_english: Just as the rain can penetrate a house with thatching that is poor, so also passion penetrates a mind that is undeveloped.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathā agāraṁ suchannaṁ, vuṭṭhī na samativijjhati; Evaṁ subhāvitaṁ cittaṁ, rāgo na samativijjhati.
english_sujato: Just as rain doesn’t seep into a well roofed house, lust doesn’t seep into a well developed mind.
interlinear_pali: Yathā agāraṁ succhannaṁ vuṭṭhī na samativijjhati, evaṁ subhāvitaṁ cittaṁ rāgo na samativijjhati.
interlinear_english: Just as rain does not penetrate a house with thatching that is good, so passion cannot penetrate a mind that is well-developed.
interlinear_notes: This is one of the most perfect of the compositions showing reversal of meaning in the two verses.

pali_mahasangiti: Idha socati pecca socati, Pāpakārī ubhayattha socati; So socati so vihaññati, Disvā kammakiliṭṭhamattano.
english_sujato: Here they grieve, hereafter they grieve, an evildoer grieves in both places. They grieve and fret, seeing their own corrupt deeds.
interlinear_pali: Idha socati, pecca socati, pāpakārī ubhayattha socati, so socati, so vihaññati, disvā kammakiliṭṭham-attano.
interlinear_english: Here he laments, after death he laments, the wicked one laments in both places, he laments, he suffers vexation, seeing the defilement of his own deeds.
interlinear_notes: Here means here in this world. Idha often has this meaning, just as loke, in the world, often means simply here.
Again this and the following verse, which were probably composed together have been separated by the commentary and given different foundation stories.

pali_mahasangiti: Idha modati pecca modati, Katapuñño ubhayattha modati; So modati so pamodati, Disvā kammavisuddhimattano.
english_sujato: Here they rejoice, hereafter they rejoice, one who does good rejoices in both places. They rejoice and celebrate, seeing their own pure deeds.
interlinear_pali: Idha modati, pecca modati, katapuñño ubhayattha modati, so modati, so pamodati, disvā kammavisuddhim-attano.
interlinear_english: Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices, the meritorious one rejoices in both places, he rejoices, he greatly rejoices, seeing the purity of his own deeds.

pali_mahasangiti: Idha tappati pecca tappati, Pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati; “Pāpaṁ me katan”ti tappati, Bhiyyo tappati duggatiṁ gato.
english_sujato: Here they’re tormented, <j>hereafter they’re tormented, an evildoer is tormented in both places. They’re tormented <j>thinking of bad things they’ve done; when gone to a bad place, <j>they’re tormented all the more.
interlinear_pali: Idha tappati, pecca tappati, pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati, “Pāpaṁ mĕ katan”-ti tappati, bhiyyo tappati duggatiṁ gato.
interlinear_english: Here he suffers, after death he suffers, the wicked one suffers in both places, he suffers, thinking: “I have done wickedness,” gone to a bad fate, he suffers much more.
interlinear_notes: This and the following verse, which again belong together, do not have any parallels in other collections of Dhammapadāni, and may have been composed as variations of the preceding pair of verses.

pali_mahasangiti: Idha nandati pecca nandati, Katapuñño ubhayattha nandati; “Puññaṁ me katan”ti nandati, Bhiyyo nandati suggatiṁ gato.
english_sujato: Here they delight, hereafter they delight, one who does good delights in both places. They delight thinking of good things they’ve done; when gone to a good place, they delight all the more.
interlinear_pali: Idha nandati, pecca nandati, katapuñño ubhayattha nandati, “Puññaṁ mĕ katan”-ti nandati, bhiyyo nandati suggatiṁ gato.
interlinear_english: Here she is happy, after death she is happy, the righteous one is happy in both places, she is happy, thinking: “I have done merit,” gone to a good fate, she is happy much more.
interlinear_notes: According to the commentary the verse was spoken about Anāthapiṇḍika’s younger sister.

pali_mahasangiti: Bahumpi ce saṁhita bhāsamāno, Na takkaro hoti naro pamatto; Gopova gāvo gaṇayaṁ paresaṁ, Na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
english_sujato: Much though they may recite scripture, if a negligent person does not apply them, then, like a cowherd who counts the cattle of others, they miss out on the blessings of the ascetic life.
interlinear_pali: Bahum-pi ce sahitaṁ bhāsamāno, na takkaro hoti naro pamatto, gopo va gāvo gaṇayaṁ paresaṁ, na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
interlinear_english: Even though reciting abundant scriptures, the heedless fellow, who does not do (what they say), like a cowboy counting other’s cattle, does not partake of the ascetic life.
interlinear_notes: In Sanskrit the g Veda is called saṁhita (a variant form of this word), but according to the commentary sahita means the Tipiṭaka here.
= taṁ kāro, with assimilation.
narrative_pali: Bahum-pi ce sahitaṁ bhāsamāno, na takkaro hoti naro pamatto, gopo va gāvo gaṇayaṁ paresaṁ, na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti. Even though reciting abundant scriptures,
narrative_english: the heedless one, who does not what they say, like a cowboy counting other’s cattle, does not partake of the ascetic life.

pali_mahasangiti: Appampi ce saṁhita bhāsamāno, Dhammassa hoti anudhammacārī; Rāgañca dosañca pahāya mohaṁ, Sammappajāno suvimuttacitto; Anupādiyāno idha vā huraṁ vā, Sa bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
english_sujato: Little though they may recite scripture, if they live in line with the teaching, having given up greed, hate, and delusion, with deep understanding and heart well freed, not grasping to this life or the next, they share in the blessings of the ascetic life.
interlinear_pali: Appam-pi ce sahitaṁ bhāsamāno, Dhammassa hoti anudhammacārī, rāgañ-ca dosañ-ca pahāya mohaṁ, sammappajāno suvimuttacitto, anupādiyāno idha vā huraṁ vā, sa bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
interlinear_english: Even though reciting but few scriptures, but living righteously in accordance with Dhamma, abandoning greed, hate and delusion, understanding aright, with mind well-released, that one, unattached here and hereafter, (surely) partakes of the ascetic life.

pali_mahasangiti: Appamādo amatapadaṁ, pamādo maccuno padaṁ; Appamattā na mīyanti, ye pamattā yathā matā.
english_sujato: Heedfulness is the state free of death; heedlessness is the state of death. The heedful do not die, while the heedless are like the dead.
interlinear_pali: Appamādo amatapadaṁ, pamādo maccuno padaṁ, appamattā na mīyanti, ye pamattā yathā matā.
interlinear_english: Heedfulness is the deathless state, heedlessness the state of the dead, the heedful do not die, (but) those who are heedless are as if dead.
narrative_pali: Appamādo amatapadaṁ, pamādo maccuno padaṁ, appamattā na mīyanti, ye pamattā yathā matā.
narrative_english: Heedfulness is the deathless state, heedlessness the state of the dead, the heedful do not die, but those who are heedless are as if dead.

pali_mahasangiti: Evaṁ visesato ñatvā, appamādamhi paṇḍitā; Appamāde pamodanti, ariyānaṁ gocare ratā.
english_sujato: Understanding this distinction when it comes to heedfulness, the astute rejoice in heedfulness, happy in the noble ones’ domain.
interlinear_pali: Etaṁ visesato ñatvā appamādamhi paṇḍitā, appamāde pamodanti, Ariyānaṁ gocare ratā.
interlinear_english: The wise, understanding this difference in regard to heedfulness, rejoice in heedfulness, delight in the domain of the Noble Ones.

pali_mahasangiti: Te jhāyino sātatikā, niccaṁ daḷhaparakkamā; Phusanti dhīrā nibbānaṁ, yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.
english_sujato: They who regularly meditate, always staunchly vigorous; the attentive realize extinguishment, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.
interlinear_pali: Te jhāyino sātatikā, niccaṁ daḷhaparakkamā, phusanti dhīrā Nibbānaṁ, yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.
interlinear_english: Those who meditate all the time, constant and firm in their effort, those wise ones reach Nibbāna, the unsurpassed release from (all) bonds.

pali_mahasangiti: Uṭṭhānavato satīmato, Sucikammassa nisammakārino; Saññatassa dhammajīvino, Appamattassa yasobhivaḍḍhati.
english_sujato: For the hard-working and mindful, pure of deed and attentive, restrained, living righteously, and diligent, their reputation only grows.
interlinear_pali: Uṭṭhānavato satīmato, sucikammassa nisammakārino, saññatassa ca Dhammajīvino, appamattassa yasobhivaḍḍhati.
interlinear_english: For he who is active, mindful, pure in deeds, considerate, self-controlled, living by Dhamma, heedful, fame greatly increases.
interlinear_notes: The string of genitives in this verse allows us to see side by side some of the different forms the case ending can take: -vato (neuter), -ato (neuter), -assa (masculine) and -ino (masculine).
narrative_pali: Uṭṭhānavato satīmato sucikammassa nisammakārino, saññatassa ca Dhammajīvino appamattassa yasobhivaḍḍhati.
narrative_english: For he who is active, mindful, pure in deeds and considerate, self-controlled, living by Dhamma,

pali_mahasangiti: Uṭṭhānenappamādena, saṁyamena damena ca; Dīpaṁ kayirātha medhāvī, yaṁ ogho nābhikīrati.
english_sujato: By hard work and diligence, by restraint and by self-control, a smart person would build an island that the floods cannot overflow.
interlinear_pali: Uṭṭhānen’ appamādena saṁyamena damena ca, dīpaṁ kayirātha medhāvī yaṁ ogho nābhikīrati.
interlinear_english: Through activity, heedfulness, through self-control and through restraint, the sage should make an island that no flood waters can overcome.
narrative_pali: Uṭṭhānen’ appamādena saṁyamena damena ca, dīpaṁ kayirātha medhāvī yaṁ ogho nābhikīrati.
narrative_english: Through activity, heedfulness, through self-control and through restraint,

pali_mahasangiti: Pamādamanuyuñjanti, bālā dummedhino janā; Appamādañca medhāvī, dhanaṁ seṭṭhaṁva rakkhati.
english_sujato: Fools and simpletons devote themselves to negligence. But the wise protect diligence as their best treasure.
interlinear_pali: Pamādam-anuyuñjanti bālā dummedhino janā, appamādañ-ca medhāvī dhanaṁ seṭṭhaṁ va rakkhati.
interlinear_english: The foolish and stupid people cultivate heedlessness, but the sagacious one guards heedfulness just as his greatest wealth.
narrative_pali: Pamādam-anuyuñjanti bālā dummedhino janā, appamādañ-ca medhāvī dhanaṁ seṭṭhaṁ va rakkhati. Foolish, stupid people cultivate heedlessness,
narrative_english: the sage guards heedfulness just as his greatest wealth.

pali_mahasangiti: Mā pamādamanuyuñjetha, mā kāmaratisanthavaṁ; Appamatto hi jhāyanto, pappoti vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: Don’t devote yourself to negligence, or delight in erotic intimacy. For if you’re diligent and meditate, you’ll attain abundant happiness.
interlinear_pali: Mā pamādam-anuyuñjetha mā kāmaratisanthavaṁ, appamatto hi jhāyanto pappoti vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: Do not cultivate heedlessness, do not be acquainted with delight in sensual pleasure, for the heedful one, meditating, (surely) attains great happiness.

pali_mahasangiti: Pamādaṁ appamādena, yadā nudati paṇḍito; Paññāpāsādamāruyha, asoko sokiniṁ pajaṁ; Pabbataṭṭhova bhūmaṭṭhe, dhīro bāle avekkhati.
english_sujato: When the astute dispel negligence by means of diligence, ascending the palace of wisdom, sorrowless, they behold this generation of sorrow, as an attentive one on a mountain top beholds the fools below.
interlinear_pali: Pamādaṁ appamādena yadā nudati paṇḍito, paññāpāsādam-āruyha, asoko sokiniṁ pajaṁ, pabbataṭṭho va bhummaṭṭhe dhīro bāle avekkhati.
interlinear_english: When the wise one eliminates heedlessness with his heedfulness, and mounts the palace of wisdom, griefless, (he looks) on grieving people; the wise one, like one standing on a mountain, looks down on the fools, who are standing on the plains.
narrative_pali: Pamādaṁ appamādena yadā nudati paṇḍito, paññāpāsādam-āruyha, asoko sokiniṁ pajaṁ, pabbataṭṭho va bhummaṭṭhe dhīro bāle avekkhati.
narrative_english: When the wise one eliminates heedlessness with his heedfulness, and mounts the palace of wisdom, griefless, he looks on grieving people; the wise one, like one standing on a mountain, looks down on the fools, who are standing on the plains.

pali_mahasangiti: Appamatto pamattesu, suttesu bahujāgaro; Abalassaṁva sīghasso, hitvā yāti sumedhaso.
english_sujato: Heedful among the heedless, wide awake while others sleep— a true sage leaves them behind, like a swift horse passing a feeble.
interlinear_pali: Appamatto pamattesu, suttesu bahujāgaro, abalassaṁ va sīghasso hitvā, yāti sumedhaso.
interlinear_english: Heedful amongst the heedless ones, wakeful amongst the ones who sleep, like a swift horse who abandons a weak horse, the true sage moves on.

pali_mahasangiti: Appamādena maghavā, devānaṁ seṭṭhataṁ gato; Appamādaṁ pasaṁsanti, pamādo garahito sadā.
english_sujato: Maghavā became chief of the gods by means of diligence. People praise diligence, while negligence is always deplored.
interlinear_pali: Appamādena Maghavā devānaṁ seṭṭhataṁ gato, appamādaṁ pasaṁsanti, pamādo garahito sadā.
interlinear_english: Through heedfulness Maghavā attained leadership of the gods, (the good) praise heedfulness, (but) heedlessness is always blamed.
interlinear_notes: Maghavā is another name for Sakka, how he became Sakka is told in the commentary. The verse assumes the auditor has some knowledge of the legend, or it may be, that the verse is extracted from the story.
narrative_pali: Appamādena Maghavā devānaṁ seṭṭhataṁ gato, appamādaṁ pasaṁsanti, pamādo garahito sadā.
narrative_english: Through heedfulness did Maghavā attain leadership of the gods, the good always praise heedfulness, but heedlessness is always blamed.

pali_mahasangiti: Appamādarato bhikkhu, pamāde bhayadassi vā; Saṁyojanaṁ aṇuṁ thūlaṁ, ḍahaṁ aggīva gacchati.
english_sujato: A mendicant who loves diligence, seeing fear in negligence— advances like fire, burning up fetters big and small.
interlinear_pali: Appamādarato bhikkhu, pamāde bhayadassivā, saṁyojanaṁ aṇuṁ-thūlaṁ ḍahaṁ aggīva gacchati.
interlinear_english: A monastic who delights in heedfulness, seeing danger in heedlessness, advances like burning fire against the fetter, small or large.
interlinear_notes: It is odd that saṁyojanaṁ is singular, where we might have expected a plural, saṁyojanā. The commentary defines it as one of the ten kinds of fetter. The idea is that his heedfulness burns the fetter, as a fire burns and consumes whatever it is attached to. Same at v. 221 below.

pali_mahasangiti: Appamādarato bhikkhu, pamāde bhayadassi vā; Abhabbo parihānāya, nibbānasseva santike.
english_sujato: A mendicant who loves diligence, seeing fear in negligence— such a one can’t decline, and has drawn near to extinguishment.
interlinear_pali: Appamādarato bhikkhu, pamāde bhayadassivā, abhabbo parihānāya: Nibbānasseva santike.
interlinear_english: A monastic who delights in heedfulness, seeing danger in heedlessness, is unable to fall away: he is well-nigh to Nibbāna.
interlinear_notes: This is the infinitive-like dative, which we also use in English.

pali_mahasangiti: Phandanaṁ capalaṁ cittaṁ, dūrakkhaṁ dunnivārayaṁ; Ujuṁ karoti medhāvī, usukārova tejanaṁ.
english_sujato: The mind quivers and shakes, hard to guard, hard to curb. The discerning straighten it out, like a fletcher an arrow.
interlinear_pali: Phandanaṁ capalaṁ cittaṁ, dūrakkhaṁ dunnivārayaṁ, ujuṁ karoti medhāvī, usukāro va tejanaṁ.
interlinear_english: An agitated, unsteady mind, difficult to guard, difficult to ward, the sagacious one makes straight, as a fletcher does his arrow.
interlinear_notes: In every case in this chapter citta is in the singular, and must mean mind, not thoughts (plural) as many translations have it, which also makes more sense contextually.
narrative_pali: Phandanaṁ capalaṁ cittaṁ, dūrakkhaṁ dunnivārayaṁ, ujuṁ karoti medhāvī, usukāro va tejanaṁ.
narrative_english: An agitated and unsteady mind, difficult to guard, difficult to ward, the sagacious one will make straight, as a fletcher does his arrow.

pali_mahasangiti: Vārijova thale khitto, okamokataubbhato; Pariphandatidaṁ cittaṁ, māradheyyaṁ pahātave.
english_sujato: Like a fish pulled from the sea and cast upon the shore, this mind flounders about, trying to throw off Māra’s dominion.
interlinear_pali: Vārijo va thale khitto, oka-m-okata ubbhato, pariphandatidaṁ cittaṁ, Māradheyyaṁ pahātave.
interlinear_english: Like a fish thrown up on dry land, pulled out from its watery home, the mind is agitated, (one ought) to throw off the sway of Māra.
interlinear_notes: Oka has both meanings: water and home.

The grammar is not clear here, and words need to be supplied to make good sense, the bold words are added into these translations: Norman: this thought quivers all over in order to escape the dominion of Māra; Carter: This mind flaps; [Fit] to discard [is] Māra’s sway; Burlingame: These thoughts writhe and quiver in their efforts to shake off the power of Māra. I think the ethical force of the verse really demands the imperative interpretation.

pali_mahasangiti: Dunniggahassa lahuno, yatthakāmanipātino; Cittassa damatho sādhu, cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
english_sujato: Hard to hold back, flighty, alighting where it will; it’s good to tame the mind; a tamed mind leads to bliss.
interlinear_pali: Dunniggahassa lahuno yatthakāmanipātino, cittassa damatho sādhu, cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
interlinear_english: * For the mind that is difficult to subdue, flighty, flitting wherever it will, restraint is good, a restrained mind brings happiness.

pali_mahasangiti: Sududdasaṁ sunipuṇaṁ, yatthakāmanipātinaṁ; Cittaṁ rakkhetha medhāvī, cittaṁ guttaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
english_sujato: So hard to see, so subtle, alighting where it will; the discerning protect the mind, a guarded mind leads to bliss.
interlinear_pali: Sududdasaṁ sunipuṇaṁ yatthakāmanipātinaṁ, cittaṁ rakkhetha medhāvī, cittaṁ guttaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
interlinear_english: Hard to see, very subtle, flitting wherever it will, the sage should guard the mind, a guarded mind brings happiness.
narrative_pali: Sududdasaṁ sunipuṇaṁ yatthakāmanipātinaṁ, cittaṁ rakkhetha medhāvī, cittaṁ guttaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
narrative_english: Hard to see and very subtle, and flitting wherever it will,

pali_mahasangiti: Dūraṅgamaṁ ekacaraṁ, asarīraṁ guhāsayaṁ; Ye cittaṁ saṁyamissanti, mokkhanti mārabandhanā.
english_sujato: The mind travels far, wandering alone; incorporeal, it lies hidden in the heart. Those who will restrain the mind are freed from Māra’s bonds.
interlinear_pali: Dūraṅgamaṁ ekacaraṁ, asarīraṁ guhāsayaṁ, ye cittaṁ saññam-essanti, mokkhanti Mārabandhanā.
interlinear_english: * Those who will restrain the mind that roams far, is lonesome, without a body, hidden, gain release from the bonds of Māra.
narrative_pali: Dūraṅgamaṁ ekacaraṁ, asarīraṁ guhāsayaṁ, ye cittaṁ saññam-essanti, mokkhanti Mārabandhanā.
narrative_english: Those who will restrain the mind that roams far away, and is lonesome,

pali_mahasangiti: Anavaṭṭhitacittassa, saddhammaṁ avijānato; Pariplavapasādassa, paññā na paripūrati.
english_sujato: Those of unsteady mind, who don’t understand the true teaching, and whose confidence wavers, do not perfect their wisdom.
interlinear_pali: Anavaṭṭhitacittassa, Saddhammaṁ avijānato, pariplavapasādassa, paññā na paripūrati.
interlinear_english: For the one with unsettled mind, who does not know the True Dhamma, whose confidence is wavering, wisdom is unfulfilled.
narrative_pali: Anavaṭṭhitacittassa, Saddhammaṁ avijānato, pariplavapasādassa, paññā na paripūrati.
narrative_english: For the one with unsettled mind, who does not know the True Dhamma, whose confidence is wavering, wisdom is surely unfulfilled.

pali_mahasangiti: Anavassutacittassa, ananvāhatacetaso; Puññapāpapahīnassa, natthi jāgarato bhayaṁ.
english_sujato: One whose mind is not festering, whose heart is undamaged, who’s given up right and wrong, alert, has nothing to fear.
interlinear_pali: Anavassutacittassa, ananvāhatacetaso, puññapāpapahīnassa natthi jāgarato bhayaṁ.
interlinear_english: For the one with mind free of lust, for the one with mind unperplexed, for the one who has abandoned making merit and demerit, for the watchful, there is no fear.

pali_mahasangiti: Kumbhūpamaṁ kāyamimaṁ viditvā, Nagarūpamaṁ cittamidaṁ ṭhapetvā; Yodhetha māraṁ paññāvudhena, Jitañca rakkhe anivesano siyā.
english_sujato: Knowing this body breaks like a pot, and fortifying the mind like a citadel, attack Māra with the sword of wisdom, guard your conquest, and never settle.
interlinear_pali: Kumbhūpamaṁ kāyam-imaṁ viditvā, nagarūpamaṁ cittam-idaṁ ṭhapetvā, yodhetha Māraṁ paññāvudhena, jitañ-ca rakkhe, anivesano siyā.
interlinear_english: Knowing this body is (frail) like a jar, establishing the mind like a fortress, fight Māra with the weapon of wisdom, guard your success, and do not be attached.
interlinear_notes: I.e. is fragile.
Solid and protected.
I do not understand Norman’s translation here of anivesano siyā as: one should take no rest, as nivesana never seems to mean taking a rest.
narrative_pali: Kumbhūpamaṁ kāyam-imaṁ viditvā, nagarūpamaṁ cittam-idaṁ ṭhapetvā, yodhetha Māraṁ paññāvudhena, jitañ-ca rakkhe, anivesano siyā.
narrative_english: Knowing this body is frail like a jar, establishing the mind like a fortress, fight Māra with the weapon of wisdom, guard your success, and do not be attached.

pali_mahasangiti: Aciraṁ vatayaṁ kāyo, pathaviṁ adhisessati; Chuddho apetaviññāṇo, niratthaṁva kaliṅgaraṁ.
english_sujato: All too soon this body will lie upon the earth, bereft of consciousness, tossed aside like a worthless log.
interlinear_pali: Aciraṁ vatayaṁ kāyo paṭhaviṁ adhisessati, chuddho apetaviññāṇo, niratthaṁ va kaliṅgaraṁ.
interlinear_english: Before long has passed by, alas, this body will lie on the ground, rejected, without consciousness, just like a useless piece of wood.
interlinear_notes: On the ground, or maybe in the ground, but burial was not common, either the body was discarded at the charnel ground, to be taken care of by animals and insects, or it was burned, and sometimes disposed of in bodies of water.
narrative_pali: Aciraṁ vatayaṁ kāyo paṭhaviṁ adhisessati, chuddho apetaviññāṇo, niratthaṁ va kaliṅgaraṁ.
narrative_english: Before long has passed by, alas, this body will lie on the ground,

pali_mahasangiti: Diso disaṁ yaṁ taṁ kayirā, verī vā pana verinaṁ; Micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ, pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.
english_sujato: A wrongly directed mind would do you more harm than a hater to the hated, or an enemy to their foe.
interlinear_pali: Diso disaṁ yan-taṁ kayirā, verī vā pana verinaṁ – micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.
interlinear_english: Whatever an aggressor might do to an aggressor, or an enemy to an enemy – a mind that is badly-directed can do far worse than that to him.
narrative_pali: Diso disaṁ yan-taṁ kayirā, verī vā pana verinaṁ – micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.
narrative_english: Whatever an aggressor might do to an aggressor, or an enemy to an enemy: a mind that’s badly-directed can do far worse than that to him.

pali_mahasangiti: Na taṁ mātā pitā kayirā, aññe vāpi ca ñātakā; Sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ, seyyaso naṁ tato kare.
english_sujato: A rightly directed mind would do you more good than your mother or father or any other relative.
interlinear_pali: Na taṁ mātā pitā kayirā, aññe vā pi ca ñātakā, sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ seyyaso naṁ tato kare.
interlinear_english: Mother and father might not do for him, or other relatives, as much good as a mind that is well-directed can do for him.
interlinear_notes: We would better read: Yaṁ taṁ here, whatever Mother and Father and other relatives might do for him.
narrative_pali: Na taṁ mātā pitā kayirā, aññe vā pi ca ñātakā, sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ seyyaso naṁ tato kare.
narrative_english: Mother and father might not do for him, or other relatives, as much good as a mind that is well-directed can do for him.

pali_mahasangiti: Ko imaṁ pathaviṁ vicessati, Yamalokañca imaṁ sadevakaṁ; Ko dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ, Kusalo pupphamiva pacessati.
english_sujato: Who bestirs this earth, and the Yama realm with its gods? Who sets out the well-taught word of truth, as an expert a flower?
interlinear_pali: Kŏ imaṁ paṭhaviṁ vicessati yamalokañ-ca imaṁ sadevakaṁ? Ko dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ kusalo puppham-ivappacessati?
interlinear_english: Who will know this earth and the lower realm, together with the gods? Who (will reflect) on the well-taught verse of Dhamma as a good man reflects on a flower?
interlinear_notes: Often translated as overcome, or conquer, as far as I can see the word is unattested with that meaning, unless it be here. Comm: attano ñāṇena vicinissati vijānissati, paṭivijjhissati, sacchikarissati; note the similarity in meaning to pacessati below.
Comm: Yamalokañ-cā ti catubbidhaṃ apāyalokaṁ; Yama’s realm means the fourfold lower realm.
The sentence is evidently meant to encompass the three realms of existence. Norman’s translation here: this world of Yama with its gods is wrong, as there are no gods in the lower realms of course.
Many times translated as gather or pluck, the commentary defines it with: vicinissati vijānissati upaparikkhissati paṭivijjhissati, sacchikarissati.
narrative_pali: Kŏ imaṁ paṭhaviṁ vicessati yamalokañ-ca imaṁ sadevakaṁ? Ko dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ kusalo puppham-ivappacessati?
narrative_english: Who will know this earth and the lower realm, together with the gods? Who will try to reflect on the well-taught verse of Dhamma as a good man reflects on a flower?

pali_mahasangiti: Sekho pathaviṁ vicessati, Yamalokañca imaṁ sadevakaṁ; Sekho dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ, Kusalo pupphamiva pacessati.
english_sujato: A trainee bestirs this earth, and the Yama realm with its gods. A trainee sets out the well-taught word of truth, as an expert a flower.
interlinear_pali: Sekho paṭhaviṁ vicessati yamalokañ-ca imaṁ sadevakaṁ. Sekho dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ kusalo puppham-ivappacessati.
interlinear_english: The trainee will know this earth and the lower realm, together with the gods. The trainee (will reflect) on the well-taught verse of Dhamma as a good man reflects on a flower.
interlinear_notes: Sekha is a technical term meaning one who is training, having attained at least to Stream-Entry, but not yet to the final stage of Awakening.

pali_mahasangiti: Pheṇūpamaṁ kāyamimaṁ viditvā, Marīcidhammaṁ abhisambudhāno; Chetvāna mārassa papupphakāni, Adassanaṁ maccurājassa gacche.
english_sujato: Knowing this body’s like foam, realizing it’s all just a mirage, and cutting off Māra’s blossoming, vanish from the King of Death.
interlinear_pali: Pheṇūpamaṁ kāyam-imaṁ viditvā, marīcidhammaṁ abhisambudhāno, chetvāna Mārassa papupphakāni, adassanaṁ Maccurājassa gacche.
interlinear_english: Knowing that this body is just like froth, understanding it has the nature of a mirage, cutting off Māra’s flower-tipped (arrows), one should go beyond the King of Death’s sight.
interlinear_notes: The emphasis is on its unsubstantiality.
The point here is the illusory nature of permanence.
Or, we might say, Māra’s temptations.
That is, to Nibbāna, which is something beyond the ken of Māra who is the king of death.
narrative_pali: Pheṇūpamaṁ kāyam-imaṁ viditvā, marīcidhammaṁ abhisambudhāno, chetvāna Mārassa papupphakāni, adassanaṁ Maccurājassa gacche.
narrative_english: Knowing that this body is just like froth, understanding it is like a mirage,

pali_mahasangiti: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ, byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ; Suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahoghova, maccu ādāya gacchati.
english_sujato: As a mighty flood sweeps off a sleeping village, death steals away a man even as he gathers flowers, his mind caught up in them.
interlinear_pali: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahogho va, maccu ādāya gacchati.
interlinear_english: * Death takes up and carries away the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers, like a great flood (carries off) a sleeping village.
interlinear_notes: Here metaphorical for the strands of sense-pleasures (kāmaguṇa). Comm: evaṃ pañcakāmaguṇasaṅkhātāni pupphāni eva pacinantaṃ ... kāmaguṇe byāsattamanasaṃ naraṃ.
narrative_pali: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahogho va, maccu ādāya gacchati.
narrative_english: Death takes up and carries away the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers, like a flood carries off a sleeping village.

pali_mahasangiti: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ, byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ; Atittaññeva kāmesu, antako kurute vasaṁ.
english_sujato: The terminator gains control of the man who has not had his fill of pleasures, even as he gathers flowers, his mind caught up in them.
interlinear_pali: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, atittaṁ yeva kāmesu Antako kurute vasaṁ.
interlinear_english: * The End-Maker takes control of the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers, even though he is unsated with sense pleasures.
interlinear_notes: Antaka, another name for Māra.
narrative_pali: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, atittaṁ yeva kāmesu Antako kurute vasaṁ.
narrative_english: The End-Maker takes control of the one whose mind is attached to

pali_mahasangiti: Yathāpi bhamaro pupphaṁ, vaṇṇagandhamaheṭhayaṁ; Paleti rasamādāya, evaṁ gāme munī care.
english_sujato: A bee takes the nectar and moves on, doing no damage to the flower’s beauty and fragrance; and that’s how a sage should walk in the village.
interlinear_pali: Yathā pi bhamaro pupphaṁ vaṇṇagandhaṁ aheṭhayaṁ paḷeti rasam-ādāya, evaṁ gāme munī care.
interlinear_english: Just as a bee, without hurting the flower, its colour or scent, gathers its nectar and escapes, so should the seer roam in the village.
interlinear_notes: An interesting choice of words, implying I think that the muni should not only be harmless, but also escape engagement in the village.
narrative_pali: Yathā pi bhamaro pupphaṁ vaṇṇagandhaṁ aheṭhayaṁ paḷeti rasam-ādāya, evaṁ gāme munī care.
narrative_english: Just as a bee, without hurting the flower, its colour or scent, gathers its nectar and escapes, so should the seer roam in village.

pali_mahasangiti: Na paresaṁ vilomāni, na paresaṁ katākataṁ; Attanova avekkheyya, katāni akatāni ca.
english_sujato: Don’t find fault with others, with what they’ve done or left undone. You should only watch yourself, what you’ve done or left undone.
interlinear_pali: Na paresaṁ vilomāni, na paresaṁ katākataṁ attano va avekkheyya, katāni akatāni ca.
interlinear_english: Not the wrongs of others, or what others have done or have not done one should consider, but what has been done and not done by oneself.
interlinear_notes: This verse has no mention of flowers, or anything similar, and also does not seem to be connected by word collocation, so its inclusion here is rather a mystery.
narrative_pali: Na paresaṁ vilomāni, na paresaṁ katākataṁ attano va avekkheyya, katāni akatāni ca.
narrative_english: Not the wrong of others, or what others have done or have not done, one should consider, but what has been done and not done by oneself.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathāpi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ, vaṇṇavantaṁ agandhakaṁ; Evaṁ subhāsitā vācā, aphalā hoti akubbato.
english_sujato: Just like a glorious flower that’s colorful but lacks fragrance; eloquent speech is fruitless for one who does not act on it.
interlinear_pali: Yathā pi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ vaṇṇavantaṁ agandhakaṁ, evaṁ subhāsitā vācā aphalā hoti akubbato.
interlinear_english: Just like a beautiful flower, which has colour, but lacks fragrance, so are well-spoken words fruitless for the one who acts not (on them).
interlinear_notes: Gandha, fragrance, is connected to virtue, so the implication is that one who lacks virtue lacks fragrance.
narrative_pali: Yathā pi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ vaṇṇavantaṁ agandhakaṁ, evaṁ subhāsitā vācā aphalā hoti akubbato.
narrative_english: Just like a beautiful flower, which has colour, but lacks fragrance, so are well-spoken words fruitless for the one who acts not on them.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathāpi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ, Vaṇṇavantaṁ sagandhakaṁ; Evaṁ subhāsitā vācā, Saphalā hoti kubbato.
english_sujato: Just like a glorious flower that’s both colorful and fragrant, eloquent speech is fruitful for one who acts on it.
interlinear_pali: Yathā pi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ vaṇṇavantaṁ sagandhakaṁ, evaṁ subhāsitā vācā saphalā hoti pakubbato.
interlinear_english: Just like a beautiful flower, which has colour, and has fragrance, so are well-spoken words fruitful for the one who does act (on them).

pali_mahasangiti: Yathāpi puppharāsimhā, kayirā mālāguṇe bahū; Evaṁ jātena maccena, kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ bahuṁ.
english_sujato: Just as one would create many garlands from a heap of flowers, when a person has come to be born, they should do many skillful things.
interlinear_pali: Yathā pi puppharāsimhā kayirā mālāguṇe bahū, evaṁ jātena maccena kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ bahuṁ.
interlinear_english: Just as from a heap of flowers one might make a lot of garlands, so should many good deeds be done by one who is born a mortal.
narrative_pali: Yathā pi puppharāsimhā kayirā mālāguṇe bahū, evaṁ jātena maccena kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ bahuṁ.
narrative_english: Just as from a heap of flowers one might make a lot of garlands,

pali_mahasangiti: Na pupphagandho paṭivātameti, Na candanaṁ tagaramallikā vā; Satañca gandho paṭivātameti, Sabbā disā sappuriso pavāyati.
english_sujato: The fragrance of flowers doesn’t spread upwind, nor sandalwood, pinwheel, or jasmine; but the fragrance of the good spreads upwind; a true person’s virtue spreads in every direction.
interlinear_pali: Na pupphagandho paṭivātam-eti, na candanaṁ tagaramallikā vā, satañ-ca gandho paṭivātam-eti, sabbā disā sappuriso pavāyati.
interlinear_english: The fragrance of flowers goes not against the wind, nor does sandalwood or pinwheel or white jasmine, but the fragrance of the good goes against the wind, the true person’s (fragrance) permeates all directions.
interlinear_notes: Meaning his virtue.

pali_mahasangiti: Candanaṁ tagaraṁ vāpi, uppalaṁ atha vassikī; Etesaṁ gandhajātānaṁ, sīlagandho anuttaro.
english_sujato: Among all the fragrances— sandalwood or pinwheel or lotus or jasmine— the fragrance of virtue is supreme.
interlinear_pali: Candanaṁ tagaraṁ vā pi, uppalaṁ atha vassikī, etesaṁ gandhajātānaṁ sīlagandho anuttaro.
interlinear_english: Sandalwood, pinwheel, then water lily and striped jasmine, amongst these kinds of fragrance virtue’s fragrance is unsurpassed.
narrative_pali: Candanaṁ tagaraṁ vā pi, uppalaṁ atha vassikī, etesaṁ gandhajātānaṁ sīlagandho anuttaro.
narrative_english: Sandalwood and pinwheel also water lily and striped jasmine, amongst these kinds of good fragrance virtue’s fragrance is unsurpassed.

pali_mahasangiti: Appamatto ayaṁ gandho, yāyaṁ tagaracandanī; Yo ca sīlavataṁ gandho, vāti devesu uttamo.
english_sujato: Faint is the fragrance of sandal or pinwheel; but the fragrance of the virtuous floats to the highest gods.
interlinear_pali: Appamatto ayaṁ gandho yāyaṁ tagaracandanī, yo ca sīlavataṁ gandho vāti devesu uttamo.
interlinear_english: Pinwheel and sandalwood fragrance are insignificant, but the fragrance of one who has virtue flutters supreme amongst the gods.
interlinear_notes: Vāti means both blow, flutter and weave, and in the commentarial story Sakka takes the form of a weaver.
narrative_pali: Appamatto ayaṁ gandho yāyaṁ tagaracandanī, yo ca sīlavataṁ gandho vāti devesu uttamo.
narrative_english: Pinwheel and sandalwood fragrance are insignificant, but the fragrance of one who has virtue flutters supreme amongst the gods.

pali_mahasangiti: Tesaṁ sampannasīlānaṁ, appamādavihārinaṁ; Sammadaññāvimuttānaṁ, māro maggaṁ na vindati.
english_sujato: For those accomplished in ethics, meditating diligently, freed through the highest knowledge, Māra cannot find their path.
interlinear_pali: Tesaṁ sampannasīlānaṁ, appamādavihārinaṁ, sammad-aññāvimuttānaṁ, Māro maggaṁ na vindati.
interlinear_english: * Māra cannot find the path of those endowed with virtue, who live heedfully, and who are freed through complete and deep knowledge.
interlinear_notes: This is a common simile in the discourses also, as Māra can only find what is still inside the rounds of birth and death.
Again this verse has no connection to flowers, there may be word-collocation on sīla in the previous verse attracting into this position.
narrative_pali: Tesaṁ sampannasīlānaṁ, appamādavihārinaṁ, sammad-aññāvimuttānaṁ, Māro maggaṁ na vindati.
narrative_english: Māra cannot find the path of those who are endowed with virtue, who live heedfully, and who are freed through complete and deep knowledge.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathā saṅkāradhānasmiṁ, ujjhitasmiṁ mahāpathe; Padumaṁ tattha jāyetha, sucigandhaṁ manoramaṁ.
english_sujato: From a heap of trash discarded on the highway, a lotus might blossom, fragrant and delightful.
interlinear_pali: Yathā saṅkāradhānasmiṁ ujjhitasmiṁ mahāpathe padumaṁ tattha jāyetha, sucigandhaṁ manoramaṁ,
interlinear_english: Just as in a forsaken and discarded heap along the highway a lotus might arise in that place, with a pure fragrance, delighting the mind,
interlinear_notes: Jāyetha is 3rd singular optative in the middle voice.

pali_mahasangiti: Evaṁ saṅkārabhūtesu, andhabhūte puthujjane; Atirocati paññāya, sammāsambuddhasāvako.
english_sujato: So too, among those thought of as trash, a disciple of the perfect Buddha outshines with their wisdom the blind ordinary folk.
interlinear_pali: evaṁ saṅkārabhūtesu, andhabhūte puthujjane atirocati paññāya Sammāsambuddhasāvako.
interlinear_english: * so amongst the forsaken, the Perfect Sambuddha’s disciple outshines the blind and ordinary folk through his wisdom.
interlinear_notes: The verse lacks the symmetry we might expect.

pali_mahasangiti: Dīghā jāgarato ratti, dīghaṁ santassa yojanaṁ; Dīgho bālāna saṁsāro, saddhammaṁ avijānataṁ.
english_sujato: Long is the night for the wakeful; long is the league for the weary; long transmigrate the fools who don’t understand the true teaching.
interlinear_pali: Dīghā jāgarato ratti, dīghaṁ santassa yojanaṁ, dīgho bālānaṁ saṁsāro Saddhammaṁ avijānataṁ.
interlinear_english: Long is the night for one awake, long is a league for one tired, long is the round of births and deaths for fools who know not True Dhamma.
interlinear_notes: The similes do not quite match the statement, nights feel long, leagues feel long, but the continuance in saṁsāra actually is long for a fool. The verse provides a good illustration of how adjectives, here dīgha, adapt to the nouns they qualify: ratti, feminine; yojana, neut, and saṁsāra, masculine.
narrative_pali: Dīghā jāgarato ratti, dīghaṁ santassa yojanaṁ, dīgho bālānaṁ saṁsāro Saddhammaṁ avijānataṁ.
narrative_english: Long is the night for one awake, long is a league for one tired, long is the round of births and deaths for fools who know not True Dhamma.

pali_mahasangiti: Carañce nādhigaccheyya, Seyyaṁ sadisamattano; Ekacariyaṁ daḷhaṁ kayirā, Natthi bāle sahāyatā.
english_sujato: If while wandering you find no partner equal or better than yourself, then firmly resolve to wander alone— there’s no fellowship with fools.
interlinear_pali: Carañ-ce nādhigaccheyya seyyaṁ sadisam-attano, ekacariyaṁ daḷhaṁ kayirā: natthi bāle sahāyatā.
interlinear_english: If while roaming one cannot find one better or the same as oneself, one should resolve to go alone: there is no friendship with fools.
interlinear_notes: Although this does express a common Buddhist sentiment, we should remember that in the early Tuvaṭakasuttaṁ of the Aṭṭhakavagga (Sn 4, XIV vs. 4), we are cautioned about thinking of others as better, the same or worse than ourselves.

pali_mahasangiti: Puttā matthi dhanaṁ matthi, iti bālo vihaññati; Attā hi attano natthi, kuto puttā kuto dhanaṁ.
english_sujato: “Sons are mine, wealth is mine”— thus the fool frets. For even your self is not your own, let alone your sons or wealth.
interlinear_pali: “Puttā matthi, dhanam-matthi,” iti bālo vihaññati, attā hi attano natthi, kuto puttā, kuto dhanaṁ?
interlinear_english: “Sons are mine, riches are mine,” so the fool suffers vexation, when even self is not his own, how then sons, how then riches?
interlinear_notes: This parses as me atthi.
If his self was really his, he would have control over it, and be able to say: let this body be thus, let it not be thus, but he cannot (see Anattalakkhaṇasuttaṁ).
narrative_pali: “Puttā matthi, dhanam-matthi,” iti bālo vihaññati, attā hi attano natthi, kuto puttā, kuto dhanaṁ?
narrative_english: “Sons are mine, and riches are mine,” so the fool suffers vexation, when even self is not his own, how then sons, and how then riches?

pali_mahasangiti: Yo bālo maññati bālyaṁ, paṇḍito vāpi tena so; Bālo ca paṇḍitamānī, sa ve “bālo”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: The fool who thinks they’re a fool is wise at least to that extent. But the true fool is said to be one who imagines that they are wise.
interlinear_pali: Yo bālo maññati bālyaṁ, paṇḍito vāpi tena so, bālo ca paṇḍitamānī, sa ve bālo ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: The fool who knows (his) foolishness, is at least wise in that (matter), the fool who is proud of his wisdom, he is said to be a fool indeed.
narrative_pali: Yo bālo maññati bālyaṁ, paṇḍito vāpi tena so, bālo ca paṇḍitamānī, sa ve bālo ti vuccati.
narrative_english: The fool who knows his foolishness, is at least wise in that matter, the fool who’s proud of his wisdom, is said to be a fool indeed.

pali_mahasangiti: Yāvajīvampi ce bālo, paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati; Na so dhammaṁ vijānāti, dabbī sūparasaṁ yathā.
english_sujato: Though a fool attends to the wise even for the rest of their life, they still don’t understand the teaching, like a spoon the taste of the soup.
interlinear_pali: Yāvajīvam-pi ce bālo paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati, na so Dhammaṁ vijānāti, dabbī sūparasaṁ yathā.
interlinear_english: Even if a fool attends on a wise man for his whole life long, he does not learn Dhamma, just as spoon learns not the taste of curry.
narrative_pali: Yāvajīvam-pi ce bālo paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati,
narrative_english: na so Dhammaṁ vijānāti, dabbī sūparasaṁ yathā. Even if a fool attends on a wise man for his whole life long, he does not learn Dhamma, just as spoon learns not the taste of curry.

pali_mahasangiti: Muhuttamapi ce viññū, paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati; Khippaṁ dhammaṁ vijānāti, jivhā sūparasaṁ yathā.
english_sujato: If a clever person attends to the wise even just for an hour or so, they swiftly understand the teaching, like a tongue the taste of the soup.
interlinear_pali: Muhuttam-api ce viññū paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati, khippaṁ Dhammaṁ vijānāti, jivhā sūparasaṁ yathā.
interlinear_english: If a perceptive man attends on a wise man even for a second, he quickly learns Dhamma, just as the tongue (learns) the taste of curry.
narrative_pali: Muhuttam-api ce viññū paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati, khippaṁ Dhammaṁ vijānāti, jivhā sūparasaṁ yathā.
narrative_english: If a perceptive man attends on a wise man for a second, he quickly learns Dhamma, just as the tongue learns the taste of curry.

pali_mahasangiti: Caranti bālā dummedhā, amitteneva attanā; Karontā pāpakaṁ kammaṁ, yaṁ hoti kaṭukapphalaṁ.
english_sujato: Fools and simpletons behave like their own worst enemies, doing wicked deeds that ripen as bitter fruit.
interlinear_pali: Caranti bālā dummedhā amitteneva attanā, karontā pāpakaṁ kammaṁ, yaṁ hoti kaṭukapphalaṁ.
interlinear_english: Stupid fools live having themselves as their own foes, committing wicked deeds, which produce bitter fruit.
narrative_pali: Caranti bālā dummedhā amitteneva attanā, karontā pāpakaṁ kammaṁ, yaṁ hoti kaṭukapphalaṁ. Stupid fools live having
narrative_english: themselves as their own foes,

pali_mahasangiti: Na taṁ kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā anutappati; Yassa assumukho rodaṁ, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
english_sujato: It’s not good to do a deed that plagues you later on, for which you weep and wail, as its effect stays with you.
interlinear_pali: Na taṁ kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā anutappati, yassa assumukho rodaṁ, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
interlinear_english: That deed is not well done, which, having done, one has regret, for which he has tears on his face, as the result follows him round.
narrative_pali: Na taṁ kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā anutappati, yassa assumukho rodaṁ, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
narrative_english: That deed is not at all well done, which, having done, one has regret, for which he has tears on his face, as the result follows him round.

pali_mahasangiti: Tañca kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā nānutappati; Yassa patīto sumano, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
english_sujato: It is good to do a deed that doesn’t plague you later on, that gladdens and cheers, as its effect stays with you.
interlinear_pali: Tañ-ca kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā nānutappati, yassa patīto sumano, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
interlinear_english: But that deed is well done, which, having done, one has no regret, for which he is pleased and happy, as the result follows him round.
interlinear_notes: These two verses again form a pair, and interestingly neither mention fools, the subject of this chapter, but may have come in through collocation on the word kamma.
narrative_pali: Tañ-ca kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā nānutappati, yassa patīto sumano, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
narrative_english: But that deed is truly well done, which, having done, one has no regret, about which one is pleased and happy, as the result follows him round.

pali_mahasangiti: Madhuṁvā maññati bālo, yāva pāpaṁ na paccati; Yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ, atha dukkhaṁ nigacchati.
english_sujato: The fool imagines that evil is sweet, so long as it has not yet ripened. But as soon as that evil ripens, they fall into suffering.
interlinear_pali: Madhuvā maññati bālo, yāva pāpaṁ na paccati, yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ, bālo dukkhaṁ nigacchati.
interlinear_english: The fool thinks it sweet, as long as the wicked deed does not ripen, but when the wicked deed ripens, the fool undergoes suffering.
narrative_pali: Madhuvā maññati bālo, yāva pāpaṁ na paccati, yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ, bālo dukkhaṁ nigacchati.
narrative_english: The fool thinks it sweet, as long as the wicked deed does not ripen, but when the wicked deed ripens, the fool undergoes suffering.

pali_mahasangiti: Māse māse kusaggena, bālo bhuñjeyya bhojanaṁ; Na so saṅkhātadhammānaṁ, kalaṁ agghati soḷasiṁ.
english_sujato: Month after month a fool may eat food from a grass-blade’s tip; but they’ll never be worth a sixteenth part of one who has appraised the teaching.
interlinear_pali: Māse māse kusaggena bālo bhuñjetha bhojanaṁ, na so saṅkhātadhammānaṁ kalaṁ agghati soḷasiṁ.
interlinear_english: From month to month the fool may eat food with the tip of kusa-grass, (but) he is not worth a sixteenth part of those who have mastered Dhamma.
interlinear_notes: Meaning he may be an ascetic engaging in very strict practices, such as eating very little.
narrative_pali: Māse māse kusaggena bālo bhuñjetha bhojanaṁ,
narrative_english: na so saṅkhātadhammānaṁ kalaṁ agghati soḷasiṁ. From month to month the fool may eat food with the tip of kusa-grass, but he’s not worth a sixteenth part of those who have mastered Dhamma.

pali_mahasangiti: Na hi pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ, Sajjukhīraṁva muccati; Ḍahantaṁ bālamanveti, Bhasmacchannova pāvako.
english_sujato: For a wicked deed that has been done does not curdle quickly like milk. Smoldering, it follows the fool, like a fire smothered over with ash.
interlinear_pali: Na hi pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ, sajju khīraṁ va muccati, ḍahantaṁ bālam-anveti, bhasmacchanno va pāvako.
interlinear_english: A wicked deed that has been done, like milk, does not turn all at once, smouldering, it follows the fool, like a fire covered with ashes.
interlinear_notes: Ḍahati means burns, smoulders, consumes, torments; it is hard to get the force of it over in natural English.
There is a mix of similes in this verse, which don’t fit well together.
narrative_pali: Na hi pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ, sajju khīraṁ va muccati, ḍahantaṁ bālam-anveti, bhasmacchanno va pāvako.
narrative_english: A wicked deed that has been done, like milk, does not turn all at once, smouldering, it follows the fool, like a fire covered with ashes.

pali_mahasangiti: Yāvadeva anatthāya, ñattaṁ bālassa jāyati; Hanti bālassa sukkaṁsaṁ, muddhamassa vipātayaṁ.
english_sujato: Whatever fame a fool may get, it only gives rise to harm. Whatever good features they have it ruins, and blows their head into bits.
interlinear_pali: Yāvad-eva anatthāya ñattaṁ bālassa jāyati, hanti bālassa sukkaṁsaṁ, muddham-assa vipātayaṁ.
interlinear_english: As far as learning arises for a fool, it is only to his disadvantage, it destroys the fool’s good fortune, and it will destroy his head.
interlinear_notes: The commentary explains that his head here means his wisdom, though it would have been easy to write paññam-assa vipātayaṁ if that was what was intended.
narrative_pali: Yāvad-eva anatthāya ñattaṁ bālassa jāyati, hanti bālassa sukkaṁsaṁ, muddham-assa vipātayaṁ.
narrative_english: Learning arises for a fool only to his disadvantage, it destroys the fool’s good fortune, it will destroy his very head.

pali_mahasangiti: Asantaṁ bhāvanamiccheyya, Purekkhārañca bhikkhusu; Āvāsesu ca issariyaṁ, Pūjaṁ parakulesu ca.
english_sujato: They’d seek the esteem that they lack, and status among the mendicants; authority over monasteries, and honor among other families.
interlinear_pali: Asataṁ bhāvanam-iccheyya, purekkhārañ-ca bhikkhusu, āvāsesu ca issariyaṁ, pūjā parakulesu ca:
interlinear_english: He may wish for the respect that is lacking, and status amongst the monastics, for control in the living quarters, and worship amongst good families:

pali_mahasangiti: Mameva kata maññantu, gihī pabbajitā ubho; Mamevātivasā assu, kiccākiccesu kismici; Iti bālassa saṅkappo, icchā māno ca vaḍḍhati.
english_sujato: “Let both layfolk and renunciants think the work was done by me alone. In anything at all that’s to be done, let them fall under my sway alone.” So thinks the fool, their greed and pride only growing.
interlinear_pali: “Mameva kata’ maññantu gihī pabbajitā ubho, mameva ativasā assu, kiccākiccesu kismici”, iti bālassa saṅkappo, icchā māno ca vaḍḍhati.
interlinear_english: “Householders and renunciants should both think this was done by me, let them (all) be under my sway, in all to be done and not done”, so does the fool think, (meanwhile) his desires and conceit increase.
narrative_pali: “Mameva kata’ maññantu gihī pabbajitā ubho, mameva ativasā assu, kiccākiccesu kismici”, iti bālassa saṅkappo, icchā māno ca vaḍḍhati.
narrative_english: “Householders and renunciants should both think this was done by me, let them all be under my sway, in all to be done and not done,” so does the fool think, meanwhile his desires and conceit increase.

pali_mahasangiti: Aññā hi lābhūpanisā, aññā nibbānagāminī; Evametaṁ abhiññāya, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako; Sakkāraṁ nābhinandeyya, vivekamanubrūhaye.
english_sujato: For the means to profit and the path to quenching are two quite different things. A mendicant disciple of the Buddha, understanding what this really means, would never delight in honors, but rather would foster seclusion.
interlinear_pali: Aññā hi lābhūpanisā, aññā Nibbānagāminī, evam-etaṁ abhiññāya bhikkhu Buddhassa sāvako sakkāraṁ nābhinandeyya, vivekam-anubrūhaye.
interlinear_english: For the means to gains is one thing, the (path) going to Nibbāna another, thus knowing this the monastic disciple of the Buddha should not delight in honours, (but) practise in solitude.
interlinear_notes: Again the verse lacks any mention of fools, and might have been better placed in the Bhikkhuvagga.
narrative_pali: Aññā hi lābhūpanisā, aññā Nibbānagāminī, evam-etaṁ abhiññāya bhikkhu Buddhassa sāvako sakkāraṁ nābhinandeyya, vivekam-anubrūhaye.
narrative_english: For the means to gains is one thing, the way to Nibbāna another, thus knowing this the disciple

pali_mahasangiti: Nidhīnaṁva pavattāraṁ, yaṁ passe vajjadassinaṁ; Niggayhavādiṁ medhāviṁ, tādisaṁ paṇḍitaṁ bhaje; Tādisaṁ bhajamānassa, seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.
english_sujato: Regard one who sees your faults as a guide to a hidden treasure. Stay close to one so intelligent and astute who curbs you when you need it. Sticking close to such an impartial person, things get better, not worse.
interlinear_pali: Nidhīnaṁ va pavattāraṁ yaṁ passe vajjadassinaṁ, niggayhavādiṁ medhāviṁ tādisaṁ paṇḍitaṁ bhaje; tādisaṁ bhajamānassa seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.
interlinear_english: One should regard someone who shows your faults just like one who points out hidden treasure, one should keep company with such a sagacious, learned person who reproves you; keeping company with such is (surely) better for you, not worse.
narrative_pali: Nidhīnaṁ va pavattāraṁ yaṁ passe vajjadassinaṁ, niggayhavādiṁ medhāviṁ tādisaṁ paṇḍitaṁ bhaje; tādisaṁ bhajamānassa seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.
narrative_english: One should treat one who shows your faults just like one who points out treasure, one should keep company with such a sagacious, learned person; keeping company with such is surely better for you, not worse.

pali_mahasangiti: Ovadeyyānusāseyya, asabbhā ca nivāraye; Satañhi so piyo hoti, asataṁ hoti appiyo.
english_sujato: Advise and instruct; curb wickedness: for you shall be loved by the good, and disliked by the bad.
interlinear_pali: Ovadeyyānusāseyya, asabbhā ca nivāraye, sataṁ hi so piyo hoti, asataṁ hoti appiyo.
interlinear_english: One should advise and instruct, and forbid whatever is vile, for he is dear to the good, (but) he is not dear to the bad.
interlinear_notes: Although the theme of the good person is present, neither this verse nor the next mention the paṇḍita.
narrative_pali: Ovadeyyānusāseyya, asabbhā ca nivāraye,
narrative_english: sataṁ hi so piyo hoti, asataṁ hoti appiyo. One should both advise and instruct, and forbid whatever is vile, for it is dear to the good, but it is not dear to the bad.

pali_mahasangiti: Na bhaje pāpake mitte, na bhaje purisādhame; Bhajetha mitte kalyāṇe, bhajetha purisuttame.
english_sujato: Don’t mix with bad friends, nor with the worst of men. Mix with spiritual friends, and with the best of men.
interlinear_pali: Na bhaje pāpake mitte, na bhaje purisādhame, bhajetha mitte kalyāṇe, bhajetha purisuttame.
interlinear_english: One should not keep company with wicked friends, one should not keep company with the ignoble, you should keep company with spiritual friends, you should keep company with superior people.
interlinear_notes: This is a bit irregular: the first two lines are in the 3rd person singular, and the second two in the 2nd person (polite) plural. It is possible we should take the last two lines as being in middle voice, but it would have been easy to write bhajeyya if the change of person wasn’t intended. Patna reads bhajetha throughout, and Udānavarga reads bhaje, probably trying to regularise the reading.

pali_mahasangiti: Dhammapīti sukhaṁ seti, vippasannena cetasā; Ariyappavedite dhamme, sadā ramati paṇḍito.
english_sujato: Through joy in the teaching you sleep at ease, with clear and confident heart. An astute person always delights in the teaching proclaimed by the Noble One.
interlinear_pali: Dhammapīti sukhaṁ seti, vippasannena cetasā, Ariyappavedite Dhamme sadā ramati paṇḍito.
interlinear_english: The one who drinks Dhamma lives well, with a clear mind, the wise one will always delight in the Dhamma that is made known by the Noble.
interlinear_notes: Comm: Dhammapayako Dhammaṁ pivanto ti attho... ariyasaccāni paṭivijjhanto; the one who makes (others) drink Dhamma, who drinks Dhamma... who experiences the Noble truths. It seems both causative and active meanings may be intended.

pali_mahasangiti: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā, Usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ; Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, Attānaṁ damayanti paṇḍitā.
english_sujato: While irrigators guide water, fletchers bend arrows straight, and carpenters bend timber straight, the astute tame themselves.
interlinear_pali: Udakaṁ hi nayanti nettikā, usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ, dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, attānaṁ damayanti paṇḍitā.
interlinear_english: Course-makers lead water, fletchers straighten arrows, carpenters straighten wood, the wise master themselves.
interlinear_notes: For a variant of this verse, see 145 below.

pali_mahasangiti: Selo yathā ekaghano, vātena na samīrati; Evaṁ nindāpasaṁsāsu, na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.
english_sujato: As the wind cannot stir a solid mass of rock, so too blame and praise do not affect the wise.
interlinear_pali: Selo yathā ekaghano vātena na samīrati, evaṁ nindāpasaṁsāsu na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.
interlinear_english: Just as solid rock is not shaken by the wind, so the wise are not moved by blame or praise.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathāpi rahado gambhīro, vippasanno anāvilo; Evaṁ dhammāni sutvāna, vippasīdanti paṇḍitā.
english_sujato: Like a deep lake, clear and unclouded, so clear are the astute when they hear the teachings.
interlinear_pali: Yathā pi rahado gambhīro vippasanno anāvilo, evaṁ Dhammāni sutvāna vippasīdanti paṇḍitā.
interlinear_english: Like a lake that is deep, clear and unruffled, just so the wise are confident after listening to Dhamma.
interlinear_notes: There is a play on meaning of the forms derived from vippasīdati, it means both clear and confident.

pali_mahasangiti: Sabbattha ve sappurisā cajanti, Na kāmakāmā lapayanti santo; Sukhena phuṭṭhā atha vā dukhena, Na uccāvacaṁ paṇḍitā dassayanti.
english_sujato: True persons give up everything, they don’t cajole for the things they desire. Though touched by sadness or happiness, the astute appear neither depressed nor elated.
interlinear_pali: Sabbattha ve sappurisā cajanti, na kāmakāmā lapayanti santo; sukhena phuṭṭhā atha vā dukhena, noccāvacaṁ paṇḍitā dassayanti.
interlinear_english: True people surely everywhere renounce, the good do not talk of desiring sense-pleasures; when touched by pleasure or by suffering, the wise show neither elation or depression.

pali_mahasangiti: Na attahetu na parassa hetu, Na puttamicche na dhanaṁ na raṭṭhaṁ; Na iccheyya adhammena samiddhimattano, Sa sīlavā paññavā dhammiko siyā.
english_sujato: Never wish for success by unjust means, for your own sake or that of another, desiring children, wealth, or nation; rather, be virtuous, wise, and just.
interlinear_pali: Na attahetu na parassa hetu, na puttam-icche na dhanaṁ na raṭṭhaṁ – na iccheyya adhammena samiddhim-attano; sa sīlavā paññavā dhammiko siyā.
interlinear_english: Not for one’s own sake and not for another’s sake, not desiring a child, riches, or a kingdom – he should not desire his success through corruption; he should be both virtuous and wise and righteous.
interlinear_notes: Through wrong, unrighteous or corrupt ways.

pali_mahasangiti: Appakā te manussesu, ye janā pāragāmino; Athāyaṁ itarā pajā, tīramevānudhāvati.
english_sujato: Few are those among humans who cross to the far shore. The rest just run around on the near shore.
interlinear_pali: Appakā te manussesu ye janā pāragāmino, athāyaṁ itarā pajā tīram-evānudhāvati,
interlinear_english: Amongst humans few people go beyond, the rest of the people run down the bank,

pali_mahasangiti: Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte, dhamme dhammānuvattino; Te janā pāramessanti, maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ.
english_sujato: When the teaching is well explained, the people who practice accordingly will cross over Death’s dominion so hard to pass.
interlinear_pali: ye ca kho sammad-akkhāte Dhamme dhammānuvattino, te janā pāram-essanti, maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ.
interlinear_english: but those who live righteously, conforming with this well-taught Dhamma, those folk will go beyond the realm of death, which is very hard to cross.
interlinear_notes: There is no mention of paṇḍita in this verse, the closest being those who live righteously.

pali_mahasangiti: Kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ vippahāya, Sukkaṁ bhāvetha paṇḍito; Okā anokamāgamma, Viveke yattha dūramaṁ.
english_sujato: Rid of dark qualities, an astute person would develop the bright. Having left home for homelessness in seclusion, where joy is hard,
interlinear_pali: Kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ vippahāya, sukkaṁ bhāvetha paṇḍito, okā anokaṁ āgamma; viveke yattha dūramaṁ,
interlinear_english: Having abandoned the dark state, the wise one should develop the bright, having gone forth to homelessness from home; in solitude, where it is hard to delight.
narrative_pali: Kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ vippahāya, sukkaṁ bhāvetha paṇḍito, okā anokaṁ āgamma; viveke yattha dūramaṁ,
narrative_english: Having abandoned the dark state, the wise should develop the bright, having gone forth to homelessness from home, living in solitude, where it is hard to find delight.

pali_mahasangiti: Tatrābhiratimiccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano; Pariyodapeyya attānaṁ, cittaklesehi paṇḍito.
english_sujato: they’d long for satisfaction there. Forsaking sensual pleasures, owning nothing, an astute person would cleanse themselves of mental corruptions.
interlinear_pali: Tatrābhiratim-iccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano, pariyodapeyya attānaṁ cittaklesehi paṇḍito.
interlinear_english: One should desire to delight in that place, having given up sense pleasures, and having no possessions, the wise one should purify the self of defilements of mind.

pali_mahasangiti: Yesaṁ sambodhiyaṅgesu, sammā cittaṁ subhāvitaṁ; Ādānapaṭinissagge, anupādāya ye ratā; Khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā.
english_sujato: And those whose minds are rightly developed in the awakening factors; who, letting go of attachments, delight in not grasping: with defilements ended, brilliant, they are quenched in this world.
interlinear_pali: Yesaṁ sambodhi-aṅgesu sammā cittaṁ subhāvitaṁ, ādānapaṭinissagge anupādāya ye ratā, khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā.
interlinear_english: For those who have well developed with right mind the factors of complete awakening, having given up grasping, those who delight in being unattached, pollutant-free, shining forth, are emancipated in the world.

pali_mahasangiti: Gataddhino visokassa, vippamuttassa sabbadhi; Sabbaganthappahīnassa, pariḷāho na vijjati.
english_sujato: At journey’s end, rid of sorrow; everywhere free, all ties given up, no fever is found in them.
interlinear_pali: Gataddhino visokassa vippamuttassa sabbadhi, sabbaganthappahīnassa, pariḷāho na vijjati.
interlinear_english: For the one who has reached his goal, who grieves not, being released on all sides, who has abandoned all the knots, no consuming fever is found.
interlinear_notes: Usually enumerated as four: abhijjhā-, byāpāda-, sīlabbataparāmāsa-, idaṁsaccābhinivesagantha;the knots of avarice, ill-will, grasping at virtue and practices, and inclination to (insisting that) ‘this is the truth’.
Passion is the consuming fever which is implied here.

pali_mahasangiti: Uyyuñjanti satīmanto, na nikete ramanti te; Haṁsāva pallalaṁ hitvā, okamokaṁ jahanti te.
english_sujato: The mindful apply themselves; they delight in no abode. Like a swan gone from the marsh, they leave home after home behind.
interlinear_pali: Uyyuñjanti satīmanto na nikete ramanti te, haṁsā va pallalaṁ hitvā, okam-okaṁ jahanti te.
interlinear_english: The mindful ones who are striving do not delight in a dwelling, like geese who abandon a lake, they abandon fondness for homes.
interlinear_notes: It is hard to get across all the double meanings in this verse, but niketa means: home, company and attachment; and oka means water, home and attachment.

pali_mahasangiti: Yesaṁ sannicayo natthi, ye pariññātabhojanā; Suññato animitto ca, vimokkho yesaṁ gocaro; Ākāseva sakuntānaṁ, gati tesaṁ durannayā.
english_sujato: Those with nothing stored up, who have understood their food, whose domain is the liberation of the signless and the empty: their path is hard to trace, like birds in the sky.
interlinear_pali: Yesaṁ sannicayo natthi, ye pariññātabhojanā, suññato animitto ca vimokkho yesa’ gocaro, ākāse va sakuntānaṁ, gati tesaṁ durannayā.
interlinear_english: For those who have no stores, those who comprehend food aright, for those whose resort is the liberation that is empty or signless, like the birds in the sky, their track is hard to find.
interlinear_notes: The commentary defines this as having stores of kamma, which would lead to rebirth; the Arahat of course has no such stores.
Seeing its disgusting nature.
This is a reference to the three liberations (vimokkha), which are defined as being signless (animitta), desireless (apanihita) and empty (suññatā). The second is implied, rather than stated here.
Gati may mean their course, track or destiny; it means that they cannot be known either in this world, or when gone beyond.
narrative_pali: Yesaṁ sannicayo natthi, ye pariññātabhojanā, suññato animitto ca vimokkho yesa’ gocaro, ākāse va sakuntānaṁ, gati tesaṁ durannayā.
narrative_english: For those who have no stores, who know their food aright, for those whose resort is the liberation that is empty or signless, like the birds in the sky, their track is hard to find.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassāsavā parikkhīṇā, āhāre ca anissito; Suññato animitto ca, vimokkho yassa gocaro; Ākāseva sakuntānaṁ, padaṁ tassa durannayaṁ.
english_sujato: One whose defilements have ended; who’s not attached to food; whose domain is the liberation of the signless and the empty: their track is hard to trace, like birds in the sky.
interlinear_pali: Yassāsavā parikkhīṇā, āhāre ca anissito, suññato animitto ca vimokkho yassa gocaro, ākāse va sakuntānaṁ, padaṁ tassa durannayaṁ.
interlinear_english: For him whose pollutants are destroyed, who is not dependent on the foods, for him whose resort is the liberation that is empty or signless, like the birds in the sky, his footprint is hard to find.
interlinear_notes: The commentary says it means the foods of craving and views.
Pada may mean his footprint or his state; again it means that they cannot be known either in this world, or when gone beyond
narrative_pali: Yassāsavā parikkhīṇā, āhāre ca anissito, suññato animitto ca vimokkho yassa gocaro, ākāse va sakuntānaṁ, padaṁ tassa durannayaṁ.
narrative_english: For him whose pollutants are destroyed, who is not dependent on the foods, for him whose resort is the liberation that is empty or signless, like the birds in the sky, his footprint’s hard to find.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassindriyāni samathaṅgatāni, Assā yathā sārathinā sudantā; Pahīnamānassa anāsavassa, Devāpi tassa pihayanti tādino.
english_sujato: Whose faculties have become serene, like horses tamed by a charioteer, who has abandoned conceit and defilements; the unaffected one is envied by even the gods.
interlinear_pali: Yassindriyāni samathaṁ gatāni, assā yathā sārathinā sudantā, pahīnamānassa anāsavassa – devā pi tassa pihayanti tādino.
interlinear_english: For the one whose senses are stilled, like horses well-trained by their charioteer, who has abandoned conceit, who is without pollutants – even the gods envy such a one.
narrative_pali: Yassindriyāni samathaṁ gatāni, assā yathā sārathinā sudantā, pahīnamānassa anāsavassa – devā pi tassa pihayanti tādino.
narrative_english: For the one whose senses are stilled, like horses well-trained by their groom, who has abandoned all conceit, who is without all pollutants: even the gods envy such a one.

pali_mahasangiti: Pathavisamo no virujjhati, Indakhilupamo tādi subbato; Rahadova apetakaddamo, Saṁsārā na bhavanti tādino.
