english_sujato: Undisturbed like the earth, true to their vows, steady as Indra’s pillar, like a lake clear of mud; such a one does not transmigrate.
interlinear_pali: Paṭhavisamo no virujjhati, indakhīlūpamŏ tādi subbato, rahado va apetakaddamo – saṁsārā na bhavanti tādino.
interlinear_english: One untroubled just like the earth, steadfast just like a city-post, like a lake mud-free – such a one continues not in births and deaths.

pali_mahasangiti: Santaṁ tassa manaṁ hoti, santā vācā ca kamma ca; Sammadaññāvimuttassa, upasantassa tādino.
english_sujato: Their mind is peaceful, peaceful are their speech and deeds. Such a one is at peace, rightly freed through enlightenment.
interlinear_pali: Santaṁ tassa manaṁ hoti, santā vācā ca kamma’ ca, sammad-aññāvimuttassa, upasantassa tādino.
interlinear_english: His mind is calm, his speech and his actions are also calm, liberated by right knowledge, such a one is (truly) peaceful.
narrative_pali: Santaṁ tassa manaṁ hoti, santā vācā ca kamma’ ca, sammad-aññāvimuttassa, upasantassa tādino.
narrative_english: His mind is calm, his speech is calm, and his actions are also calm, liberated by right knowledge, such a one is truly peaceful.

pali_mahasangiti: Assaddho akataññū ca, sandhicchedo ca yo naro; Hatāvakāso vantāso, sa ve uttamaporiso.
english_sujato: Lacking faith, a house-breaker, one who acknowledges nothing, purged of hope, they’ve wasted their chance: that is indeed the supreme person!
interlinear_pali: Assaddho akataññū ca sandhicchedo ca yo naro, hatāvakāso vantāso, sa ve uttamaporiso.
interlinear_english: The person who is beyond (mere) faith, who knows that which is unmade, who has cut off (rebirth-)linking, who has destroyed the occasion, who has thrown out hope and desire, is surely the person supreme.
interlinear_notes: Because he has seen the truth for himself.
Nibbāna.
Sandhi here is short for paṭisandhi, rebirth-linking.
Destroyed the occasion for good and bad deeds.
Āsa, hope, desire, is here a synonym for craving.

pali_mahasangiti: Gāme vā yadi vāraññe, Ninne vā yadi vā thale; Yattha arahanto viharanti, Taṁ bhūmirāmaṇeyyakaṁ.
english_sujato: Whether in village or wilderness, in a valley or the uplands, wherever the perfected ones live is a delightful place.
interlinear_pali: Gāme vā yadi vāraññe, ninne vā yadi vā thale, yattharahanto viharanti, taṁ bhūmiṁ rāmaṇeyyakaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whether in the village or wilds, whether on low or on high ground, wherever the Arahats live, that ground is (surely) delightful.
interlinear_notes: This is the only verse in this chapter which actually speaks of Arahats.
narrative_pali: Gāme vā yadi vāraññe, ninne vā yadi vā thale, yattharahanto viharanti, taṁ bhūmiṁ rāmaṇeyyakaṁ.
narrative_english: Whether in the village or wilds, whether on low or on high ground, wherever the Arahats live, that ground is surely delightful.

pali_mahasangiti: Ramaṇīyāni araññāni, yattha na ramatī jano; Vītarāgā ramissanti, na te kāmagavesino.
english_sujato: Delightful are the wildernesses where no people delight. Those free of greed will delight there, not those who seek sensual pleasures.
interlinear_pali: Ramaṇīyāni araññāni yattha na ramatī jano, vītarāgā ramissanti, na te kāmagavesino.
interlinear_english: The delightful wildernesses where the people do not delight, those without passion will take delight, (but) not those who seek sense pleasures.
narrative_pali: Ramaṇīyāni araññāni yattha na ramatī jano, vītarāgā ramissanti, na te kāmagavesino.
narrative_english: The delightful wildernesses where the people do not delight, those without passion delight in, but not those who seek sense pleasures.

pali_mahasangiti: Sahassamapi ce vācā, anatthapadasaṁhitā; Ekaṁ atthapadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
english_sujato: Better than a thousand meaningless sayings is a single meaningful saying, hearing which brings you peace.
interlinear_pali: Sahassam-api ce vācā anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ atthapadaṁ seyyo yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
interlinear_english: Though there are a thousand sayings consisting of useless words, better is one useful word hearing which one is brought to peace.
narrative_pali: Sahassam-api ce vācā anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ atthapadaṁ seyyo yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
narrative_english: Though there are a thousand sayings consisting of quite useless words, better is just one useful word hearing which one is brought to peace.

pali_mahasangiti: Sahassamapi ce gāthā, anatthapadasaṁhitā; Ekaṁ gāthāpadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
english_sujato: Better than a thousand meaningless verses is a single meaningful verse, hearing which brings you peace.
interlinear_pali: Sahassam-api ce gāthā anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ gāthāpadaṁ seyyo yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
interlinear_english: Though there are a thousand verses consisting of useless words, better is one word of a verse hearing which one is brought to peace.
narrative_pali: Sahassam-api ce gāthā anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ gāthāpadaṁ seyyo yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
narrative_english: Though there are a thousand verses consisting of quite useless words, better is one word of a verse hearing which one is brought to peace.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca gāthā sataṁ bhāse, anatthapadasaṁhitā; Ekaṁ dhammapadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
english_sujato: Better than reciting a hundred meaningless verses is a single saying of Dhamma, hearing which brings you peace.
interlinear_pali: Yo ce gāthāsataṁ bhāse anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ Dhammapadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
interlinear_english: One may speak a hundred verses consisting of useless words, better is one verse of Dhamma, hearing which one is brought to peace.
narrative_pali: Yo ce gāthāsataṁ bhāse anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ Dhammapadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
narrative_english: One may speak a hundred verses consisting of quite useless words, better is one verse of Dhamma, hearing which one is brought to peace.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo sahassaṁ sahassena, saṅgāme mānuse jine; Ekañca jeyyamattānaṁ, sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.
english_sujato: The supreme conqueror is not he who conquers a million men in battle, but he who conquers a single man: himself.
interlinear_pali: Yo sahassaṁ sahassena saṅgāme mānuse jine, ekañ-ca jeyya attānaṁ, sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.
interlinear_english: One may conquer a thousand men a thousand times in a battle, but having conquered one’s own self, one would surely be supreme in battle.

pali_mahasangiti: Attā have jitaṁ seyyo, yā cāyaṁ itarā pajā; Attadantassa posassa, niccaṁ saññatacārino.
english_sujato: It is surely better to conquer oneself than all those other folk. When a person has tamed themselves, always living restrained,
interlinear_pali: Attā have jitaṁ seyyo yā cāyaṁ itarā pajā, attadantassa posassa, niccaṁ saññatacārino,
interlinear_english: Conquest over self is better than that over other people, for the person who conquers himself, who lives constantly well-restrained,

pali_mahasangiti: Neva devo na gandhabbo, na māro saha brahmunā; Jitaṁ apajitaṁ kayirā, tathārūpassa jantuno.
english_sujato: no god nor centaur, nor Māra nor divinity, can undo the victory of such a personage.
interlinear_pali: neva devo na gandhabbo, na Māro saha Brahmunā, jitaṁ apajitaṁ kayirā tathārūpassa jantuno.
interlinear_english: neither gods, nor gandhabbas, nor Māra together with Brahmās, can turn conquest into defeat for a person who is like this.

pali_mahasangiti: Māse māse sahassena, yo yajetha sataṁ samaṁ; Ekañca bhāvitattānaṁ, muhuttamapi pūjaye; Sāyeva pūjanā seyyo, yañce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
english_sujato: Rather than a thousandfold sacrifice, every month for a full century, it’s better to honor for a single hour one who has developed themselves. That offering is better than the hundred year sacrifice.
interlinear_pali: Māse māse sahassena yo yajetha sataṁ samaṁ; ekañ-ca bhāvitattānaṁ muhuttam-api pūjaye – sā yeva pūjanā seyyo yañ-ce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
interlinear_english: One might give alms impartially with a thousand (coins of money) month by month for a hundred (years); and one might worship someone with developed self for a second – that worship is surely better than the hundred-year sacrifice.
interlinear_notes: Other translations seem to take samaṁ as meaning year, perhaps following the paraphrase in the commentary; however, it doesn’t seem to be attested in that meaning, and the singular number would be wrong, both of which are against it. Rather is seems we should take it as an adjective with the meaning, equally, indifferently, impartially.
The commentary says it means anyone who is a Noble Person or one who has attained any of the four stages of Awakening.
narrative_pali: Māse māse sahassena yo yajetha sataṁ samaṁ; ekañ-ca bhāvitattānaṁ muhuttam-api pūjaye – sā yeva pūjanā seyyo yañ-ce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
narrative_english: One might give alms impartially with a thousand coins of money month by month for a hundred years; and one might worship someone with developed self for a second – that worship is surely better than the hundred-year sacrifice.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca vassasataṁ jantu, aggiṁ paricare vane; Ekañca bhāvitattānaṁ, muhuttamapi pūjaye; Sāyeva pūjanā seyyo, yañce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
english_sujato: Rather than serve the sacred flame in the forest for a hundred years, it’s better to honor for a single hour a personage who has developed themselves. That offering is better than the hundred year sacrifice.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jantu aggiṁ paricare vane; ekañ-ca bhāvitattānaṁ muhuttam-api pūjaye – sā yeva pūjanā seyyo yañ-ce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
interlinear_english: One person might care for the fire in the woods for a hundred years; and one might worship someone with developed self for a second – that worship is surely better than the hundred-year sacrifice.

pali_mahasangiti: Yaṁ kiñci yiṭṭhaṁ va hutaṁ va loke, Saṁvaccharaṁ yajetha puññapekkho; Sabbampi taṁ na catubhāgameti, Abhivādanā ujjugatesu seyyo.
english_sujato: Whatever sacrifice or offering in the world a seeker of merit may make for a year, none of it is worth a quarter of bowing to the sincere.
interlinear_pali: Yaṁ kiñci yiṭṭhaṁ ca hutaṁ ca loke saṁvaccharaṁ yajetha puññapekkho, sabbam-pi taṁ na catubhāgam-eti – abhivādanā ujjugatesu seyyo.
interlinear_english: Whatever the alms or the sacrifice in the world the one seeking merit may give for a year, all that comes not to a quarter (of the merit) – better is the worship of the upright.
narrative_pali: Yaṁ kiñci yiṭṭhaṁ ca hutaṁ ca loke saṁvaccharaṁ yajetha puññapekkho,

pali_mahasangiti: Abhivādanasīlissa, niccaṁ vuḍḍhāpacāyino; Cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti, āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṁ balaṁ.
english_sujato: For one in the habit of bowing, always honoring the elders, four blessings grow: lifespan, beauty, happiness, and strength.
interlinear_pali: Abhivādanasīlissa niccaṁ vaddhāpacāyino, cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti: āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṁ balaṁ.
interlinear_english: For the one who is constantly worshipping honourable elders, four things increase: the length of life, beauty, happiness, and strength.
narrative_pali: Abhivādanasīlissa niccaṁ vaddhāpacāyino, cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti: āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṁ balaṁ.
narrative_english: For the one who is constantly

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, dussīlo asamāhito; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, sīlavantassa jhāyino.
english_sujato: Better to live a single day ethical and absorbed in meditation than to live a hundred years unethical and lacking immersion.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, dussīlo asamāhito, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, sīlavantassa jhāyino.
interlinear_english: One might live for a hundred years, unvirtuous and uncomposed, (but) a life of one day is better, for one with virtue and meditation.
narrative_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, dussīlo asamāhito, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, sīlavantassa jhāyino.
narrative_english: One might live for a hundred years, unvirtuous and uncomposed, but one day is better, for one with virtue and meditation.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, duppañño asamāhito; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, paññavantassa jhāyino.
english_sujato: Better to live a single day wise and absorbed in meditation than to live a hundred years witless and lacking immersion.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, duppañño asamāhito, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, paññavantassa jhāyino.
interlinear_english: One might live for a hundred years, lacking in wisdom, uncomposed, (but) a life of one day is better, for one endowed with wisdom and meditation.
narrative_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, duppañño asamāhito, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, paññavantassa jhāyino.
narrative_english: One might live for a hundred years, lacking in wisdom, uncomposed, but one day is better, for one with wisdom and absorption.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, kusīto hīnavīriyo; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, vīriyamārabhato daḷhaṁ.
english_sujato: Better to live a single day energetic and strong, than to live a hundred years lazy and lacking energy.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, kusīto hīnavīriyo, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, viriyam-ārabhato daḷhaṁ.
interlinear_english: One might live for a hundred years, indolent, with less energy, (but) a life of one day is better, for one with energy set up and firm.
narrative_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, kusīto hīnavīriyo, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, viriyam-ārabhato daḷhaṁ.
narrative_english: One might live for a hundred years, indolent, with less energy, but one day is better, for one with energy set up and firm.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, apassaṁ udayabbayaṁ; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, passato udayabbayaṁ.
english_sujato: Better to live a single day seeing rise and fall than to live a hundred years blind to rise and fall.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ udayabbayaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato udayabbayaṁ.
interlinear_english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing rise and fall, (but) a life of one day is better (for the one) seeing rise and fall.
narrative_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ udayabbayaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato udayabbayaṁ.
narrative_english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing rise and fall, but a life of one day’s better for the one seeing rise and fall.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, apassaṁ amataṁ padaṁ; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, passato amataṁ padaṁ.
english_sujato: Better to live a single day seeing the state free of death than to live a hundred years blind to the state free of death.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ amataṁ padaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato amataṁ padaṁ.
interlinear_english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing the deathless state, (but) a life of one day is better (for one) seeing the deathless state.
narrative_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ amataṁ padaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato amataṁ padaṁ.
narrative_english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing the deathless state, but a life of one day’s better for one seeing the deathless state.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, apassaṁ dhammamuttamaṁ; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, passato dhammamuttamaṁ.
english_sujato: Better to live a single day seeing the supreme teaching than to live a hundred years blind to the supreme teaching.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ dhammam-uttamaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato dhammam-uttamaṁ.
interlinear_english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing the supreme state, (but) a life of one day is better (for one) seeing the supreme state.
narrative_pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ dhammam-uttamaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato dhammam-uttamaṁ.
narrative_english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing the supreme state, but a life of one day is better for one seeing the supreme state.

pali_mahasangiti: Abhittharetha kalyāṇe, pāpā cittaṁ nivāraye; Dandhañhi karoto puññaṁ, pāpasmiṁ ramatī mano.
english_sujato: Rush to do good, shield your mind from evil; for when you’re slow to do good, your thoughts delight in wickedness.
interlinear_pali: Abhittharetha kalyāṇe, pāpā cittaṁ nivāraye, dandhaṁ hi karato puññaṁ pāpasmiṁ ramatī mano.
interlinear_english: Hasten to do wholesome deeds, ward off the mind from wickedness, for the mind of the one slow in merit delights in wickedness.
narrative_pali: Abhittharetha kalyāṇe, pāpā cittaṁ nivāraye, dandhaṁ hi karato puññaṁ pāpasmiṁ ramatī mano.
narrative_english: Hasten to do wholesome deeds, ward off the mind from wickedness, for the mind of the one slow in merit delights in wickedness.

pali_mahasangiti: Pāpañce puriso kayirā, Na naṁ kayirā punappunaṁ; Na tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, Dukkho pāpassa uccayo.
english_sujato: If you do something bad, don’t do it again and again, don’t set your heart on it, for piling up evil is suffering.
interlinear_pali: Pāpañ-ce puriso kayirā, na taṁ kayirā punappunaṁ, na tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, dukkho pāpassa uccayo.
interlinear_english: Should a person do that which is wicked, he should not do it again and again, let him not place his intention in it, (for) there is an accumulation of suffering for the wicked one.
narrative_pali: Pāpañ-ce puriso kayirā, na taṁ kayirā punappunaṁ, na tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, dukkho pāpassa uccayo.
narrative_english: If a person should do that which is wrong, he should not do it again and again, let him not place his intention in it, for suffering grows for the wicked one.

pali_mahasangiti: Puññañce puriso kayirā, kayirā naṁ punappunaṁ; Tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, sukho puññassa uccayo.
english_sujato: If you do something good, do it again and again, set your heart on it, for piling up goodness is joyful.
interlinear_pali: Puññañ-ce puriso kayirā, kayirāthetaṁ punappunaṁ, tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, sukho puññassa uccayo.
interlinear_english: If a person should make merit, he should do it again and again, let him place his intention there, there is an increase of joy for the one who has made merit.
narrative_pali: Puññañ-ce puriso kayirā, kayirāthetaṁ punappunaṁ, tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, sukho puññassa uccayo.
narrative_english: If a person should make merit, he should do it again and again, let him place

pali_mahasangiti: Pāpopi passati bhadraṁ, Yāva pāpaṁ na paccati; Yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ, Atha pāpo pāpāni passati.
english_sujato: Even the wicked see good things, so long as their wickedness has not ripened. But as soon as that wickedness ripens, then the wicked see wicked things.
interlinear_pali: Pāpo pi passati bhadraṁ yāva pāpaṁ na paccati, yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ atha pāpo pāpāni passati.
interlinear_english: Even the wicked one experiences good fortune while the wickedness does not ripen, but when the wickedness ripens then the wicked one experiences wicked things.
narrative_pali: Pāpo pi passati bhadraṁ yāva pāpaṁ na paccati, yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ atha pāpo pāpāni passati.
narrative_english: The wicked experience good fortune while the wickedness done does not ripen, but when the wickedness ripens then the wicked will experience wicked things.

pali_mahasangiti: Bhadropi passati pāpaṁ, Yāva bhadraṁ na paccati; Yadā ca paccati bhadraṁ, Atha bhadro bhadrāni passati.
english_sujato: Even the good see wicked things, so long as their goodness has not ripened. But as soon as that goodness ripens, then the good see good things.
interlinear_pali: Bhadro pi passati pāpaṁ yāva bhadraṁ na paccati, yadā ca paccati bhadraṁ atha bhadro bhadrāni passati.
interlinear_english: Even the fortunate one experiences wickedness as long as the good fortune does not ripen, but when the fortune ripens then the fortunate one experiences good fortune.

pali_mahasangiti: Māvamaññetha pāpassa, na mantaṁ āgamissati; Udabindunipātena, udakumbhopi pūrati; Bālo pūrati pāpassa, thokaṁ thokampi ācinaṁ.
english_sujato: Think not lightly of evil, that it won’t come back to you. The pot is filled with water falling drop by drop; the fool is filled with wickedness piled up bit by bit.
interlinear_pali: Māppamaññetha pāpassa: na maṁ taṁ āgamissati, udabindunipātena udakumbho pi pūrati, bālo pūrati pāpassa, thokaṁ thokam-pi ācinaṁ.
interlinear_english: One should not despise a little wickedness (thinking): it will not come to me, through the falling of water drops the water-pot is (quickly) filled, the fool, gathering bit by bit, becomes full of wickedness.
narrative_pali: Māppamaññetha pāpassa: na maṁ taṁ āgamissati, udabindunipātena udakumbho pi pūrati, bālo pūrati pāpassa, thokaṁ thokam-pi ācinaṁ.
narrative_english: One should not despise wickedness thinking: it will not come to me, through the falling of water drops even the water-pot is filled, the fool is filled with wickedness, accumulating bit by bit.

pali_mahasangiti: Māvamaññetha puññassa, na mandaṁ āgamissati; Udabindunipātena, udakumbhopi pūrati; Dhīro pūrati puññassa, thokaṁ thokampi ācinaṁ.
english_sujato: Think not lightly of goodness, that it won’t come back to you. The pot is filled with water falling drop by drop; the attentive one is filled with goodness piled up bit by bit.
interlinear_pali: Māppamaññetha puññassa: na maṁ taṁ āgamissati. udabindunipātena udakumbho pi pūrati, dhīro pūrati puññassa, thokathokam-pi ācinaṁ.
interlinear_english: One should not despise a little merit (thinking): it will not come to me, through the falling of water drops the water-pot is (quickly) filled, the wise one, gathering bit by bit, becomes full of merit.
narrative_pali: Māppamaññetha puññassa: na maṁ taṁ āgamissati. udabindunipātena udakumbho pi pūrati, dhīro pūrati puññassa, thokathokam-pi ācinaṁ.
narrative_english: One should not despise one’s merit thinking: it will not come to me, through the falling of water drops

pali_mahasangiti: Vāṇijova bhayaṁ maggaṁ, appasattho mahaddhano; Visaṁ jīvitukāmova, pāpāni parivajjaye.
english_sujato: Avoid wickedness, as a merchant with rich cargo and small escort would avoid a dangerous road, or one who loves life would avoid drinking poison.
interlinear_pali: Vāṇijo va bhayaṁ maggaṁ, appasattho mahaddhano, visaṁ jīvitukāmo va, pāpāni parivajjaye.
interlinear_english: Like a merchant on a fearful path, with few friends and great wealth, as one loving life (would avoid) poison, (so) should one avoid wicked deeds.

pali_mahasangiti: Pāṇimhi ce vaṇo nāssa, hareyya pāṇinā visaṁ; Nābbaṇaṁ visamanveti, natthi pāpaṁ akubbato.
english_sujato: You can carry poison in your hand if it has no wound, for poison does not infect without a wound; nothing bad happens unless you do bad.
interlinear_pali: Pāṇimhi ce vaṇo nāssa hareyya pāṇinā visaṁ, nābbaṇaṁ visam-anveti, natthi pāpaṁ akubbato.
interlinear_english: If there is no wound in his hand he can carry poison with his hand, poison does not enter without a wound, there is no bad result for the one who does no (wrong).
narrative_pali: Pāṇimhi ce vaṇo nāssa hareyya pāṇinā visaṁ, nābbaṇaṁ visam-anveti, natthi pāpaṁ akubbato.
narrative_english: If there is no wound in his hand he can carry poison with it, poison does not enter without a wound, there is no bad result for the one who does not do wrong.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati, Suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa; Tameva bālaṁ pacceti pāpaṁ, Sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṁva khitto.
english_sujato: Whoever wrongs a man who has done no wrong, a pure man who has not a blemish, the evil backfires on the fool, like fine dust thrown upwind.
interlinear_pali: So appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati, suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa, tam-eva bālaṁ pacceti pāpaṁ, sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṁ va khitto.
interlinear_english: One offends against the inoffensive one, a purified and passionless person, that wicked deed (then) returns to the fool, like fine dust that is thrown against the wind.

pali_mahasangiti: Gabbhameke uppajjanti, nirayaṁ pāpakammino; Saggaṁ sugatino yanti, parinibbanti anāsavā.
english_sujato: Some are born in a womb; evildoers go to hell; the virtuous go to heaven; the undefiled are fully extinguished.
interlinear_pali: Gabbham-eke ’papajjanti, nirayaṁ pāpakammino, saggaṁ sugatino yanti, parinibbanti anāsavā.
interlinear_english: Some are reborn in the womb, (but) those who are wicked in the underworld, the righteous go to heaven, those who are pollutant-free are emancipated.

pali_mahasangiti: Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe, Na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa; Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso, Yatthaṭṭhito mucceyya pāpakammā.
english_sujato: Not in midair, nor mid-ocean, nor hiding in a mountain cleft; you’ll find no place on the planet to escape your wicked deeds.
interlinear_pali: Na antalikkhe, na samuddamajjhe, na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa: na vijjatī so jagatippadeso yatthaṭṭhito mucceyya pāpakammā.
interlinear_english: Neither in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor after entering a mountain cleft: there is no place found on this earth where one can be free from (the results of) wicked deeds.

pali_mahasangiti: Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe, Na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa; Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso, Yatthaṭṭhitaṁ nappasaheyya maccu.
english_sujato: Not in midair, nor mid-ocean, nor hiding in a mountain cleft; you’ll find no place on the planet where you won’t be vanquished by death.
interlinear_pali: Na antalikkhe, na samuddamajjhe, na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa: na vijjatī so jagatippadeso, yatthaṭṭhitaṁ nappasahetha maccu.
interlinear_english: Neither in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor after entering a mountain cleft: there is no place found on this earth, in which death does not overcome one.

pali_mahasangiti: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbe bhāyanti maccuno; Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
english_sujato: All tremble at the rod, all fear death. Treating others like oneself, neither kill nor incite to kill.
interlinear_pali: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbe bhāyanti maccuno, attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
interlinear_english: Everyone trembles at the stick, everyone is in fear of death, comparing oneself (with others), one should not hurt or have (them) hurt.

pali_mahasangiti: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbesaṁ jīvitaṁ piyaṁ; Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
english_sujato: All tremble at the rod, all love life. Treating others like oneself, neither kill nor incite to kill.
interlinear_pali: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbesaṁ jīvitaṁ piyaṁ, attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
interlinear_english: Everyone trembles at the stick, for all of them life is dear, comparing oneself (with others), one should not hurt or have (them) hurt.
narrative_pali: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbesaṁ jīvitaṁ piyaṁ, attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
narrative_english: Everyone trembles at the stick, for all of them their life is dear, comparing oneself with others, one should not hurt or have them hurt.

pali_mahasangiti: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni, yo daṇḍena vihiṁsati; Attano sukhamesāno, pecca so na labhate sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: Creatures love happiness, so if you harm them with a stick in search of your own happiness, after death you won’t find happiness.
interlinear_pali: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni yo daṇḍena vihiṁsati, attano sukham-esāno, pecca so na labhate sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: One who harms with a stick beings who desire happiness, while seeking happiness for himself, won’t find happiness after death.
narrative_pali: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni yo daṇḍena vihiṁsati,
narrative_english: attano sukham-esāno, pecca so na labhate sukhaṁ. One who harms with a stick beings who also desire happiness,

pali_mahasangiti: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni, yo daṇḍena na hiṁsati; Attano sukhamesāno, pecca so labhate sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: Creatures love happiness, so if you don’t harm them with a stick in search of your own happiness, after death you will find happiness.
interlinear_pali: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni yo daṇḍena na hiṁsati, attano sukham-esāno, pecca so labhate sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: One who harms not with a stick beings who desire happiness, while seeking happiness for himself, will find happiness after death.

pali_mahasangiti: Māvoca pharusaṁ kañci, vuttā paṭivadeyyu taṁ; Dukkhā hi sārambhakathā, paṭidaṇḍā phuseyyu taṁ.
english_sujato: Don’t speak harshly, they may speak harshly back. For aggressive speech is painful, and the rod may spring back on you.
interlinear_pali: Māvoca pharusaṁ kañci, vuttā paṭivadeyyu’ taṁ, dukkhā hi sārambhakathā, paṭidaṇḍā phuseyyu’ taṁ.
interlinear_english: Do not say anything harsh, spoken to they might answer back to you, for arrogant talk entails misery, and they might strike you back with a stick.
narrative_pali: Māvoca pharusaṁ kañci, vuttā paṭivadeyyu’ taṁ, dukkhā hi sārambhakathā, paṭidaṇḍā phuseyyu’ taṁ. Don’t say anything harsh,
narrative_english: spoken to, they might answer back to you,

pali_mahasangiti: Sace neresi attānaṁ, kaṁso upahato yathā; Esa pattosi nibbānaṁ, sārambho te na vijjati.
english_sujato: If you still yourself like a broken gong, you reach extinguishment and know no conflict.
interlinear_pali: Sace neresi attānaṁ kaṁso upahato yathā, esa pattosi Nibbānaṁ, sārambho te na vijjati.
interlinear_english: If you make no sound like a gong that is broken, you are (like) one who has attained Nibbāna, contention is not found in you.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathā daṇḍena gopālo, gāvo pājeti gocaraṁ; Evaṁ jarā ca maccu ca, āyuṁ pājenti pāṇinaṁ.
english_sujato: As a cowherd drives the cows to pasture with the rod, so too old age and death drive life from living beings.
interlinear_pali: Yathā daṇḍena gopālo gāvo pāceti gocaraṁ, evaṁ jarā ca maccu ca āyuṁ pācenti pāṇinaṁ.
interlinear_english: Like a cowherd with a stick drives cattle to pasture, so do old age and death drive life out of beings.
narrative_pali: Yathā daṇḍena gopālo gāvo pāceti gocaraṁ, evaṁ jarā ca maccu ca āyuṁ pācenti pāṇinaṁ.
narrative_english: Like a cowherd with stick drives cattle to pasture, so do old age and death drive life out of beings.

pali_mahasangiti: Atha pāpāni kammāni, karaṁ bālo na bujjhati; Sehi kammehi dummedho, aggidaḍḍhova tappati.
english_sujato: The fool does not understand the evil that they do. But because of those deeds, that simpleton is tormented as if burnt by fire.
interlinear_pali: Atha pāpāni kammāni karaṁ bālo na bujjhati, sehi kammehi dummedho aggidaḍḍho va tappati.
interlinear_english: The fool does not understand the wicked deeds he is doing, the stupid one is consumed by his deeds as (by) a burning fire.
narrative_pali: Atha pāpāni kammāni karaṁ bālo na bujjhati, sehi kammehi dummedho aggidaḍḍho va tappati.
narrative_english: The fool does not yet understand the wicked deeds he is doing, the stupid one is consumed by his deeds as by a burning fire.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo daṇḍena adaṇḍesu, appaduṭṭhesu dussati; Dasannamaññataraṁ ṭhānaṁ, khippameva nigacchati.
english_sujato: One who violently attacks the peaceful and the innocent swiftly falls to one of ten bad states:
interlinear_pali: Yo daṇḍena adaṇḍesu appaduṭṭhesu dussati dasannam-aññataraṁ ṭhānaṁ khippam-eva nigacchati:
interlinear_english: Whoever offends with a stick those who are inoffensive and harmless will quickly fall into one of ten states:
narrative_pali: Yo daṇḍena adaṇḍesu appaduṭṭhesu dussati dasannam-aññataraṁ ṭhānaṁ khippam-eva nigacchati:
narrative_english: Whoever offends with a stick those who are inoffensive and harmless will quickly fall into one of the following ten states:

pali_mahasangiti: Vedanaṁ pharusaṁ jāniṁ, sarīrassa va bhedanaṁ; Garukaṁ vāpi ābādhaṁ, cittakkhepaṁ va pāpuṇe.
english_sujato: harsh pain; loss; the breakup of the body; serious illness; mental distress;
interlinear_pali: vedanaṁ pharusaṁ, jāniṁ, sarīrassa ca bhedanaṁ, garukaṁ vā pi ābādhaṁ, cittakkhepaṁ va pāpuṇe,
interlinear_english: harsh feelings, loss (of his wealth), and the break up of the body, or even heavy affliction, or surely he will lose his mind,

pali_mahasangiti: Rājato vā upasaggaṁ, Abbhakkhānaṁ va dāruṇaṁ; Parikkhayaṁ va ñātīnaṁ, Bhogānaṁ va pabhaṅguraṁ.
english_sujato: hazards from rulers; vicious slander; loss of kin; destruction of wealth;
interlinear_pali: rājato vā upassaggaṁ, abbhakkhānaṁ va dāruṇaṁ, parikkhayaṁ va ñātīnaṁ, bhogānaṁ va pabhaṅguraṁ,
interlinear_english: (there may be) danger from the King, or slander that is terrible, (he may suffer from) loss of kin, or (from) the destruction of wealth,

pali_mahasangiti: Atha vāssa agārāni, aggi ḍahati pāvako; Kāyassa bhedā duppañño, nirayaṁ sopapajjati.
english_sujato: or else their home is consumed by fire. When their body breaks up, that witless person is reborn in hell.
interlinear_pali: atha vāssa agārāni aggi ḍahati pāvako, kāyassa bhedā duppañño nirayaṁ so upapajjati.
interlinear_english: also his houses may be consumed by flames and fire, and at the break-up of the body that one lacking in wisdom will arise in the underworld.

pali_mahasangiti: Na naggacariyā na jaṭā na paṅkā, Nānāsakā thaṇḍilasāyikā vā; Rajojallaṁ ukkuṭikappadhānaṁ, Sodhenti maccaṁ avitiṇṇakaṅkhaṁ.
english_sujato: Not nudity, nor matted hair, nor mud, nor fasting, nor lying on bare ground, nor wearing dust and dirt, or squatting on the heels, will cleanse a mortal not free of doubt.
interlinear_pali: Na naggacariyā na jaṭā na paṅkā, nānāsakā thaṇḍilasāyikā vā, rājo ca jallaṁ ukkuṭikappadhānaṁ, sodhenti maccaṁ avitiṇṇakaṅkhaṁ.
interlinear_english: Not going naked, nor matted hair, nor mud, nor fasting or lying on stony ground, dust and dirt, (or) striving while squatting, can purify a mortal who has not removed uncertainty.
interlinear_notes: There seems to be no particular reason this is in the Chapter about the Stick.
narrative_pali: Na naggacariyā na jaṭā na paṅkā, nānāsakā thaṇḍilasāyikā vā, rājo ca jallaṁ ukkuṭikappadhānaṁ, sodhenti maccaṁ avitiṇṇakaṅkhaṁ.
narrative_english: Not nakedness, matted hair, mud, fasting, lying on stony ground, dust, dirt, or striving while squatting, can purify a mortal who has not removed uncertainty.

pali_mahasangiti: Alaṅkato cepi samaṁ careyya, Santo danto niyato brahmacārī; Sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṁ, So brāhmaṇo so samaṇo sa bhikkhu.
english_sujato: Dressed up they may be, but if they live well— peaceful, tamed, committed to the spiritual path, having laid aside violence toward all creatures— they are a brahmin, an ascetic, a mendicant.
interlinear_pali: Alaṅkato ce pi samaṁ careyya, santo danto niyato brahmacārī, sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṁ, so brāhmaṇo so samaṇo sa bhikkhu.
interlinear_english: Even if he were to adorn himself, (but) is peaceful, trained, settled, spiritual, and has put aside the stick towards all beings, he is a brahmin, an ascetic, a monastic.
interlinear_notes: This could also be translated as has put aside violence towards all beings.

pali_mahasangiti: Hirīnisedho puriso, koci lokasmi vijjati; Yo niddaṁ apabodheti, asso bhadro kasāmiva.
english_sujato: Can a person constrained by conscience be found in the world? Who shies away from blame, like a fine horse from the whip?
interlinear_pali: Hirīnisedho puriso koci lokasmi’ vijjati, yo nindaṁ appabodhati, asso bhadro kasām-iva.
interlinear_english: Whatever person in the world is found restrained by conscience, and is aware of his fault, is like a good horse that is (restrained) by a whip.

pali_mahasangiti: Asso yathā bhadro kasāniviṭṭho, Ātāpino saṁvegino bhavātha; Saddhāya sīlena ca vīriyena ca, Samādhinā dhammavinicchayena ca; Sampannavijjācaraṇā patissatā, Jahissatha dukkhamidaṁ anappakaṁ.
english_sujato: Like a fine horse under the whip, be keen and full of urgency. With faith, ethics, and energy, immersion, and investigation of principles, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, mindful, give up this vast suffering.
interlinear_pali: Asso yathā bhadro kasāniviṭṭho, ātāpino saṁvegino bhavātha. Saddhāya sīlena ca vīriyena ca, samādhinā Dhammavinicchayena ca. Sampannavijjācaraṇā patissatā, pahassatha dukkham-idaṁ anappakaṁ.
interlinear_english: Like a good horse restrained by the whip, you should be ardent and spiritually intense. Having faith, virtue and energy, concentration and investigation of the Dhamma. One who has understanding and good conduct, mindfulness, will abandon this not insignificant suffering.
interlinear_notes: Again these two verses have no connection to a stick, but also do not fit in thematically with any other chapter either.
narrative_pali: Asso yathā bhadro kasāniviṭṭho, ātāpino saṁvegino bhavātha. Saddhāya sīlena ca vīriyena ca, samādhinā Dhammavinicchayena ca. Sampannavijjācaraṇā patissatā, pahassatha dukkham-idaṁ anappakaṁ.
narrative_english: Like a good horse restrained by whip, you should be ardent and intense.

pali_mahasangiti: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā, Usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ; Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, Attānaṁ damayanti subbatā.
english_sujato: While irrigators guide water, fletchers bend arrows straight, and carpenters bend timber straight, those true to their vows tame themselves.
interlinear_pali: Udakaṁ hi nayanti nettikā, usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ, dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, attānaṁ damayanti subbatā.
interlinear_english: Course-makers lead water, fletchers straighten arrows, carpenters straighten wood, the mild master themselves.
interlinear_notes: For a variant of this verse, see verse 80 above.

pali_mahasangiti: Ko nu hāso kimānando, niccaṁ pajjalite sati; Andhakārena onaddhā, padīpaṁ na gavesatha.
english_sujato: What is joy, what is laughter, when the flames are ever burning? Swathed in darkness, would you not seek a light?
interlinear_pali: Ko nu hāso, kim-ānando, niccaṁ pajjalite sati, andhakārena onaddhā, padīpaṁ na gavesatha?
interlinear_english: Why this laughter, why this joy, when the world is constantly burning, why, when enveloped by darkness, do you not seek for a light?

pali_mahasangiti: Passa cittakataṁ bimbaṁ, arukāyaṁ samussitaṁ; Āturaṁ bahusaṅkappaṁ, yassa natthi dhuvaṁ ṭhiti.
english_sujato: See this fancy puppet, a body built of sores, diseased, obsessed over, in which nothing lasts at all.
interlinear_pali: Passa cittakataṁ bimbaṁ, arukāyaṁ samussitaṁ, āturaṁ bahusaṅkappaṁ, yassa natthi dhuvaṁ ṭhiti.
interlinear_english: See this beautified manikin, a heap of sores that is raised up, sick, imagined in many ways, which has nothing stable or firm.
interlinear_notes: It is very unclear how we should read this, as we are talking about the body it seems translations indicating it has many intentions are incorrect. The comm. says: mahājanena bahudhā saṅkappaṁ, which I follow.
narrative_pali: Passa cittakataṁ bimbaṁ, arukāyaṁ samussitaṁ, āturaṁ bahusaṅkappaṁ, yassa natthi dhuvaṁ ṭhiti.
narrative_english: See this beautified manikin, a heap of sores that is raised up, sick, imagined in many ways, which has nothing stable or firm.

pali_mahasangiti: Parijiṇṇamidaṁ rūpaṁ, roganīḷaṁ pabhaṅguraṁ; Bhijjati pūtisandeho, maraṇantañhi jīvitaṁ.
english_sujato: This body is decrepit and frail, a nest of disease. This foul carcass falls apart, for life ends in death.
interlinear_pali: Parijiṇṇam-idaṁ rūpaṁ, roganīḷaṁ pabhaṅguraṁ, bhijjati pūtisandeho, maraṇantaṁ hi jīvitaṁ.
interlinear_english: This body is worn out, a nest of disease, perishing, the putrid body comes to destruction, for life ends in death.
narrative_pali: Parijiṇṇam-idaṁ rūpaṁ, roganīḷaṁ pabhaṅguraṁ, bhijjati pūtisandeho, maraṇantaṁ hi jīvitaṁ.
narrative_english: This body is worn out, a nest of disease, perishing, putrid, the putrid body will come to destruction, for life ends in death.

pali_mahasangiti: Yānimāni apatthāni, alābūneva sārade; Kāpotakāni aṭṭhīni, tāni disvāna kā rati.
english_sujato: These dove-grey bones are tossed away like dried gourds in the autumn— what joy is there in such a sight?
interlinear_pali: Yānimāni apatthāni alāpūneva sārade kāpotakāni aṭṭhīni, tāni disvāna kā rati?
interlinear_english: Like discarded white gourds thrown away in autumn are these grey bones; seeing them, why is there delight?
interlinear_notes: The comm. positions the Buddha as pointing out discarded corpses as he says this; the word specifically means white gourds.
narrative_pali: Yānimāni apatthāni alāpūneva sārade kāpotakāni aṭṭhīni, tāni disvāna kā rati?
narrative_english: Like discarded white gourds thrown away in autumn are these grey bones; seeing them, why is there delight?

pali_mahasangiti: Aṭṭhīnaṁ nagaraṁ kataṁ, maṁsalohitalepanaṁ; Yattha jarā ca maccu ca, māno makkho ca ohito.
english_sujato: In this city built of bones, plastered with flesh and blood, old age and death are stashed away, along with conceit and contempt.
interlinear_pali: Aṭṭhīnaṁ nagaraṁ kataṁ, maṁsalohitalepanaṁ, yattha jarā ca maccu ca, māno makkho ca ohito.
interlinear_english: This fortress is made out of bones, plastered over with flesh and blood, but hidden within lie old age, death, also conceit and anger.
interlinear_notes: It seems strange to say that the mental states of conceit and anger lie hidden in the body here.
narrative_pali: Aṭṭhīnaṁ nagaraṁ kataṁ, maṁsalohitalepanaṁ, yattha jarā ca maccu ca, māno makkho ca ohito.
narrative_english: This fortress is made out of bones, plastered over with flesh and blood, but hidden within lie old age, death, also conceit and anger.

pali_mahasangiti: Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā, Atho sarīrampi jaraṁ upeti; Satañca dhammo na jaraṁ upeti, Santo have sabbhi pavedayanti.
english_sujato: Fancy chariots of kings wear out, and even this body gets old. But the truth of the good never gets old— so the good proclaim to the good.
interlinear_pali: Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā, atho sarīram-pi jaraṁ upeti, satañ-ca Dhammo na jaraṁ upeti, santo have sabbhi pavedayanti.
interlinear_english: Decorated royal chariots decay, and the body also decays, but the good Dhamma does not decay, the good surely pass it on to the good.
narrative_pali: Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā, atho sarīram-pi jaraṁ upeti, satañ-ca Dhammo na jaraṁ upeti,
narrative_english: santo have sabbhi pavedayanti. Royal chariots will decay, and the body also decays, but the Dhamma does not decay, the good pass it on to the good.

pali_mahasangiti: Appassutāyaṁ puriso, balībaddhova jīrati; Maṁsāni tassa vaḍḍhanti, paññā tassa na vaḍḍhati.
english_sujato: A person of little learning ages like an ox— their flesh grows, but not their wisdom.
interlinear_pali: Appassutāyaṁ puriso balivaddo va jīrati, maṁsāni tassa vaḍḍhanti, paññā tassa na vaḍḍhati.
interlinear_english: The person of little learning increases in age like an ox, (for although) his flesh does increase, his wisdom does not increase.

pali_mahasangiti: Anekajātisaṁsāraṁ, sandhāvissaṁ anibbisaṁ; Gahakāraṁ gavesanto, dukkhā jāti punappunaṁ.
english_sujato: Transmigrating through countless rebirths, I’ve journeyed without reward, searching for the house-builder; painful is birth again and again.
interlinear_pali: Anekajātisaṁsāraṁ sandhāvissaṁ anibbisaṁ gahakārakaṁ gavesanto: dukkhā jāti punappunaṁ.
interlinear_english: Through the round of countless births and deaths I have wandered without finding the housebuilder I was seeking: born and suffering once again.
narrative_pali: Anekajātisaṁsāraṁ sandhāvissaṁ anibbisaṁ gahakārakaṁ gavesanto: dukkhā jāti punappunaṁ.
narrative_english: Through the round of births and deaths I have wandered without finding

pali_mahasangiti: Gahakāraka diṭṭhosi, puna gehaṁ na kāhasi; Sabbā te phāsukā bhaggā, gahakūṭaṁ visaṅkhataṁ; Visaṅkhāragataṁ cittaṁ, taṇhānaṁ khayamajjhagā.
english_sujato: I’ve seen you, house-builder! You won’t build a house again! Your rafters are all broken, your roof-peak demolished. The mind, set on demolition, has reached the end of cravings.
interlinear_pali: Gahakāraka diṭṭhosi! Puna gehaṁ na kāhasi: sabbā te phāsukā bhaggā, gahakūṭaṁ visaṅkhitaṁ, visaṅkhāragataṁ cittaṁ, taṇhānaṁ khayam-ajjhagā.
interlinear_english: O housebuilder, now you are seen! You will not build the house again: all your rafters have been broken, and the ridgepole has been destroyed, my mind has reached the unconditioned, and craving’s end has been achieved.

pali_mahasangiti: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ, aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ; Jiṇṇakoñcāva jhāyanti, khīṇamaccheva pallale.
english_sujato: When young they spurned the spiritual path and failed to earn any wealth. Now they brood like old cranes in a pond bereft of fish.
interlinear_pali: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ, aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ, jiṇṇakoñcā ca jhāyanti khīṇamacche va pallale.
interlinear_english: Not having lived the holy life, not having gained wealth in their youth, they waste away like herons in a small lake devoid of fish.

pali_mahasangiti: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ, aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ; Senti cāpātikhīṇāva, purāṇāni anutthunaṁ.
english_sujato: When young they spurned the spiritual path and failed to earn any wealth. Now they lie like spent arrows, bemoaning over things past.
interlinear_pali: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ senti cāpātikhittā va, purāṇāni anutthunaṁ.
interlinear_english: Not having lived the holy life, not having gained wealth in their youth, they lie like (shafts) shot from a bow, wailing about things in the past.

pali_mahasangiti: Attānañce piyaṁ jaññā, rakkheyya naṁ surakkhitaṁ; Tiṇṇaṁ aññataraṁ yāmaṁ, paṭijaggeyya paṇḍito.
english_sujato: If you knew your self as beloved, you’d look after it so well. In one of the night’s three watches, an astute person would remain alert.
interlinear_pali: Attānañ-ce piyaṁ jaññā rakkheyya naṁ surakkhitaṁ, tiṇṇam-aññataraṁ yāmaṁ paṭijaggeyya paṇḍito.
interlinear_english: If one regards oneself as dear one should guard oneself right well, during one of the three watches (of the night) the wise one should stay alert.
interlinear_notes: The commentary takes yāma as meaning one of the three periods (of life): youth, adulthood and old age; but the Buddha often recommended that one watch of the night should be spent in meditation, and this is the meaning I follow here.
narrative_pali: Attānañ-ce piyaṁ jaññā rakkheyya naṁ surakkhitaṁ, tiṇṇam-aññataraṁ yāmaṁ paṭijaggeyya paṇḍito.
narrative_english: If one regards oneself as dear, one should guard oneself well, during one of three watches of the night the wise person should stay alert.

pali_mahasangiti: Attānameva paṭhamaṁ, patirūpe nivesaye; Athaññamanusāseyya, na kilisseyya paṇḍito.
english_sujato: The astute would avoid being corrupted by first grounding themselves in what is suitable, and then instructing others.
interlinear_pali: Attānam-eva paṭhamaṁ patirūpe nivesaye, athaññam-anusāseyya, na kilisseyya paṇḍito.
interlinear_english: First one should establish oneself in what is suitable, then one can advise another, the wise one should not have (any) defilement.
narrative_pali: Attānam-eva paṭhamaṁ patirūpe nivesaye, athaññam-anusāseyya, na kilisseyya paṇḍito.
narrative_english: First one should establish oneself in what is suitable, then one can advise another, the wise one should not have any defilement.

pali_mahasangiti: Attānañce tathā kayirā, yathāññamanusāsati; Sudanto vata dametha, attā hi kira duddamo.
english_sujato: If one were to treat oneself as one instructs another, the well-tamed indeed would tame: for the self, it seems, is hard to tame.
interlinear_pali: Attānañ-ce tathā kayirā yathaññam-anusāsati, sudanto vata dametha, attā hi kira duddamo.
interlinear_english: He should do himself as he would advise another (to do), being well-trained, he could surely train (another), for it is said the self is difficult to train.
narrative_pali: Attānañ-ce tathā kayirā yathaññam-anusāsati, sudanto vata dametha, attā hi kira duddamo.
narrative_english: He should do as he would advise another to do, then being well-trained, he could train another, for self is difficult to train.

pali_mahasangiti: Attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā; Attanā hi sudantena, nāthaṁ labhati dullabhaṁ.
english_sujato: One is indeed the lord of oneself, for who else would be one’s lord? By means of a well-tamed self, one gains a lord that’s rare indeed.
interlinear_pali: Attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā? Attanā va sudantena nāthaṁ labhati dullabhaṁ.
interlinear_english: For the self is the friend of self, for what other friend would there be? When the self is well-trained, one finds a friend that is hard to find.
narrative_pali: Attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā? Attanā va sudantena nāthaṁ labhati dullabhaṁ.
narrative_english: For the self is the friend of self, for what other friend would there be? When the self has been well-trained, one finds a friend that is hard to find.

pali_mahasangiti: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ, Attajaṁ attasambhavaṁ; Abhimatthati dummedhaṁ, Vajiraṁvasmamayaṁ maṇiṁ.
english_sujato: For the evil that is done by oneself, born and produced in oneself, grinds down a simpleton, as diamond grinds a lesser gem.
interlinear_pali: Attanā va kataṁ pāpaṁ, attajaṁ attasambhavaṁ, abhimatthati dummedhaṁ vajiraṁ vasmamayaṁ maṇiṁ.
interlinear_english: That wickedness done by oneself, born in oneself, arising in oneself, crushes the one who is stupid, as a diamond (crushes) a rock-jewel.
interlinear_notes: It seems odd to compare wickedness to a diamond and the self to a rock-jewel (presumably meaning a fake jewel), and the simile is not convincing. It is presumably the ease with which a diamond crushes a fake jewel which is being highlighted.
narrative_pali: Attanā va kataṁ pāpaṁ, attajaṁ attasambhavaṁ, abhimatthati dummedhaṁ vajiraṁ vasmamayaṁ maṇiṁ.
narrative_english: That wickedness done by oneself, born and arising in oneself, crushes the one who is stupid, as diamond a rock-jewel.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa accantadussilyaṁ, māluvā sālamivotthataṁ; Karoti so tathattānaṁ, yathā naṁ icchatī diso.
english_sujato: One choked by immorality, as a sal tree by a creeper, does to themselves what a foe only wishes.
interlinear_pali: Yassa accantadussīlyaṁ, māluvā Sālam-ivotataṁ, karoti so tathattānaṁ yathā naṁ icchatī diso.
interlinear_english: The one who has an exceeding lack of virtue, like a deadly creeper covering a Sal tree, makes himself the same as his enemy wishes him to be.
narrative_pali: Yassa accantadussīlyaṁ māluvā Sālam-ivotataṁ
narrative_english: karoti so tathattānaṁ yathā naṁ icchatī diso.

pali_mahasangiti: Sukarāni asādhūni, attano ahitāni ca; Yaṁ ve hitañca sādhuñca, taṁ ve paramadukkaraṁ.
english_sujato: It’s easy to do bad things harmful to oneself, but good things that are helpful are the hardest things to do.
interlinear_pali: Sukarāni asādhūni, attano ahitāni ca, yaṁ ve hitañ-ca sādhuñ-ca taṁ ve paramadukkaraṁ.
interlinear_english: Easily done are things not good, and unbeneficial for oneself, but that which is beneficial and good is supremely hard to do.
narrative_pali: Sukarāni asādhūni, attano ahitāni ca, yaṁ ve hitañ-ca sādhuñ-ca taṁ ve paramadukkaraṁ.
narrative_english: Easily done are things not good, unbeneficial for oneself, but that which is beneficial is exceedingly hard to do.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo sāsanaṁ arahataṁ, ariyānaṁ dhammajīvinaṁ; Paṭikkosati dummedho, diṭṭhiṁ nissāya pāpikaṁ; Phalāni kaṭṭhakasseva, attaghātāya phallati.
english_sujato: On account of wicked views— scorning the guidance of the perfected ones, the noble ones living righteously— the idiot begets their own self’s demise, like the bamboo bearing fruit.
interlinear_pali: Yo sāsanaṁ arahataṁ Ariyānaṁ Dhammajīvinaṁ paṭikkosati dummedho diṭṭhiṁ nissāya pāpikaṁ, phalāni kaṭṭhakasseva attaghaññāya phallati.
interlinear_english: * Whoever reviles the worthy teaching of the Noble Ones who live by Dhamma, that stupid one, depending on wicked views, like the bamboo when it bears fruit, brings about his own destruction.
interlinear_notes: The bamboo flowers only after a very great length of time (often 60+ years or more), and then dies.
narrative_pali: Yo sāsanaṁ arahataṁ Ariyānaṁ Dhammajīvinaṁ paṭikkosati dummedho diṭṭhiṁ nissāya pāpikaṁ, phalāni kaṭṭhakasseva attaghaññāya phallati.
narrative_english: Whoever reviles the worthy teaching of the Noble Ones who live by Dhamma, that stupid one, depending on wrong views, like the bamboo when it bears fruit, brings about his own destruction.

pali_mahasangiti: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ, attanā saṅkilissati; Attanā akataṁ pāpaṁ, attanāva visujjhati; Suddhī asuddhi paccattaṁ, nāñño aññaṁ visodhaye.
english_sujato: For it is by oneself that evil’s done, one is corrupted by oneself. It’s by oneself that evil’s not done, one is purified by oneself. Purity and impurity are personal matters, no one can purify another.
interlinear_pali: Attanā va kataṁ pāpaṁ, attanā saṅkilissati, attanā akataṁ pāpaṁ, attanā va visujjhati, suddhī asuddhī paccattaṁ, nāñño aññaṁ visodhaye.
interlinear_english: By oneself alone is a wicked deed done, by oneself is one defiled, by oneself is a wicked deed left undone, by oneself is one purified, purity and impurity come from oneself, (for) no one can purify another.
narrative_pali: Attanā va kataṁ pāpaṁ, attanā saṅkilissati, attanā akataṁ pāpaṁ, attanā va visujjhati, suddhī asuddhī paccattaṁ, nāñño aññaṁ visodhaye.
narrative_english: By self is a wicked deed done, by self is one defiled, by self is a wicked deed left undone, by oneself is one purified, purity and impurity come from oneself, for no one can

pali_mahasangiti: Attadatthaṁ paratthena, bahunāpi na hāpaye; Attadatthamabhiññāya, sadatthapasuto siyā.
english_sujato: Never neglect what is good for yourself for the sake of another, however great. Knowing well what is good for yourself, be intent upon your heart’s goal.
interlinear_pali: Atta-d-atthaṁ paratthena bahunā pi na hāpaye; atta-d-attham-abhiññāya sa-d-atthapasuto siyā.
interlinear_english: One should not neglect one’s own good for another’s, however great; knowing what is good for oneself one should be intent on that good.

pali_mahasangiti: Hīnaṁ dhammaṁ na seveyya, pamādena na saṁvase; Micchādiṭṭhiṁ na seveyya, na siyā lokavaḍḍhano.
english_sujato: Don’t resort to lowly things, don’t abide in negligence, don’t resort to wrong views, don’t perpetuate the world.
interlinear_pali: Hīnaṁ dhammaṁ na seveyya, pamādena na saṁvase, micchādiṭṭhiṁ na seveyya, na siyā lokavaḍḍhano.
interlinear_english: One should not follow lowly things, one should not abide heedlessly, one should not follow a wrong view, one should not foster worldliness.
interlinear_notes: Defined as being the five strands of sense pleasure.
narrative_pali: Hīnaṁ dhammaṁ na seveyya, pamādena na saṁvase, micchādiṭṭhiṁ na seveyya, na siyā lokavaḍḍhano.
narrative_english: One should not follow lowly things, one should not abide heedlessly, one should not follow a wrong view, one should not foster worldliness.

pali_mahasangiti: Uttiṭṭhe nappamajjeyya, dhammaṁ sucaritaṁ care; Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti, asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
english_sujato: Get up, don’t be heedless, live by principle, with good conduct. For one of good conduct sleeps at ease, in this world and the next.
interlinear_pali: Uttiṭṭhe nappamajjeyya, Dhammaṁ sucaritaṁ care, Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
interlinear_english: One should strive, not be heedless, one should live by Dhamma, with good conduct, living by Dhamma one lives at ease in this world and the next.

pali_mahasangiti: Dhammaṁ care sucaritaṁ, na naṁ duccaritaṁ care; Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti, asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
english_sujato: Live by principle, with good conduct, don’t conduct yourself badly. For one of good conduct sleeps at ease, in this world and the next.
interlinear_pali: Dhammaṁ care sucaritaṁ, na naṁ duccaritaṁ care, Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
interlinear_english: One should live by Dhamma, with good conduct, not with bad conduct, living by Dhamma one lives at ease in this world and the next.
narrative_pali: Dhammaṁ care sucaritaṁ, na naṁ duccaritaṁ care, Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
narrative_english: One should live by Dhamma, with good conduct and not with bad conduct, living by Dhamma one will live at ease in this world and the next.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathā pubbuḷakaṁ passe, yathā passe marīcikaṁ; Evaṁ lokaṁ avekkhantaṁ, maccurājā na passati.
english_sujato: Look upon the world as a bubble or a mirage, then the King of Death won’t see you.
interlinear_pali: Yathā bubbulakaṁ passe, yathā passe marīcikaṁ, evaṁ lokaṁ avekkhantaṁ Maccurājā na passati.
interlinear_english: One should see it as a bubble, one should see it as a mirage, looking on the world in this way the King of Death does not see (one).
narrative_pali: Yathā bubbulakaṁ passe, yathā passe marīcikaṁ, evaṁ lokaṁ avekkhantaṁ Maccurājā na passati.
narrative_english: One should see it as a bubble, one should see it as a mirage, looking on the world in this way the King of Death does not see one.

pali_mahasangiti: Etha passathimaṁ lokaṁ, cittaṁ rājarathūpamaṁ; Yattha bālā visīdanti, natthi saṅgo vijānataṁ.
english_sujato: Come, see this world decked out like a fancy royal chariot. Here fools founder, but the discerning are not chained.
interlinear_pali: Etha passathimaṁ lokaṁ cittaṁ rājarathūpamaṁ, yattha bālā visīdanti – natthi saṅgo vijānataṁ.
interlinear_english: Come, look upon this world adorned like a king’s gilded chariot, where fools become depressed – there is no bond for those who understand.
narrative_pali: Etha passathimaṁ lokaṁ cittaṁ rājarathūpamaṁ, yattha bālā visīdanti – natthi saṅgo vijānataṁ.
narrative_english: Come, look upon this world adorned like a king’s gilded chariot, where fools become depressed – there is no bond for those who understand.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca pubbe pamajjitvā, pacchā so nappamajjati; Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.
english_sujato: He who once was heedless, but turned to heedfulness, lights up the world like the moon freed from clouds.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca pubbe pamajjitvā, pacchā so nappamajjati, sŏ imaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti abbhā mutto va candimā.
interlinear_english: Whoever was heedless before, but later is not heedless, that one shines brightly on this world like the moon released from a cloud.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ, kusalena pidhīyati; Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.
english_sujato: Someone whose bad deed is supplanted by the good, lights up the world, like the moon freed from clouds.
interlinear_pali: Yassa pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ kusalena pithīyati – sŏ imaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti abbhā mutto va candimā.
interlinear_english: The one whose wicked deed is covered over by a good deed – that one shines brightly on this world like the moon released from a cloud.
narrative_pali: Yassa pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ kusalena pithīyati – sŏ imaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti abbhā mutto va candimā.
narrative_english: The person whose wicked deed is covered over by a good deed – that one shines brightly on this world like the moon released from a cloud.

pali_mahasangiti: Andhabhūto ayaṁ loko, tanukettha vipassati; Sakuṇo jālamuttova, appo saggāya gacchati.
english_sujato: Blind is the world, few are those who clearly see. Only a handful go to heaven, like a bird freed from a net.
interlinear_pali: Andhabhūto ayaṁ loko, tanukettha vipassati, sakunto jālamutto va appo saggāya gacchati.
interlinear_english: This world is blind, few here have true insight, as few go to heaven as birds that escape from the net.

pali_mahasangiti: Haṁsādiccapathe yanti, ākāse yanti iddhiyā; Nīyanti dhīrā lokamhā, jetvā māraṁ savāhiniṁ.
english_sujato: Swans fly by the sun’s path, psychic sages fly through space. The attentive leave the world, having vanquished Māra with his legions.
interlinear_pali: Haṁsādiccapathe yanti, ākāse yanti iddhiyā, nīyanti dhīrā lokamhā, jetvā Māraṁ savāhanaṁ.
interlinear_english: Geese go through the path of the sky, they go through the firmament by their power, the wise are led out of the world, after beating Māra and his host.
narrative_pali: Haṁsādiccapathe yanti, ākāse yanti iddhiyā, nīyanti dhīrā lokamhā, jetvā Māraṁ savāhanaṁ.
narrative_english: Geese go through the path of the sky, through the heavens by their power,

pali_mahasangiti: Ekaṁ dhammaṁ atītassa, musāvādissa jantuno; Vitiṇṇaparalokassa, natthi pāpaṁ akāriyaṁ.
english_sujato: When a personage, spurning the hereafter, transgresses in just one thing— lying— there is no evil they would not do.
interlinear_pali: Ekaṁ dhammaṁ atītassa, musāvādissa jantuno, vitiṇṇaparalokassa, natthi pāpaṁ akāriyaṁ.
interlinear_english: For the person speaking falsely, who has transgressed in this one thing, who has abandoned the next world, there is no wickedness left undone.
narrative_pali: Ekaṁ dhammaṁ atītassa, musāvādissa jantuno, vitiṇṇaparalokassa, natthi pāpaṁ akāriyaṁ.
narrative_english: For the person speaking falsely who transgresses in this one thing, who has abandoned the next world, there is no bad thing left undone.

pali_mahasangiti: Na ve kadariyā devalokaṁ vajanti, Bālā have nappasaṁsanti dānaṁ; Dhīro ca dānaṁ anumodamāno, Teneva so hoti sukhī parattha.
english_sujato: The miserly don’t ascend to heaven, it takes a fool to not praise giving. The attentive celebrate giving, and so find happiness in the hereafter.
interlinear_pali: Na ve kadariyā devalokaṁ vajanti, bālā have nappasaṁsanti dānaṁ, dhīro ca dānaṁ anumodamāno, teneva so hoti sukhī parattha.
interlinear_english: The miserly go not to the world of the gods, fools surely do not praise giving, but the wise one rejoices in giving, and through that he is happy hereafter.

pali_mahasangiti: Pathabyā ekarajjena, saggassa gamanena vā; Sabbalokādhipaccena, sotāpattiphalaṁ varaṁ.
english_sujato: The fruit of stream-entry is better than being the one king of the earth, than going to heaven, than lordship over all the world.
interlinear_pali: Pathavyā ekarajjena, saggassa gamanena vā, sabbalokādhipaccena – sotāpattiphalaṁ varaṁ.
interlinear_english: Having sole sovereignty over the earth, or going to heaven, or lordship over the whole world – better is the fruit of stream-entry.
interlinear_notes: These three terms (ekarajjena, gamanena, ādhipaccena) are ablative-like instrumentals.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa jitaṁ nāvajīyati, Jitaṁ yassa noyāti koci loke; Taṁ buddhamanantagocaraṁ, Apadaṁ kena padena nessatha.
english_sujato: He whose victory may not be undone, a victory unrivaled in all the world; by what track would you trace that Buddha, who leaves no track in his infinite range?
interlinear_pali: Yassa jitaṁ nāvajīyati, - jitaṁ assa no yāti koci loke, tam-Buddham-anantagocaraṁ, apadaṁ kena padena nessatha?
interlinear_english: He whose victory cannot be undone, whose victory no one here approaches, the Buddha, whose range is endless, by what path can you lead the pathless one?
narrative_pali: Yassa jitaṁ nāvajīyati, -
narrative_english: jitaṁ assa no yāti koci loke,

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa jālinī visattikā, Taṇhā natthi kuhiñci netave; Taṁ buddhamanantagocaraṁ, Apadaṁ kena padena nessatha.
english_sujato: Of craving, the weaver, the clinger, he has none: so where can he be traced? By what track would you trace that Buddha, who leaves no track in his infinite range?
interlinear_pali: Yassa jālinī visattikā, taṇhā natthi kuhiñci netave, tam-Buddham-anantagocaraṁ, apadaṁ kena padena nessatha?
interlinear_english: * For him there is no desire, attachment, or craving to lead (him) anywhere, the Buddha, whose range is endless, by what path can you lead the pathless one?
interlinear_notes: This is the clue to the translation of this verse; what it is talking about is having none of the states (padāni) of craving (taṇhā), etc. by which the one beyond those states (apadaṁ) could be led.

pali_mahasangiti: Ye jhānapasutā dhīrā, nekkhammūpasame ratā; Devāpi tesaṁ pihayanti, sambuddhānaṁ satīmataṁ.
english_sujato: The attentive intent on absorption, who love the peace of renunciation, the Buddhas, ever mindful, are envied by even the gods.
interlinear_pali: Ye jhānapasutā dhīrā, nekkhammūpasame ratā, devā pi tesaṁ pihayanti, Sambuddhānaṁ satīmataṁ.
interlinear_english: Those wise ones intent on meditation, who delight in the peace of renunciation, even the gods are envious of them, the Sambuddhas, the ones who are mindful.
interlinear_notes: Comm: jhānapasutā ti lakkhaṇūpanijjhānaṃ ārammaṇūpanijjhānan-ti; intent on meditation means meditating on the signs, meditating on the (concentration) object.
narrative_pali: Ye jhānapasutā dhīrā, nekkhammūpasame ratā, devā pi tesaṁ pihayanti, Sambuddhānaṁ satīmataṁ.
narrative_english: Those wise ones intent on meditation, who love the peace of renunciation, even the gods are envious of them, the Sambuddhas, the ones who are mindful.

pali_mahasangiti: Kiccho manussapaṭilābho, kicchaṁ maccāna jīvitaṁ; Kicchaṁ saddhammassavanaṁ, kiccho buddhānamuppādo.
english_sujato: It’s hard to gain a human birth; the life of mortals is hard; it’s hard to hear the true teaching; the arising of Buddhas is hard.
interlinear_pali: Kiccho manussapaṭilābho, kicchaṁ maccāna’ jīvitaṁ, kicchaṁ Saddhammasavanaṁ, kiccho Buddhānam-uppādo.
interlinear_english: It is rare to acquire (birth as a) human, rare is the life of mortals, it is rare to hear the True Dhamma, rare the arising of Buddhas.
narrative_pali: Kiccho manussapaṭilābho, kicchaṁ maccāna’ jīvitaṁ, kicchaṁ Saddhammasavanaṁ, kiccho Buddhānam-uppādo.
narrative_english: It is rare to be born human, rare is the life of the mortals, it is rare to hear True Dhamma, rare the arising of Buddhas.

pali_mahasangiti: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā; Sacittapariyodapanaṁ, etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.
english_sujato: Not to do any evil; to embrace the good; to purify one’s mind: this is the instruction of the Buddhas.
interlinear_pali: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā, sacittapariyodapanaṁ - etaṁ Buddhāna’ sāsanaṁ.
interlinear_english: The non-doing of anything wicked, undertaking of what is good, the purification of one’s mind - this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
narrative_pali: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā, sacittapariyodapanaṁ - etaṁ Buddhāna’ sāsanaṁ.
narrative_english: Not doing anything wicked undertaking of what is good, purification of one’s mind is the teaching of the Buddhas.

pali_mahasangiti: Khantī paramaṁ tapo titikkhā, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ vadanti buddhā; Na hi pabbajito parūpaghātī, Na samaṇo hoti paraṁ viheṭhayanto.
english_sujato: Patient acceptance is the ultimate fervor. Extinguishment is the ultimate, say the Buddhas. No true renunciate injures another, nor does an ascetic hurt another.
interlinear_pali: Khantī paramaṁ tapo titikkhā, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ vadanti Buddhā, na hi pabbajito parūpaghātī, samaṇo hoti paraṁ viheṭhayanto.
interlinear_english: Enduring patience is the supreme austerity, Nibbāna is supreme say the Buddhas, for one gone forth does not hurt another, (nor does) an ascetic harass another.

pali_mahasangiti: Anūpavādo anūpaghāto, Pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro; Mattaññutā ca bhattasmiṁ, Pantañca sayanāsanaṁ; Adhicitte ca āyogo, Etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.
english_sujato: Not speaking ill nor doing harm; restraint in the monastic code; moderation in eating; staying in remote lodgings; commitment to the higher mind— this is the instruction of the Buddhas.
interlinear_pali: Anupavādo anupaghāto, pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro, mattaññutā ca bhattasmiṁ, pantañ-ca sayanāsanaṁ, adhicitte ca āyogo - etaṁ Buddhāna’ sāsanaṁ.
interlinear_english: Not finding fault, not hurting, restraint by the regulations, knowing the right measure of food, (living in) a remote dwelling, devotion to meditation - this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

pali_mahasangiti: Na kahāpaṇavassena, titti kāmesu vijjati; Appassādā dukhā kāmā, iti viññāya paṇḍito.
english_sujato: Even if it were raining money, you’d not be sated in sensual pleasures. An astute person understands that sensual pleasures offer little gratification and much suffering.
interlinear_pali: Na kahāpaṇavassena titti kāmesu vijjati, “Appassādā dukhā kāmā,” iti viññāya paṇḍito,
interlinear_english: Not through a rain of coins is satisfaction found for sense desires, the wise one knowing: “Sense pleasures have little joy, (much) suffering,”

pali_mahasangiti: Api dibbesu kāmesu, ratiṁ so nādhigacchati; Taṇhakkhayarato hoti, sammāsambuddhasāvako.
english_sujato: Thus they find no delight even in celestial pleasures. A disciple of the fully awakened Buddha delights in the ending of craving.
interlinear_pali: api dibbesu kāmesu ratiṁ so nādhigacchati. Taṇhakkhayarato hoti Sammāsambuddhasāvako.
interlinear_english: does not find delight even in heavenly pleasures. The disciple of the Perfect Sambuddha delights in craving’s destruction.

pali_mahasangiti: Bahuṁ ve saraṇaṁ yanti, pabbatāni vanāni ca; Ārāmarukkhacetyāni, manussā bhayatajjitā.
english_sujato: So many go for refuge to mountains and forest groves, to shrines in tended parks; those people are driven by fear.
interlinear_pali: Bahuṁ ve saraṇaṁ yanti pabbatāni vanāni ca ārāmarukkhacetyāni, manussā bhayatajjitā.
interlinear_english: * Many people shaken by fear go for refuge to woods and mountains, to tree shrines in pleasure parks.
narrative_pali: Bahuṁ ve saraṇaṁ yanti pabbatāni vanāni ca ārāmarukkhacetyāni, manussā bhayatajjitā.
narrative_english: Many people shaken by fear go for refuge to woods, mountains, and to tree shrines in pleasure parks.

pali_mahasangiti: Netaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ, netaṁ saraṇamuttamaṁ; Netaṁ saraṇamāgamma, sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
english_sujato: But such refuge is no sanctuary, it is no supreme refuge. By going to that refuge, you’re not released from all suffering.
interlinear_pali: Netaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ, netaṁ saraṇam-uttamaṁ, netaṁ saraṇam-āgamma sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
interlinear_english: That is not a secure refuge, that is not the refuge supreme, that is not the refuge to come to that liberates from all suffering.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca buddhañca dhammañca, saṅghañca saraṇaṁ gato; Cattāri ariyasaccāni, sammappaññāya passati.
english_sujato: One gone for refuge to the Buddha, to his teaching and to the Saṅgha, sees the four noble truths with right understanding:
interlinear_pali: Yo ca Buddhañ-ca Dhammañ-ca Saṅghañ-ca saraṇaṁ gato, cattāri ariyasaccāni sammappaññāya passati:
interlinear_english: Whoever has gone refuge to the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Saṅgha, and who sees with right wisdom the four noble truths:

pali_mahasangiti: Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ, dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ; Ariyaṁ caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ, dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.
english_sujato: suffering, suffering’s origin, suffering’s transcendence, and the noble eightfold path that leads to the stilling of suffering.
interlinear_pali: Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ, ariyañ-caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.
interlinear_english: Suffering, arising of suffering, and the overcoming of suffering, the eightfold noble path leading to the stilling of suffering.

pali_mahasangiti: Etaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ, etaṁ saraṇamuttamaṁ; Etaṁ saraṇamāgamma, sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
english_sujato: Such refuge is a sanctuary, it is the supreme refuge. By going to that refuge, you’re released from all suffering.
interlinear_pali: Etaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ, etaṁ saraṇam-uttamaṁ, etaṁ saraṇam-āgamma sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
interlinear_english: That is a secure refuge, that is the refuge supreme, that is the refuge to come to that liberates from all suffering.

pali_mahasangiti: Dullabho purisājañño, na so sabbattha jāyati; Yattha so jāyati dhīro, taṁ kulaṁ sukhamedhati.
english_sujato: It’s hard to find a thoroughbred man: they’re not born just anywhere. A family where that attentive one is born prospers in happiness.
interlinear_pali: Dullabho purisājañño, na so sabbattha jāyati, yattha so jāyate dhīro, taṁ kulaṁ sukham-edhati.
interlinear_english: A person of good breed is rare, that one is not born everywhere, wherever that wise one is born, that family gains happiness.
narrative_pali: Dullabho purisājañño, na so sabbattha jāyati,
narrative_english: yattha so jāyate dhīro, taṁ kulaṁ sukham-edhati. A person of good breed is rare, that one is not born in all places, wherever that wise one is born, that family gains happiness.

pali_mahasangiti: Sukho buddhānamuppādo, sukhā saddhammadesanā; Sukhā saṅghassa sāmaggī, samaggānaṁ tapo sukho.
english_sujato: Happy, the arising of Buddhas! Happy, the teaching of Dhamma! Happy is the harmony of the Saṅgha, and the striving of the harmonious is happy.
interlinear_pali: Sukho Buddhānam-uppādo, sukhā Saddhammadesanā, sukhā Saṅghassa sāmaggī, samaggānaṁ tapo sukho.
interlinear_english: The arising of the Buddhas is good, the teaching of the True Dhamma is good, the harmony of the Saṅgha is good, devotion to harmony is good.

pali_mahasangiti: Pūjārahe pūjayato, buddhe yadi va sāvake; Papañcasamatikkante, tiṇṇasokapariddave.
english_sujato: When a person venerates the worthy— the Buddha or his disciple, who have transcended proliferation, and have left behind grief and lamentation,
interlinear_pali: Pūjārahe pūjayato, Buddhe yadi va sāvake, papañcasamatikkante, tiṇṇasokapariddave;
interlinear_english: For those who worship those worthy of worship, whether Buddhas or disciples, who have overcome the impediments, crossed over grief and lamentation;

pali_mahasangiti: Te tādise pūjayato, nibbute akutobhaye; Na sakkā puññaṁ saṅkhātuṁ, imettamapi kenaci.
english_sujato: quenched, fearing nothing from any quarter— the merit of one venerating such as these, cannot be calculated by anyone, saying it is just this much.
interlinear_pali: te tādise pūjayato, nibbute akutobhaye, na sakkā puññaṁ saṅkhātuṁ, imettam-api kenaci.
interlinear_english: for those who worship such as these, the emancipated, the fearless, no one is able to measure their (vast) merit, (saying:) it is as much as this.

pali_mahasangiti: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma, verinesu averino; Verinesu manussesu, viharāma averino.
english_sujato: Let us live so very happily, loving among the hostile. Among hostile humans, let us live with love.
interlinear_pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma verinesu averino, verinesu manussesu viharāma averino.
interlinear_english: Let us live truly happily, without hatred, amongst those who have hatred, amongst humans who have hatred let us live without hatred.

pali_mahasangiti: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma, āturesu anāturā; Āturesu manussesu, viharāma anāturā.
english_sujato: Let us live so very happily, healthy among the ailing. Among ailing humans let us live healthily.
interlinear_pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma āturesu anāturā, āturesu manussesu viharāma anāturā.
interlinear_english: Let us live truly happily, without sickness, amongst those who are sick, amongst humans who have sickness let us live without sickness.
interlinear_notes: Comm: kilesāturesu; amongst those who are sick with defilements.
narrative_pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma āturesu anāturā, āturesu manussesu viharāma anāturā.
narrative_english: Let us live on without sickness, amongst those who do have sickness, amongst humans who have sickness

pali_mahasangiti: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma, ussukesu anussukā; Ussukesu manussesu, viharāma anussukā.
english_sujato: Let us live so very happily, content among the greedy. Among greedy humans, let us live content.
interlinear_pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma ussukesu anussukā ussukesu manussesu viharāma anussukā.
interlinear_english: Let us live truly happily, without longing, amongst those who are longing, amongst humans who are longing let us live without longing.
interlinear_notes: Comm: pañcakāmaguṇapariyesane; seeking the five strands of sense pleasure.

pali_mahasangiti: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma, yesaṁ no natthi kiñcanaṁ; Pītibhakkhā bhavissāma, devā ābhassarā yathā.
english_sujato: Let us live so very happily, we who have nothing. We shall feed on rapture, like the gods of streaming radiance.
interlinear_pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma yesaṁ no natthi kiñcanaṁ, pītibhakkhā bhavissāma devā Ābhassarā yathā.
interlinear_english: We live truly happily enough having no possessions ourselves, we will feed on joy like the gods of Streaming Light.
interlinear_notes: Comm: rāgādīsu kiñcanesu; with no possessions like passion and so forth.
The Ābhassara devas are traditionally positioned at the seventeenth level of existence, at the top of the three levels said to correspond to the second absorption.
narrative_pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma yesaṁ no natthi kiñcanaṁ, pītibhakkhā bhavissāma devā Ābhassarā yathā.
narrative_english: We can live happily enough having no possessions ourselves, we will feed on joy like the gods of Streaming Light.

pali_mahasangiti: Jayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, dukkhaṁ seti parājito; Upasanto sukhaṁ seti, hitvā jayaparājayaṁ.
english_sujato: Victory breeds enmity; the defeated sleep badly. The peaceful sleep at ease, having left victory and defeat behind.
interlinear_pali: Jayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, dukkhaṁ seti parājito, upasanto sukhaṁ seti, hitvā jayaparājayaṁ.
interlinear_english: The victor generates hatred, the defeated one finds suffering, the one at peace lives happily, having abandoned victory and defeat.
narrative_pali: Jayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, dukkhaṁ seti parājito, upasanto sukhaṁ seti, hitvā jayaparājayaṁ.
narrative_english: The victor generates hatred, the defeated finds suffering, the one at peace lives happily, without victory and defeat.

pali_mahasangiti: Natthi rāgasamo aggi, Natthi dosasamo kali; Natthi khandhasamā dukkhā, Natthi santiparaṁ sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: There is no fire like greed, no crime like hate, no suffering like the aggregates, no bliss beyond peace.
interlinear_pali: Natthi rāgasamo aggi, natthi dosasamo kali, natthi khandhasamā dukkhā, natthi santiparaṁ sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: There is no fire like passion, there is no offence like hatred, there is no suffering like the components (of mind and body), no happiness other than peace.
interlinear_notes: Comm: nibbānato uttariṁ; beyond Nibbāna.

pali_mahasangiti: Jighacchāparamā rogā, saṅkhāraparamā dukhā; Etaṁ ñatvā yathābhūtaṁ, nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: Hunger is the worst illness, conditions are the worst suffering. When one has known this as it is, extinguishment is the ultimate happiness.
interlinear_pali: Jighacchā paramā rogā, saṅkhāraparamā dukhā, etaṁ ñatvā yathābhūtaṁ, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: Hunger is the supreme sickness, conditions are the supreme suffering, knowing this as it really is, (know) Nibbāna is the supreme good.
narrative_pali: Jighacchā paramā rogā, saṅkhāraparamā dukhā, etaṁ ñatvā yathābhūtaṁ, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.
narrative_english: Hunger is the supreme sickness, conditions the supreme suffering, knowing this as it really is, Nibbāna is the supreme good.

pali_mahasangiti: Ārogyaparamā lābhā, Santuṭṭhiparamaṁ dhanaṁ; Vissāsaparamā ñāti, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: Health is the ultimate blessing; contentment, the ultimate wealth; trust is the ultimate family; extinguishment, the ultimate happiness.
interlinear_pali: Ārogyaparamā lābhā, santuṭṭhi paramaṁ dhanaṁ, vissāsā paramā ñāti, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: Health is the supreme gain, content the supreme wealth, confidence the supreme kin, Nibbāna the supreme good.
narrative_pali: Ārogyaparamā lābhā, santuṭṭhi paramaṁ dhanaṁ, vissāsā paramā ñāti, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.
narrative_english: Health is the supreme gain, content the supreme wealth, faith is the supreme kin,

pali_mahasangiti: Pavivekarasaṁ pitvā, rasaṁ upasamassa ca; Niddaro hoti nippāpo, dhammapītirasaṁ pivaṁ.
english_sujato: Having drunk the nectar of seclusion and the nectar of peace— free of stress, free of evil, drink the joyous nectar of truth.
interlinear_pali: Pavivekarasaṁ pitvā, rasaṁ upasamassa ca, niddaro hoti nippāpo, Dhammapītirasaṁ pivaṁ.
interlinear_english: Savouring the taste of solitude, and the taste of peace, he is fearless, faultless, savouring the joyful taste of Dhamma.

pali_mahasangiti: Sāhu dassanamariyānaṁ, sannivāso sadā sukho; Adassanena bālānaṁ, niccameva sukhī siyā.
english_sujato: It’s good to see the noble ones, staying with them is always good. Were you not to see fools, you’d always be happy.
interlinear_pali: Sāhu dassanam-ariyānaṁ, sannivāso sadā sukho, adassanena bālānaṁ niccam-eva sukhī siyā.
interlinear_english: Meeting with the noble is good, living together (with them) is always pleasant, through not meeting foolish people one will constantly be happy.
