interlinear_notes: Dassana normally means seeing, but in the application here and below must mean meeting with. See also the usage in 210 below.
narrative_pali: Sāhu dassanam-ariyānaṁ, sannivāso sadā sukho, adassanena bālānaṁ niccam-eva sukhī siyā.
narrative_english: Meeting with the noble ones is good, living together is pleasant, through not meeting foolish people one will constantly be happy.

pali_mahasangiti: Bālasaṅgatacārī hi, dīghamaddhāna socati; Dukkho bālehi saṁvāso, amitteneva sabbadā; Dhīro ca sukhasaṁvāso, ñātīnaṁva samāgamo.
english_sujato: For one who consorts with fools grieves long. Painful is living with fools, like being stuck with your enemy. Happy is living with an attentive one, like meeting with your kin.
interlinear_pali: Bālasaṅgatacārī hi dīgham-addhāna’ socati, dukkho bālehi saṁvāso amitteneva sabbadā, dhīro ca sukhasaṁvāso ñātīnaṁ va samāgamo.
interlinear_english: For he who consorts with fools grieves for a long time, dwelling with fools is always suffering as it is with enemies, the wise one dwells happily as with an assembly of kin.

pali_mahasangiti: Tasmā hi— Dhīrañca paññañca bahussutañca, Dhorayhasīlaṁ vatavantamariyaṁ; Taṁ tādisaṁ sappurisaṁ sumedhaṁ, Bhajetha nakkhattapathaṁva candimā.
english_sujato: Therefore: An attentive one, wise and learned, a behemoth of virtue, true to their vows, noble: follow a true and intelligent person such as this, as the moon tracks the path of the stars.
interlinear_pali: tasmā hi, dhīrañ-ca paññañ-ca bahussutañ-ca, dhorayhasīlaṁ vatavantam-ariyaṁ – taṁ tādisaṁ sappurisaṁ sumedhaṁ bhajetha nakkhattapathaṁ va candimā.
interlinear_english: therefore, the firm, the wise and the learned, the virtuous, dutiful and noble – * (accompany) such a true and intelligent person as the moon accompanies the course of the stars.

pali_mahasangiti: Ayoge yuñjamattānaṁ, yogasmiñca ayojayaṁ; Atthaṁ hitvā piyaggāhī, pihetattānuyoginaṁ.
english_sujato: Applying yourself where you ought not, neglecting what you should be doing, forgetting your goal, you cling to what you hold dear, jealous of those devoted to their heart’s goal.
interlinear_pali: Ayoge yuñjam-attānaṁ, yogasmiñ-ca ayojayaṁ, atthaṁ hitvā piyaggāhī, pihetattānuyoginaṁ.
interlinear_english: Engaging oneself in what is not suitable, not engaging in what is suitable, abandoning the good, grasping the loved, he envies the one who endeavours for himself.
narrative_pali: Ayoge yuñjam-attānaṁ, yogasmiñ-ca ayojayaṁ, atthaṁ hitvā piyaggāhī, pihetattānuyoginaṁ.
narrative_english: Engaging in what is not suitable, not engaging in what is suitable, abandoning the good, grasping the loved, he envies the person who endeavours.

pali_mahasangiti: Mā piyehi samāgañchi, appiyehi kudācanaṁ; Piyānaṁ adassanaṁ dukkhaṁ, appiyānañca dassanaṁ.
english_sujato: Don’t ever get too close to those you like or dislike. For not seeing the liked is suffering, and so is seeing the disliked.
interlinear_pali: Mā piyehi samāgañchī appiyehi kudācanaṁ, piyānaṁ adassanaṁ dukkhaṁ, appiyānañ-ca dassanaṁ.
interlinear_english: Do not associate at any time with those who are loved or with those unloved, there is suffering not meeting those loved, and (suffering from) meeting those unloved.

pali_mahasangiti: Tasmā piyaṁ na kayirātha, piyāpāyo hi pāpako; Ganthā tesaṁ na vijjanti, yesaṁ natthi piyāppiyaṁ.
english_sujato: Therefore don’t hold anything dear, for it’s bad to lose those you love. No ties are found in they who hold nothing loved or loathed.
interlinear_pali: Tasmā piyaṁ na kayirātha, piyāpāyo hi pāpako. Ganthā tesaṁ na vijjanti yesaṁ natthi piyāppiyaṁ.
interlinear_english: Therefore do not hold (anything) as loved, for losing those who are loved is loathsome. There are no knots for those who hold nothing as loved or as unloved.

pali_mahasangiti: Piyato jāyatī soko, piyato jāyatī bhayaṁ; Piyato vippamuttassa, natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.
english_sujato: Sorrow springs from what we hold dear, fear springs from what we hold dear; one free from holding anything dear has no sorrow, let alone fear.
interlinear_pali: Piyato jāyatī soko, piyato jāyatī bhayaṁ, piyato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
interlinear_english: From love there arises grief, from love there arises fear, for one who is free from love there is no grief, how is there fear?
narrative_pali: Piyato jāyatī soko, piyato jāyatī bhayaṁ, piyato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
narrative_english: From loving there arises grief, from loving there arises fear, for one who is free from loving there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali_mahasangiti: Pemato jāyatī soko, pemato jāyatī bhayaṁ; Pemato vippamuttassa, natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.
english_sujato: Sorrow springs from attachment, fear springs from attachment; one free from attachment has no sorrow, let alone fear.
interlinear_pali: Pemato jāyatī soko, pemato jāyatī bhayaṁ, pemato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
interlinear_english: From fondness there arises grief, from fondness there arises fear, for one who is free from fondness there is no grief, how is there fear?
narrative_pali: Pemato jāyatī soko, pemato jāyatī bhayaṁ, pemato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
narrative_english: From fondness there arises grief, from fondness there arises fear, for one who is free from fondness there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali_mahasangiti: Ratiyā jāyatī soko, ratiyā jāyatī bhayaṁ; Ratiyā vippamuttassa, natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.
english_sujato: Sorrow springs from relishing, fear springs from relishing; one free from relishing has no sorrow, let alone fear.
interlinear_pali: Ratiyā jāyatī soko, ratiyā jāyatī bhayaṁ, ratiyā vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
interlinear_english: From delight there arises grief, from delight there arises fear, for one who is free from delight there is no grief, how is there fear?
narrative_pali: Ratiyā jāyatī soko, ratiyā jāyatī bhayaṁ, ratiyā vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
narrative_english: From delight there arises grief, from delight there arises fear, for one who is free from delight there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali_mahasangiti: Kāmato jāyatī soko, kāmato jāyatī bhayaṁ; Kāmato vippamuttassa, natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.
english_sujato: Sorrow springs from desire, fear springs from desire; one free from desire has no sorrow, let alone fear.
interlinear_pali: Kāmato jāyatī soko, kāmato jāyatī bhayaṁ, kāmato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
interlinear_english: From desire there arises grief, from desire there arises fear, for one who is free from desire there is no grief, how is there fear?
narrative_pali: Kāmato jāyatī soko, kāmato jāyatī bhayaṁ, kāmato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
narrative_english: From desire there arises grief, from desire there arises fear, for one who is free from desire there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali_mahasangiti: Taṇhāya jāyatī soko, taṇhāya jāyatī bhayaṁ; Taṇhāya vippamuttassa, natthi soko kuto bhayaṁ.
english_sujato: Sorrow springs from craving, fear springs from craving; one free from craving has no sorrow, let alone fear.
interlinear_pali: Taṇhāya jāyatī soko, taṇhāya jāyatī bhayaṁ, taṇhāya vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
interlinear_english: From craving there arises grief, from craving there arises fear, for one who is free from craving there is no grief, how is there fear?
narrative_pali: Taṇhāya jāyatī soko, taṇhāya jāyatī bhayaṁ, taṇhāya vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
narrative_english: From craving there arises grief, from craving there arises fear,

pali_mahasangiti: Sīladassanasampannaṁ, dhammaṭṭhaṁ saccavedinaṁ; Attano kamma kubbānaṁ, taṁ jano kurute piyaṁ.
english_sujato: One accomplished in virtue and vision, firmly principled, and truthful, doing oneself what ought be done: that’s who the people love.
interlinear_pali: Sīladassanasampannaṁ, dhammaṭṭhaṁ saccavedinaṁ, attano kamma’ kubbānaṁ, taṁ jano kurute piyaṁ.
interlinear_english: Endowed with virtue and insight, principled, knowing the truths, doing the deeds that are his own, that one the people love.
interlinear_notes: Comm: tisso sikkhā tā pūrayamānan-ti attho; the meaning is fulfilling the three trainings (in higher virtue, concentration and wisdom).
narrative_pali: Sīladassanasampannaṁ, dhammaṭṭhaṁ saccavedinaṁ, attano kamma’ kubbānaṁ, taṁ jano kurute piyaṁ.
narrative_english: Endowed with virtue and insight, principled and knowing the truths, doing the deeds that are his own, that one the people truly love.

pali_mahasangiti: Chandajāto anakkhāte, Manasā ca phuṭo siyā; Kāmesu ca appaṭibaddhacitto, Uddhaṁsototi vuccati.
english_sujato: One eager to realize the ineffable would be filled with awareness. Their mind not bound to pleasures of sense, they’re said to be heading upstream.
interlinear_pali: Chandajāto anakkhāte, manasā ca phuṭo siyā, kāmesu ca appaṭibaddhacitto, ‘uddhaṁsoto’ ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: The one with desire arisen for the undeclared, will be suffused with the (awakening) mind, with a mind unconnected with sense pleasures, he is spoken of as ‘one gone upstream’.
interlinear_notes: I.e. for Nibbāna.
Comm: heṭṭhimehi tīhi maggaphalacittehi phuṭo pūrito bhaveyya; will be filled and suffused with the three lower paths and fruits.
narrative_pali: Chandajāto anakkhāte, manasā ca phuṭo siyā, kāmesu ca appaṭibaddhacitto: ‘uddhaṁsoto’ ti vuccati.
narrative_english: The one with desire for the undeclared, will be suffused with the awak’ning mind, with a mind unconnected with pleasures, he is spoken of as ‘one gone upstream.’

pali_mahasangiti: Cirappavāsiṁ purisaṁ, dūrato sotthimāgataṁ; Ñātimittā suhajjā ca, abhinandanti āgataṁ.
english_sujato: When a man returns safely after a long time spent abroad, family, friends, and loved ones celebrate his return.
interlinear_pali: Cirappavāsiṁ purisaṁ dūrato sotthim-āgataṁ, ñātimittā suhajjā ca abhinandanti āgataṁ.
interlinear_english: When one who lives abroad for a long time comes safely from afar, his relatives, friends and companions come and greatly rejoice.
narrative_pali: Cirappavāsiṁ purisaṁ dūrato sotthim-āgataṁ, ñātimittā suhajjā ca abhinandanti āgataṁ.
narrative_english: When one who lives abroad for a long time comes safely from afar, relatives and companions come and greatly rejoice.

pali_mahasangiti: Tatheva katapuññampi, asmā lokā paraṁ gataṁ; Puññāni paṭigaṇhanti, piyaṁ ñātīva āgataṁ.
english_sujato: Just so, when one who has done good goes from this world to the next, their good deeds receive them there, as family welcomes home one they love.
interlinear_pali: Tatheva katapuññam-pi asmā lokā paraṁ gataṁ, puññāni paṭigaṇhanti piyaṁ ñātīva āgataṁ.
interlinear_english: Just so, when one who has performed merit goes from this world unto the next, his merits are received just as relatives come to their loved one.

pali_mahasangiti: Kodhaṁ jahe vippajaheyya mānaṁ, Saṁyojanaṁ sabbamatikkameyya; Taṁ nāmarūpasmimasajjamānaṁ, Akiñcanaṁ nānupatanti dukkhā.
english_sujato: Give up anger, get rid of conceit, and escape every fetter. Sufferings don’t befall one who has nothing, not clinging to name and form.
interlinear_pali: Kodhaṁ jahe, vippajaheyya mānaṁ, saṁyojanaṁ sabbam-atikkameyya, taṁ nāmarūpasmiṁ asajjamānaṁ, akiñcanaṁ nānupatanti dukkhā.
interlinear_english: One should abandon anger, one should abandon conceit, one should overcome every fetter, without clinging to mind and bodily form, sufferings never do befall the one having no possessions.
interlinear_notes: Comm: rāgādīnaṃ abhāvena akiñcanaṁ; not developing possessions like passion and so on.
narrative_pali: Kodhaṁ jahe, vippajaheyya mānaṁ, saṁyojanaṁ sabbam-atikkameyya, taṁ nāmarūpasmiṁ asajjamānaṁ, akiñcanaṁ nānupatanti dukkhā.
narrative_english: One should abandon all anger, one should abandon all conceit, one should overcome every fetter, without clinging to mind and form, sufferings never do befall the one having no possessions.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo ve uppatitaṁ kodhaṁ, rathaṁ bhantaṁva vāraye; Tamahaṁ sārathiṁ brūmi, rasmiggāho itaro jano.
english_sujato: When anger surges like a lurching chariot, keep it in check. That’s what I call a charioteer; others just hold the reins.
interlinear_pali: Yo ve uppatitaṁ kodhaṁ rathaṁ bhantaṁ va dhāraye, tam-ahaṁ sārathiṁ brūmi rasmiggāho itaro jano.
interlinear_english: Whoever should hold back arisen anger just like a swerving chariot, that one I say is a charioteer, other people are just rein-holders.
narrative_pali: Yo ve uppatitaṁ kodhaṁ rathaṁ bhantaṁ va dhāraye, tam-ahaṁ sārathiṁ brūmi rasmiggāho itaro jano. Whoever should hold back anger
narrative_english: just like a swerving chariot, that one is a charioteer,

pali_mahasangiti: Akkodhena jine kodhaṁ, asādhuṁ sādhunā jine; Jine kadariyaṁ dānena, saccenālikavādinaṁ.
english_sujato: Defeat anger with kindness, villainy with virtue, stinginess with giving, and lies with truth.
interlinear_pali: Akkodhena jine kodhaṁ, asādhuṁ sādhunā jine, jine kadariyaṁ dānena, saccenālikavādinaṁ.
interlinear_english: Through kindness one should overcome anger, through goodness one should overcome a lack of goodness, through gifts one should overcome stinginess, through truth (one should overcome) lying speech.
interlinear_notes: Literally: through non-anger.
narrative_pali: Akkodhena jine kodhaṁ, asādhuṁ sādhunā jine, jine kadariyaṁ dānena, saccenālikavādinaṁ.
narrative_english: Through kindness one should overcome anger, through goodness overcome lack of goodness, through gifts one should overcome stinginess, through truth one should overcome lying speech.

pali_mahasangiti: Saccaṁ bhaṇe na kujjheyya, dajjā appampi yācito; Etehi tīhi ṭhānehi, gacche devāna santike.
english_sujato: Speak the truth, do not be angry, and give when asked, if only a little. By these three means, you may enter the presence of the gods.
interlinear_pali: Saccaṁ bhaṇe, na kujjheyya, dajjāppasmim-pi yācito, etehi tīhi ṭhānehi gacche devāna’ santike.
interlinear_english: One should speak out the truth, one should not get angry, when requested give, if only a little, through these three conditions one can go to the presence of the gods.

pali_mahasangiti: Ahiṁsakā ye munayo, niccaṁ kāyena saṁvutā; Te yanti accutaṁ ṭhānaṁ, yattha gantvā na socare.
english_sujato: Those harmless sages, always restrained in body, go to the state that does not pass, where there is no sorrow.
interlinear_pali: Ahiṁsakā ye munayo, niccaṁ kāyena saṁvutā, te yanti accutaṁ ṭhānaṁ, yattha gantvā na socare.
interlinear_english: Those sages without violence, constantly restrained in body, go to the deathless (Nibbāna), having gone there they do not grieve.
narrative_pali: Ahiṁsakā ye munayo, niccaṁ kāyena saṁvutā, te yanti accutaṁ ṭhānaṁ, yattha gantvā na socare.

pali_mahasangiti: Sadā jāgaramānānaṁ, ahorattānusikkhinaṁ; Nibbānaṁ adhimuttānaṁ, atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.
english_sujato: Always wakeful, practicing night and day, focused only on extinguishment, their defilements come to an end.
interlinear_pali: Sadā jāgaramānānaṁ, ahorattānusikkhinaṁ, Nibbānaṁ adhimuttānaṁ, atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.
interlinear_english: For those who are always wakeful, who train both by day and by night, who are intent on Nibbāna, the pollutants are laid to rest.
narrative_pali: Sadā jāgaramānānaṁ, ahorattānusikkhinaṁ, Nibbānaṁ adhimuttānaṁ, atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.
narrative_english: For those who are always wakeful, who train both by day and by night, who are intent on Nibbāna, the pollutants are laid to rest.

pali_mahasangiti: Porāṇametaṁ atula, netaṁ ajjatanāmiva; Nindanti tuṇhimāsīnaṁ, nindanti bahubhāṇinaṁ; Mitabhāṇimpi nindanti, natthi loke anindito.
english_sujato: It’s always been this way, Atula, it’s not just today. They blame you when you’re silent, they blame you when you speak a lot, and even when you speak just right: no one in the world escapes blame.
interlinear_pali: Porāṇam-etaṁ, Atula, netaṁ ajjatanām-iva: nindanti tuṇhim-āsīnaṁ, nindanti bahubhāṇinaṁ, mitabhāṇim-pi nindanti, natthi loke anindito.
interlinear_english: This is something of old, Atula, this is not something of today: they blame the one who sits silently, they blame the one who talks a lot, they blame the one who talks in moderation, there is no one in the world not blamed.
narrative_pali: Porāṇam-etaṁ, Atula, netaṁ ajjatanām-iva: nindanti tuṇhim-āsīnaṁ, nindanti bahubhāṇinaṁ, mitabhāṇim-pi nindanti, natthi loke anindito.
narrative_english: This is something of old, Atula, this is not something of today: they blame the one who sits silent, they blame the one who talks a lot, and one who talks moderately, there is no one who is not blamed.

pali_mahasangiti: Na cāhu na ca bhavissati, na cetarahi vijjati; Ekantaṁ nindito poso, ekantaṁ vā pasaṁsito.
english_sujato: There never was, nor will be, nor is there today, someone who is wholly praised or wholly blamed.
interlinear_pali: Na cāhu na ca bhavissati, na cetarahi vijjati ekantaṁ nindito poso, ekantaṁ vā pasaṁsito.
interlinear_english: There was not and there will not be, and at present there is not found a person totally blameworthy, or one totally praiseworthy.

pali_mahasangiti: Yañce viññū pasaṁsanti, anuvicca suve suve; Acchiddavuttiṁ medhāviṁ, paññāsīlasamāhitaṁ.
english_sujato: If, after watching them day in day out, discerning people praise that sage of impeccable conduct, endowed with ethics and wisdom;
interlinear_pali: Yañ-ce viññū pasaṁsanti, anuvicca suve suve, acchiddavuttiṁ medhāviṁ, paññāsīlasamāhitaṁ,
interlinear_english: The one who, after being examined day by day, is praised by the wise, faultless in conduct, sagacious, attending to virtue and wisdom,

pali_mahasangiti: Nikkhaṁ jambonadasseva, ko taṁ ninditumarahati; Devāpi naṁ pasaṁsanti, brahmunāpi pasaṁsito.
english_sujato: like a pendant of Black Plum River gold, who is worthy to criticize them? Even the gods praise them, and by the Divinity, too, they’re praised.
interlinear_pali: nekkhaṁ jambonadasseva, ko taṁ ninditum-arahati? Devā pi naṁ pasaṁsanti, Brahmunā pi pasaṁsito.
interlinear_english: one who is like a golden coin, who is there worthy to blame him? That one is praised by the gods, and has been praised by the Brahmās too.

pali_mahasangiti: Kāyappakopaṁ rakkheyya, kāyena saṁvuto siyā; Kāyaduccaritaṁ hitvā, kāyena sucaritaṁ care.
english_sujato: Guard against ill-tempered deeds, be restrained in body. Giving up bad bodily conduct, conduct yourself well in body.
interlinear_pali: Kāyappakopaṁ rakkheyya, kāyena saṁvuto siyā, kāyaduccaritaṁ hitvā, kāyena sucaritaṁ care.
interlinear_english: One should guard against bodily anger, one should be restrained bodily, abandoning wrong bodily conduct, one should have good bodily conduct.
narrative_pali: Kāyappakopaṁ rakkheyya, kāyena saṁvuto siyā, kāyaduccaritaṁ hitvā, kāyena sucaritaṁ care.
narrative_english: One should guard one’s bodily anger, one should be restrained bodily,

pali_mahasangiti: Vacīpakopaṁ rakkheyya, vācāya saṁvuto siyā; Vacīduccaritaṁ hitvā, vācāya sucaritaṁ care.
english_sujato: Guard against ill-tempered words, be restrained in speech. Giving up bad verbal conduct, conduct yourself well in speech.
interlinear_pali: Vacīpakopaṁ rakkheyya, vācāya saṁvuto siyā, vacīduccaritaṁ hitvā, vācāya sucaritaṁ care.
interlinear_english: One should guard against verbal anger, one should be restrained verbally, abandoning wrong verbal conduct, one should have good verbal conduct.

pali_mahasangiti: Manopakopaṁ rakkheyya, manasā saṁvuto siyā; Manoduccaritaṁ hitvā, manasā sucaritaṁ care.
english_sujato: Guard against ill-tempered thoughts, be restrained in mind. Giving up bad mental conduct, conduct yourself well in mind.
interlinear_pali: Manopakopaṁ rakkheyya, manasā saṁvuto siyā, manoduccaritaṁ hitvā, manasā sucaritaṁ care.
interlinear_english: One should guard against mental anger, one should be restrained mentally, abandoning wrong mental conduct, one should have good mental conduct.

pali_mahasangiti: Kāyena saṁvutā dhīrā, atho vācāya saṁvutā; Manasā saṁvutā dhīrā, te ve suparisaṁvutā.
english_sujato: An attentive one is restrained in body restrained also in speech, in thought, too, they are restrained: they are restrained in every way.
interlinear_pali: Kāyena saṁvutā dhīrā, atho vācāya saṁvutā, manasā saṁvutā dhīrā, te ve suparisaṁvutā.
interlinear_english: The wise are restrained bodily, then they are restrained verbally, the wise are restrained mentally, they are indeed very well-restrained.

pali_mahasangiti: Paṇḍupalāsova dānisi, Yamapurisāpi ca te upaṭṭhitā; Uyyogamukhe ca tiṭṭhasi, Pātheyyampi ca te na vijjati.
english_sujato: Today you’re like a withered leaf, Yama’s men await you. You stand at the departure gates, yet you have no supplies for the road.
interlinear_pali: Paṇḍupalāso va dāni ’si, Yamapurisā pi ca taṁ upaṭṭhitā, uyyogamukhe ca tiṭṭhasi, pātheyyam-pi ca te na vijjati.
interlinear_english: You are now like a withered leaf, Yama’s men stand waiting for you, you stand at decay’s door, with no provisions for the journey found.
interlinear_notes: Yama is the god of death in traditional Indian lore, his men escort one to the other world.
Comm: kusalapātheyyaṁ; provisions of wholesome deeds.
narrative_pali: Paṇḍupalāso va dāni ’si, Yamapurisā pi ca taṁ upaṭṭhitā, uyyogamukhe ca tiṭṭhasi, pātheyyam-pi ca te na vijjati.
narrative_english: You are now like a withered leaf, Yama’s men stand waiting for you, you stand at decay’s door, with no provisions for the journey found. 236. So karohi dīpam-attano,

pali_mahasangiti: So karohi dīpamattano, Khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava; Niddhantamalo anaṅgaṇo, Dibbaṁ ariyabhūmiṁ upehisi.
english_sujato: Make an island of yourself! Swiftly strive, learn to be wise! Purged of stains, flawless, you’ll go to the heavenly realm of the noble ones.
interlinear_pali: So karohi dīpam-attano, khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava, niddhantamalo, anaṅgaṇo, dibbaṁ ariyabhūmim-ehisi.
interlinear_english: One should make an island for oneself, soon the wise one should endeavour, removing the stain, blemishless, you will go to the divine and noble realm.
interlinear_notes: Comm: pañcavidhaṁ Suddhāvāsabhūmiṁ; the fivefold realm of the Pure Lands, which is where anagāmī-s are reborn, which is why it is called noble.

pali_mahasangiti: Upanītavayo ca dānisi, Sampayātosi yamassa santikaṁ; Vāso te natthi antarā, Pātheyyampi ca te na vijjati.
english_sujato: You’ve journeyed the stages of life, and now you set out to meet Yama. Along the way there’s nowhere to stay, yet you have no supplies for the road.
interlinear_pali: Upanītavayo ca dāni ’si, sampayāto ’si Yamassa santike, vāso pi ca te natthi antarā, pātheyyam-pi ca te na vijjati.
interlinear_english: You are now advanced in age, you have come to Yama’s presence, there is nowhere to dwell in between, with no provisions for the journey found.

pali_mahasangiti: So karohi dīpamattano, Khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava; Niddhantamalo anaṅgaṇo, Na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.
english_sujato: Make an island of yourself! Swiftly strive, learn to be wise! Purged of stains, flawless, you’ll not come again to rebirth and old age.
interlinear_pali: So karohi dīpam-attano, khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava, niddhantamalo anaṅgaṇo, na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.
interlinear_english: One should make an island for oneself, soon the wise one should endeavour, removing the stain, blemishless, you will not come to birth and old age again.

pali_mahasangiti: Anupubbena medhāvī, thokaṁ thokaṁ khaṇe khaṇe; Kammāro rajatasseva, niddhame malamattano.
english_sujato: A smart person would purge their own stains gradually, bit by bit, moment by moment, like a smith smelting silver.
interlinear_pali: Anupubbena medhāvī, thokathokaṁ khaṇe khaṇe, kammāro rajatasseva, niddhame malam-attano.
interlinear_english: The sage gradually, little by little, moment by moment, should remove the stain from himself, like a smith (removes the stain) from silver.
narrative_pali: Anupubbena medhāvī, thokathokaṁ khaṇe khaṇe, kammāro rajatasseva, niddhame malam-attano.
narrative_english: The intelligent person gradually, little by little, moment by moment, like a smith removes the stain from silver should surely remove the stain from himself.

pali_mahasangiti: Ayasāva malaṁ samuṭṭhitaṁ, Tatuṭṭhāya tameva khādati; Evaṁ atidhonacārinaṁ, Sāni kammāni nayanti duggatiṁ.
english_sujato: It is the rust born on the iron that eats away the place it arose. And so it is their own deeds that lead the overly-ascetic to a bad place.
interlinear_pali: Ayasā va malaṁ samuṭṭhitaṁ, taduṭṭhāya tam-eva khādati, evaṁ atidhonacārinaṁ – sakakammāni nayanti duggatiṁ.
interlinear_english: As a (rust) stain arises from iron, and arisen from that, it eats it away, so with one who is overindulgent – his deeds lead him to a bad destiny.
interlinear_notes: The commentary says it means being indulgent in regard to the four requisites.
narrative_pali: Ayasā va malaṁ samuṭṭhitaṁ, taduṭṭhāya tam-eva khādati, evaṁ atidhonacārinaṁ – sakakammāni nayanti duggatiṁ.
narrative_english: As a rust stain arises from iron, and arisen it then eats it away, so with one who is overindulgent – his deeds lead him to a bad destiny.

pali_mahasangiti: Asajjhāyamalā mantā, anuṭṭhānamalā gharā; Malaṁ vaṇṇassa kosajjaṁ, pamādo rakkhato malaṁ.
english_sujato: Not rehearsing is the stain of hymns. The stain of houses is neglect. Laziness is the stain of beauty. A guard’s stain is negligence.
interlinear_pali: Asajjhāyamalā mantā, anuṭṭhānamalā gharā, malaṁ vaṇṇassa kosajjaṁ, pamādo rakkhato malaṁ.
interlinear_english: Lack of repetition is the ruin of chants, a lack of maintenance is the ruin of homes, indolence is the ruin of one’s appearance, heedlessness is the ruin of the one on guard.
interlinear_notes: Mala, the same word is translated as stain elsewhere, but here the only translation I feel that works throughout the verse is ruin.
narrative_pali: Asajjhāyamalā mantā, anuṭṭhānamalā gharā, malaṁ vaṇṇassa kosajjaṁ, pamādo rakkhato malaṁ.
narrative_english: Lack of repetition is the ruin of chants, a lack of maintenance is the ruin of homes, indolence is the ruin of one’s appearance, heedlessness is the ruin of the one on guard.

pali_mahasangiti: Malitthiyā duccaritaṁ, maccheraṁ dadato malaṁ; Malā ve pāpakā dhammā, asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
english_sujato: Misconduct is a woman’s stain. A giver’s stain is stinginess. Bad qualities are a stain in this world and the next.
interlinear_pali: Malitthiyā duccaritaṁ, maccheraṁ dadato malaṁ, malā ve pāpakā dhammā asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
interlinear_english: Bad conduct is a woman’s stain, stinginess is a giver’s stain, wicked actions are indeed stains both in this world and in the next.

pali_mahasangiti: Tato malā malataraṁ, avijjā paramaṁ malaṁ; Etaṁ malaṁ pahantvāna, nimmalā hotha bhikkhavo.
english_sujato: But a worse stain than these is ignorance, the worst stain of all. Having given up that stain, be without stains, mendicants!
interlinear_pali: Tato malā malataraṁ, avijjā paramaṁ malaṁ, etaṁ malaṁ pahatvāna, nimmalā hotha, bhikkhavo!
interlinear_english: A stain that is worse than that stain, ignorance is the supreme stain, after abandoning that stain, be without stains, O monastics!
interlinear_notes: Note that this is the last mention of stains (mala) in this chapter, although related themes make up the rest of the chapter.
narrative_pali: Tato malā malataraṁ, avijjā paramaṁ malaṁ, etaṁ malaṁ pahatvāna, nimmalā hotha, bhikkhavo!
narrative_english: A stain that is worse than that stain, ignorance is the supreme stain, after abandoning that stain,

pali_mahasangiti: Sujīvaṁ ahirikena, kākasūrena dhaṁsinā; Pakkhandinā pagabbhena, saṅkiliṭṭhena jīvitaṁ.
english_sujato: Life is easy for the shameless. With all the rude courage of a crow, they live pushy, rude, and corrupt.
interlinear_pali: Sujīvaṁ ahirikena, kākasūrena dhaṁsinā, pakkhandinā pagabbhena, saṅkiliṭṭhena jīvitaṁ.
interlinear_english: Life is light for one without shame, with the bold courage of a crow, living a life with backbiting, recklessness, and defilements.
narrative_pali: Sujīvaṁ ahirikena, kākasūrena dhaṁsinā, pakkhandinā pagabbhena, saṅkiliṭṭhena jīvitaṁ.
narrative_english: Life is light for one without shame, with the bold courage of a crow, living a life with backbiting, recklessness, and with defilements.

pali_mahasangiti: Hirīmatā ca dujjīvaṁ, niccaṁ sucigavesinā; Alīnenāppagabbhena, suddhājīvena passatā.
english_sujato: Life is hard for the conscientious, always seeking purity, neither clinging nor rude, pure of livelihood and discerning.
interlinear_pali: Hirīmatā ca dujjīvaṁ, niccaṁ sucigavesinā, alīnenāpagabbhena, suddhājīvena passatā.
interlinear_english: Life is hard when endowed with shame, for the one constantly seeking purity, for one sincere, and not reckless, looking for purity of life.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo pāṇamatipāteti, musāvādañca bhāsati; Loke adinnamādiyati, paradārañca gacchati.
english_sujato: Take anyone in this world who kills living creatures, speaks falsely, steals, commits adultery,
interlinear_pali: Yo pāṇam-atipāteti, musāvādañ-ca bhāsati, loke adinnaṁ ādiyati, paradārañ-ca gacchati,
interlinear_english: Whoever kills a living being, and speaks a word that is not true, takes what is not given here, and goes to another’s wife,
narrative_pali: Yo pāṇam-atipāteti, musāvādañ-ca bhāsati, loke adinnaṁ ādiyati, paradārañ-ca gacchati,
narrative_english: The one who kills living beings, and speaks a word that is not true, who takes what is not given here, and who goes to another’s wife,

pali_mahasangiti: Surāmerayapānañca, yo naro anuyuñjati; Idheva meso lokasmiṁ, mūlaṁ khaṇati attano.
english_sujato: and indulges in drinking beer and wine. Right here they dig up the root of their own self.
interlinear_pali: surāmerayapānañ-ca yo naro anuyuñjati, idhevam-eso lokasmiṁ mūlaṁ khaṇati attano.
interlinear_english: that person who is devoted to a drink of liquor and wine, digs up his own root right here in the world.
interlinear_notes: It is interesting that all of these deeds are in the singular, where we would more naturally use a plural. This happens in many places, but in such a long list it stands out here.

pali_mahasangiti: Evaṁ bho purisa jānāhi, pāpadhammā asaññatā; Mā taṁ lobho adhammo ca, ciraṁ dukkhāya randhayuṁ.
english_sujato: Know this, my man: they are unrestrained and wicked. Don’t let that greed and unrighteousness inflict pain on you for long.
interlinear_pali: Evaṁ bho purisa jānāhi, pāpadhammā asaññatā, mā taṁ lobho adhammo ca ciraṁ dukkhāya randhayuṁ.
interlinear_english: Know it thus, dear sir, a lack of restraint is a bad thing, let not greed and corruption oppress you with suffering for a long time.

pali_mahasangiti: Dadāti ve yathāsaddhaṁ, yathāpasādanaṁ jano; Tattha yo ca maṅku bhavati, paresaṁ pānabhojane; Na so divā vā rattiṁ vā, samādhimadhigacchati.
english_sujato: The people give according to their faith, according to their confidence. If you get upset over that, over others’ food and drink, you’ll not, by day or by night, become immersed in samādhi.
interlinear_pali: Dadāti ve yathāsaddhaṁ, yathāpasādanaṁ jano, tattha yo maṅku bhavati paresaṁ pānabhojane na so divā vā rattiṁ vā, samādhiṁ adhigacchati.
interlinear_english: The people give according to faith, according to their confidence, herein the one who becomes dejected because of food and drink (given) to others he does not, either by day or nigh attain to (good) concentration.
interlinear_notes: Meaning, broadly, others’ gains.
narrative_pali: Dadāti ve yathāsaddhaṁ, yathāpasādanaṁ jano, tattha yo maṅku bhavati paresaṁ pānabhojane
narrative_english: na so divā vā rattiṁ vā, samādhiṁ adhigacchati. The people give according to faith, according to their confidence, the one who is dejected through food and drink given to others, does not, either by day or night, attain to good concentration.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ, mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ; Sa ve divā vā rattiṁ vā, samādhimadhigacchati.
english_sujato: Those who have cut that out, dug it up at the root, eradicated it, they will, by day or by night, become immersed in samādhi.
interlinear_pali: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ, mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ, sa ve divā vā rattiṁ vā, samādhiṁ adhigacchati.
interlinear_english: For the one in whom this (dejection) is cut off, destroyed at the root, dug up, does, by day and night, attain to (good) concentration.

pali_mahasangiti: Natthi rāgasamo aggi, natthi dosasamo gaho; Natthi mohasamaṁ jālaṁ, natthi taṇhāsamā nadī.
english_sujato: There is no fire like greed, no crime like hate, no net like delusion, no river like craving.
interlinear_pali: Natthi rāgasamo aggi, natthi dosasamo gaho, natthi mohasamaṁ jālaṁ, natthi taṇhāsamā nadī.
interlinear_english: There is no fire that is like passion, there is nothing that takes a hold like hatred, there is no snare like delusion, there is no flood like craving.

pali_mahasangiti: Sudassaṁ vajjamaññesaṁ, attano pana duddasaṁ; Paresaṁ hi so vajjāni, opunāti yathā bhusaṁ; Attano pana chādeti, kaliṁva kitavā saṭho.
english_sujato: It’s easy to see the faults of others, hard to see one’s own. For the faults of others are tossed high like hay, while one’s own are hidden, as a cheat hides a bad hand.
interlinear_pali: Sudassaṁ vajjam-aññesaṁ, attano pana duddasaṁ, paresaṁ hi so vajjāni opuṇāti yathā bhusaṁ, attano pana chādeti, kaliṁ va kitavā saṭho.
interlinear_english: Easy to see are others’ fault, but one’s own is hard to see, for one sifts other people’s faults like they were chaff, but conceals one’s own (faults), like a crafty cheat (conceals) his defeat.
interlinear_notes: The commentary explains this last line differently, saying that saṭha means a hunter who conceals his body (kali) in order to catch his prey. I know of nowhere else that saṭha means a hunter, or kali means a body; if it were correct then we could translate: like a hunter (conceals) his body.
narrative_pali: Sudassaṁ vajjam-aññesaṁ, attano pana duddasaṁ,
narrative_english: paresaṁ hi so vajjāni opuṇāti yathā bhusaṁ,

pali_mahasangiti: Paravajjānupassissa, niccaṁ ujjhānasaññino; Āsavā tassa vaḍḍhanti, ārā so āsavakkhayā.
english_sujato: When you look for the flaws of others, always finding fault, your defilements only grow, you’re far from ending defilements.
interlinear_pali: Paravajjānupassissa niccaṁ ujjhānasaññino, āsavā tassa vaḍḍhanti, ārā so āsavakkhayā.
interlinear_english: The one who constantly looks for another’s fault, who is an abject complainer, for him the pollutants increase, he is far from their destruction.
narrative_pali: Paravajjānupassissa niccaṁ ujjhānasaññino,
narrative_english: āsavā tassa vaḍḍhanti, ārā so āsavakkhayā. One who looks for another’s faults, who is an abject complainer, for him the pollutants increase, he is far from their destruction.

pali_mahasangiti: Ākāseva padaṁ natthi, samaṇo natthi bāhire; Papañcābhiratā pajā, nippapañcā tathāgatā.
english_sujato: In the atmosphere there is no track, there’s no true ascetic outside here. People enjoy proliferation, the Realized Ones are free of proliferation.
interlinear_pali: Ākāse va padaṁ natthi, samaṇo natthi bāhire, papañcābhiratā pajā, nippapañcā Tathāgatā.
interlinear_english: There is no footprint in the sky, there is no ascetic on the outside, folk greatly delight in impediments, the Realised Ones are free of impediments.
interlinear_notes: Meaning: in outside sects.
narrative_pali: Ākāse va padaṁ natthi, samaṇo natthi bāhire, papañcābhiratā pajā, nippapañcā Tathāgatā.
narrative_english: There is no footprint in the sky, no ascetic on the outside, folk delight in impediments, the Realised are free of them.

pali_mahasangiti: Ākāseva padaṁ natthi, samaṇo natthi bāhire; Saṅkhārā sassatā natthi, natthi buddhānamiñjitaṁ.
english_sujato: In the atmosphere there is no track, there’s no true ascetic outside here. No conditions last forever, the Awakened Ones are not shaken.
interlinear_pali: Ākāse va padaṁ natthi, samaṇo natthi bāhire, saṅkhārā sassatā natthi, natthi Buddhānam-iñjitaṁ.
interlinear_english: There is no footprint in the sky, there is no ascetic on the outside, there are no constant conditions, there is no disturbance for the Buddhas.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na tena hoti dhammaṭṭho, yenatthaṁ sāhasā naye; Yo ca atthaṁ anatthañca, ubho niccheyya paṇḍito.
english_sujato: You don’t become just by passing hasty judgment. An astute person evaluates both what is pertinent and what is irrelevant.
interlinear_pali: Na tena hoti Dhammaṭṭho yenatthaṁ sahasā naye, yo ca atthaṁ anatthañ-ca ubho niccheyya paṇḍito.
interlinear_english: One who would hastily settle a case because of that is not one who stands by Dhamma, the wise one should discriminate the two: what is the case and what is not the case.
narrative_pali: Na tena hoti Dhammaṭṭho yenatthaṁ sahasā naye, yo ca atthaṁ anatthañ-ca ubho niccheyya paṇḍito.
narrative_english: One who would hastily settle a case is thereby not one who stands by Dhamma,

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Asāhasena dhammena, samena nayatī pare; Dhammassa gutto medhāvī, “dhammaṭṭho”ti pavuccati.
english_sujato: A wise one judges others without haste, justly and impartially; that guardian of the law is said to be just.
interlinear_pali: Asāhasena dhammena samena nayatī pare, Dhammassa gutto medhāvī, Dhammaṭṭho ti pavuccati.
interlinear_english: The one who settles for other people without haste, justly and impartially, the sagacious one, protecting Dhamma, is said to be one who stands by Dhamma.
interlinear_notes: This is the last mention of dhammaṭṭha in this chapter.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na tena paṇḍito hoti, yāvatā bahu bhāsati; Khemī averī abhayo, “paṇḍito”ti pavuccati.
english_sujato: You’re not an astute scholar just because you speak a lot. One who is secure, free of enmity and fear, is said to be astute.
interlinear_pali: Na tena paṇḍito hoti yāvatā bahu bhāsati; khemī averī abhayo, paṇḍito ti pavuccati.
interlinear_english: One is not a wise person merely because of speaking much; being safe, hatred-free, fearless, one is called a wise person.
narrative_pali: Na tena paṇḍito hoti yāvatā bahu bhāsati; khemī averī abhayo, paṇḍito ti pavuccati.
narrative_english: One is not a wise person merely because of speaking much;

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na tāvatā dhammadharo, yāvatā bahu bhāsati; Yo ca appampi sutvāna, dhammaṁ kāyena passati; Sa ve dhammadharo hoti, yo dhammaṁ nappamajjati.
english_sujato: You’re not one who has memorized the teaching just because you recite a lot. Someone who directly sees the teaching after hearing only a little is truly one who has memorized the teaching, for they can never forget it.
interlinear_pali: Na tāvatā Dhammadharo yāvatā bahu bhāsati, yo ca appam-pi sutvāna, Dhammaṁ kāyena passati, sa ve Dhammadharo hoti, yo Dhammaṁ nappamajjati.
interlinear_english: One is not a Dhamma-bearer merely through speaking much, but the one who, having heard a little, sees Dhamma for himself, is one who bears Dhamma, the one who is not heedless regarding Dhamma.
interlinear_notes: Literally: with the body, but for himself, perhaps as an analogue of attanā, seems to be the meaning.
narrative_pali: Na tāvatā Dhammadharo yāvatā bahu bhāsati, yo ca appam-pi sutvāna, Dhammaṁ kāyena passati, sa ve Dhammadharo hoti, yo Dhammaṁ nappamajjati.
narrative_english: One is not a Dhamma-bearer merely through speaking much, but the

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na tena thero so hoti, yenassa palitaṁ siro; Paripakko vayo tassa, “moghajiṇṇo”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: You don’t become a senior by getting some grey hairs; for one ripe only in age, is said to have aged in vain.
interlinear_pali: Na tena thero hoti yenassa palitaṁ siro, paripakko vayo tassa moghajiṇṇo ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: One is not an elder because one’s head has grey hair, for the one who is (only) well-matured, aged, is said to be old in vain.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Yamhi saccañca dhammo ca, ahiṁsā saṁyamo damo; Sa ve vantamalo dhīro, “thero” iti pavuccati.
english_sujato: One who is truthful and principled, harmless, restrained, and self-controlled, attentive, purged of stains, is said to be a senior.
interlinear_pali: Yamhi saccañ-ca Dhammo ca ahiṁsā saṁyamo damo, sa ve vantamalo dhīro thero iti pavuccati.
interlinear_english: In whom is truth, Dhamma, non-violence, restraint and (good) training, the wise one who throws out the stain is (truly) called an elder.
narrative_pali: Yamhi saccañ-ca Dhammo ca ahiṁsā saṁyamo damo, sa ve vantamalo dhīro thero iti pavuccati.
narrative_english: In whom is truth, Dhamma, restraint, non-violence, and good training, the wise one who throws out the stain is truly one called an elder.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na vākkaraṇamattena, vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā; Sādhurūpo naro hoti, issukī maccharī saṭho.
english_sujato: Not by mere enunciation, or a beautiful complexion does a person become holy, if they’re jealous, stingy, and devious.
interlinear_pali: Na vākkaraṇamattena vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā sādhurūpo naro hoti, issukī maccharī saṭho;
interlinear_english: Not by eloquence only, or by a beautiful complexion, is a person honourable, (if still) jealous, selfish and deceitful;
narrative_pali: Na vākkaraṇamattena vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā sādhurūpo naro hoti, issukī maccharī saṭho;
narrative_english: Not by eloquence only, or by a beautiful complexion, is a person honourable, if jealous, selfish, deceitful;

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ, mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ; Sa vantadoso medhāvī, “sādhurūpo”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: But if they’ve cut that out, dug it up at the root, eradicated it, that intelligent one, purged of vice, is said to be holy.
interlinear_pali: yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ, mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ, sa vantadoso medhāvī sādhurūpo ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: for the one in whom this is cut off, destroyed at the root, dug up, that sage who has thrown out hatred is said to be honourable.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na muṇḍakena samaṇo, abbato alikaṁ bhaṇaṁ; Icchālobhasamāpanno, samaṇo kiṁ bhavissati.
english_sujato: A liar and breaker of vows is no ascetic just because they shave their head. How on earth can one be an ascetic who’s full of desire and greed?
interlinear_pali: Na muṇḍakena samaṇo, abbato alikaṁ bhaṇaṁ, icchālobhasamāpanno, samaṇo kiṁ bhavissati?
interlinear_english: Not through a shaven head is one an ascetic, (if) one lacks vows, speaks lies, and is endowed with greed and desire, how will one be an ascetic?
interlinear_notes: Comm: sīlavatena ca dhūtavatena ca virahito; being without the vow of virtue and the vow of asceticism.
narrative_pali: Na muṇḍakena samaṇo, abbato alikaṁ bhaṇaṁ, icchālobhasamāpanno, samaṇo kiṁ bhavissati?
narrative_english: Not through a shaven head is one an ascetic, if one lacks vows, speaks lies, and has greed and desire, how will one be an ascetic?

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Yo ca sameti pāpāni, aṇuṁthūlāni sabbaso; Samitattā hi pāpānaṁ, “samaṇo”ti pavuccati.
english_sujato: One who stops all wicked deeds, great and small, because of stopping wicked deeds is said to be an ascetic.
interlinear_pali: Yo ca sameti pāpāni, aṇuṁ-thūlāni sabbaso – samitattā hi pāpānaṁ samaṇo ti pavuccati.
interlinear_english: The one who pacifies wicked deeds, small and great, in every way – through the pacifing of wicked deeds he is said to be an ascetic.
interlinear_notes: Being here short for upasameti.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na tena bhikkhu so hoti, yāvatā bhikkhate pare; Vissaṁ dhammaṁ samādāya, bhikkhu hoti na tāvatā.
english_sujato: You don’t become a mendicant just by begging from others. One who has undertaken domestic duties has not yet become a mendicant.
interlinear_pali: Na tena bhikkhu hoti yāvatā bhikkhate pare, vissaṁ Dhammaṁ samādāya bhikkhu hoti na tāvatā.
interlinear_english: One is not a monastic merely through eating others’ almsfood, the one who undertakes a false Dhamma to that extent is not a monastic.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Yodha puññañca pāpañca, bāhetvā brahmacariyavā; Saṅkhāya loke carati, sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: But one living a spiritual life, who has banished both merit and evil, who wanders having appraised the world, is said to be a mendicant.
interlinear_pali: Yodha puññañ-ca pāpañ-ca bāhetvā brahmacariyavā, saṅkhāya loke carati sa ce, bhikkhū ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: * If he is one who lives the holy life here, warding off both merit and demerit, and wanders with discrimination in the world, that one is said to be a monastic.
narrative_pali: Yodha puññañ-ca pāpañ-ca bāhetvā brahmacariyavā, saṅkhāya loke carati sa ce, bhikkhū ti vuccati.
narrative_english: Warding off both merit and demerit, the one who lives the spiritual life, if he wanders with discrimination, that one is said to be a monastic.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na monena munī hoti, mūḷharūpo aviddasu; Yo ca tulaṁva paggayha, varamādāya paṇḍito.
english_sujato: You don’t become a sage by being sagelike, while still confused and ignorant. The astute one who holds the scales, taking only the best,
interlinear_pali: Na monena munī hoti mūḷharūpo aviddasu, yo ca tulaṁ va paggayha, varam-ādāya paṇḍito.
interlinear_english: Not through silence is a deluded fool (considered to be) a seer, the wise one, like one holding the balance, takes up what is noble.
narrative_pali: Na monena munī hoti mūḷharūpo aviddasu, yo ca tulaṁ va paggayha, varam-ādāya paṇḍito.
narrative_english: Not through silence is a poor fool considered to be a sage, the wise one, like one holding the balance, takes up what is noble. 269. Pāpāni parivajjeti sa munī tena so muni;

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Pāpāni parivajjeti, sa munī tena so muni; Yo munāti ubho loke, “muni” tena pavuccati.
english_sujato: and shunning the bad— that is a sage, <j>and that is how one becomes a sage. One who sagely weighs both in the world, is thereby said to be a sage.
interlinear_pali: Pāpāni parivajjeti sa munī tena so muni, yo munāti ubho loke muni tena pavuccati.
interlinear_english: The seer who rejects wicked deeds through that is (considered) a seer, whoever understands both worlds because of that is said to be a seer.
interlinear_notes: The phrase means being unattached to both the internal and external worlds.

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na tena ariyo hoti, yena pāṇāni hiṁsati; Ahiṁsā sabbapāṇānaṁ, “ariyo”ti pavuccati.
english_sujato: You don’t become a noble one by harming living beings. One harmless toward all living beings is said to be a noble one.
interlinear_pali: Na tena ariyo hoti yena pāṇāni hiṁsati, ahiṁsā sabbapāṇānaṁ ariyo ti pavuccati.
interlinear_english: Not through hurting breathing beings one is noble, the one who does not hurt any breathing beings is said to be noble.
narrative_pali: Na tena ariyo hoti yena pāṇāni hiṁsati, ahiṁsā sabbapāṇānaṁ ariyo ti pavuccati.
narrative_english: Through not hurting living beings one is an Ariya, the one who does

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Na sīlabbatamattena, bāhusaccena vā pana; Atha vā samādhilābhena, vivittasayanena vā.
english_sujato: Not by precepts and observances, nor by much learning, nor by meditative immersion, nor by living in seclusion,
interlinear_pali: Na sīlabbatamattena, bāhusaccena vā pana, atha vā samādhilābhena, vivittasayanena vā,
interlinear_english: Not merely through virtue or vows, or through great learning, or through the attainment of concentration, or through a secluded dwelling,

vagga_name_en: The Chapter about One Who Stands by Dhamma
pali_mahasangiti: Phusāmi nekkhammasukhaṁ, aputhujjanasevitaṁ; Bhikkhu vissāsamāpādi, appatto āsavakkhayaṁ.
english_sujato: do I experience the bliss of renunciation not frequented by ordinary people. A mendicant cannot rest confident without attaining the end of defilements.
interlinear_pali: phusāmi nekkhammasukhaṁ, aputhujjanasevitaṁ; bhikkhu vissāsa’ māpādi appatto āsavakkhayaṁ.
interlinear_english: do I attain the happiness of renunciation, not practised by worldly people; let a monastic not be confident (as long as) the destruction of the pollutants is unattained.
interlinear_notes: Defined by the commentary as anāgāmisukhaṁ; the happiness of non-returning.
This parses as vissāsaṁ mā āpādi.
There is an uncertainty of person in this verse (I and then he), it might have been better written with 3rd person phusatī (with long -ī for the metre): does he attain...

pali_mahasangiti: Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho, saccānaṁ caturo padā; Virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṁ, dvipadānañca cakkhumā.
english_sujato: Of paths, the eightfold is the best; of truths, the four statements; dispassion is the best of things, and the Clear-eyed One is the best of humans.
interlinear_pali: Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho, saccānaṁ caturo padā, virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṁ, dipadānañ-ca Cakkhumā.
interlinear_english: The eightfold is the best of paths, four principles (the best) of truths, passionlessness the best of states, the Visionary (the best) of men.
interlinear_notes: Lit: of bipeds.
narrative_pali: Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho, saccānaṁ caturo padā, virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṁ, dipadānañ-ca Cakkhumā.
narrative_english: The eightfold is the best of paths, four principles the best of truths,

pali_mahasangiti: Eseva maggo natthañño, Dassanassa visuddhiyā; Etañhi tumhe paṭipajjatha, Mārassetaṁ pamohanaṁ.
english_sujato: This is the path, there is no other for the purification of vision. You all must practice this, it is the way to baffle Māra.
interlinear_pali: Eso va maggo natthañño, dassanassa visuddhiyā, etaṁ hi tumhe paṭipajjatha, Mārassetaṁ pamohanaṁ.
interlinear_english: This is the path, there is no other, for insight and for purity, you should enter upon this path, this is the confounding of Māra.

pali_mahasangiti: Etañhi tumhe paṭipannā, dukkhassantaṁ karissatha; Akkhāto vo mayā maggo, aññāya sallakantanaṁ.
english_sujato: When you all are practicing this, you’ll make an end of suffering. I have explained the path to you for extracting the thorn with wisdom.
interlinear_pali: Etaṁ hi tumhe paṭipannā dukkhassantaṁ karissatha, akkhāto ve mayā maggo, aññāya sallasanthanaṁ.
interlinear_english: Having entered upon this path you will make an end to suffering, the path was declared by me, the removal of the dart by knowledge.

pali_mahasangiti: Tumhehi kiccamātappaṁ, akkhātāro tathāgatā; Paṭipannā pamokkhanti, jhāyino mārabandhanā.
english_sujato: You yourselves must do the work, the Realized Ones just show the way. Meditators practicing absorption are released from Māra’s bonds.
interlinear_pali: Tumhehi kiccaṁ ātappaṁ akkhātāro Tathāgatā, paṭipannā pamokkhanti jhāyino Mārabandhanā.
interlinear_english: Your duty is to have ardour declare the Realised Ones, entering this path meditators will be released from the bonds of Māra.

pali_mahasangiti: “Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”ti, yadā paññāya passati; Atha nibbindati dukkhe, esa maggo visuddhiyā.
english_sujato: All conditions are impermanent— when this is seen with wisdom, one grows disillusioned with suffering: this is the path to purity.
interlinear_pali: Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
interlinear_english: All conditions are impermanent, when one sees this with wisdom, then one grows tired of suffering – this is the path to purity.
narrative_pali: Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
narrative_english: All conditions are impermanent, when one sees this with deep wisdom,

pali_mahasangiti: “Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā”ti, yadā paññāya passati; Atha nibbindati dukkhe, esa maggo visuddhiyā.
english_sujato: All conditions are suffering— when this is seen with wisdom, one grows disillusioned with suffering: this is the path to purity.
interlinear_pali: Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
interlinear_english: All conditions are suffering, when one sees this with wisdom, then one grows tired of suffering – this is the path to purity.
narrative_pali: Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
narrative_english: All conditions are suffering, when one sees this with deep wisdom, then one grows tired of suffering, this is the path to purity.

pali_mahasangiti: “Sabbe dhammā anattā”ti, yadā paññāya passati; Atha nibbindati dukkhe, esa maggo visuddhiyā.
english_sujato: All things are not-self— when this is seen with wisdom, one grows disillusioned with suffering: this is the path to purity.
interlinear_pali: Sabbe dhammā anattā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
interlinear_english: All components (of mind and body) are without self, when one sees this with wisdom, then one grows tired of suffering – this is the path to purity.
interlinear_notes: Comm: sabbe dhammā ti pañcakkhandā.
narrative_pali: Sabbe dhammā anattā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
narrative_english: All aggregates are without self, when one sees this with deep wisdom, then one grows tired of suffering, this is the path to purity.

pali_mahasangiti: Uṭṭhānakālamhi anuṭṭhahāno, Yuvā balī ālasiyaṁ upeto; Saṁsannasaṅkappamano kusīto, Paññāya maggaṁ alaso na vindati.
english_sujato: They don’t get going when it’s time to start; they’re young and strong, but given to sloth. Their mind depressed in sunken thought, lazy and slothful, they can’t discern the path.
interlinear_pali: Uṭṭhānakālamhi anuṭṭhahāno, yuvā balī, ālasiyaṁ upeto, saṁsannasaṅkappamano kusīto – paññāya maggaṁ alaso na vindati.
interlinear_english: The one who has not energy at a time for energy, youthful, strong, (but) given to laziness, whose mind lacks (right) intention and is indolent – the lazy one does not find wisdom’s path.
narrative_pali: Uṭṭhānakālamhi anuṭṭhahāno, yuvā balī, ālasiyaṁ upeto, saṁsannasaṅkappamano kusīto – paññāya maggaṁ alaso na vindati.
narrative_english: The one who has not timely energy, youthful, strong, but given to laziness, lacking right intention and indolent – the lazy one does not find wisdom’s path.

pali_mahasangiti: Vācānurakkhī manasā susaṁvuto, Kāyena ca nākusalaṁ kayirā; Ete tayo kammapathe visodhaye, Ārādhaye maggamisippaveditaṁ.
english_sujato: Guarded in speech, restrained in mind, doing no unskillful bodily deed. Purify these three ways of performing deeds, and win the path known to seers.
interlinear_pali: Vācānurakkhī manasā susaṁvuto, kāyena ca akusalaṁ na kayirā, ete tayo kammapathe visodhaye, ārādhaye maggaṁ isippaveditaṁ.
interlinear_english: Verbally guarded, well-restrained in mind, not doing a wrong deed with the body, one should purify these three paths of action, one should undertake the path shown by seers.
narrative_pali: Vācānurakkhī manasā susaṁvuto, kāyena ca akusalaṁ na kayirā, ete tayo kammapathe visodhaye, ārādhaye maggaṁ isippaveditaṁ.
narrative_english: Verbally guarded, well-restrained in mind, not doing demerit with the body, one should purify three paths of action, and undertake the path shown by seers.

pali_mahasangiti: Yogā ve jāyatī bhūri, ayogā bhūrisaṅkhayo; Etaṁ dvedhāpathaṁ ñatvā, bhavāya vibhavāya ca; Tathāttānaṁ niveseyya, yathā bhūri pavaḍḍhati.
english_sujato: From meditation springs wisdom, without meditation, wisdom ends. Knowing these two paths— of progress and decline— you should conduct yourself so that wisdom grows.
interlinear_pali: Yogā ve jāyatī bhūri, ayogā bhūrisaṅkhayo, etaṁ dvedhāpathaṁ ñatvā bhavāya vibhavāya ca, tathattānaṁ niveseyya yathā bhūri pavaḍḍhati.
interlinear_english: From effort arises wisdom, without effort wisdom is destroyed, having understood these two paths of development and decline, one should establish oneself so that one’s wisdom increases.
narrative_pali: Yogā ve jāyatī bhūri, ayogā bhūrisaṅkhayo, etaṁ dvedhāpathaṁ ñatvā bhavāya vibhavāya ca, tathattānaṁ niveseyya yathā bhūri pavaḍḍhati.
narrative_english: From effort arises wisdom, without effort wisdom is lost,

pali_mahasangiti: Vanaṁ chindatha mā rukkhaṁ, vanato jāyate bhayaṁ; Chetvā vanañca vanathañca, nibbanā hotha bhikkhavo.
english_sujato: Cut down the jungle, not just a tree; from the jungle springs fear. Having cut down jungle and snarl, be free of jungles, mendicants!
interlinear_pali: Vanaṁ chindatha mā rukkhaṁ, vanato jāyatī bhayaṁ, chetvā vanañ-ca vanathañ-ca, nibbanā hotha bhikkhavo.
interlinear_english: Cut down the forest (of defilements) not just a tree, from the forest arises a danger, having cut down the forest and thicket, you should be without forests, monastics.
interlinear_notes: Comm: rāgādikilesavanaṁ.
narrative_pali: Vanaṁ chindatha mā rukkhaṁ, vanato jāyatī bhayaṁ, chetvā vanañ-ca vanathañ-ca, nibbanā hotha bhikkhavo.
narrative_english: Cut down the forest and not just a tree, from the forest arises a danger, having cut down the forest and thicket, you should be without forests, monastics.

pali_mahasangiti: Yāva hi vanatho na chijjati, Aṇumattopi narassa nārisu; Paṭibaddhamanova tāva so, Vaccho khīrapakova mātari.
english_sujato: So long as the vine, no matter how small, that ties a man to women is not cut, his mind remains trapped, like a calf suckling its mother.
interlinear_pali: Yāva hi vanatho na chijjati aṇumatto pi narassa nārisu, paṭibaddhamano va tāva so, vaccho khīrapako va mātari.
interlinear_english: * For as long as an atom of desire of a man for a woman is not cut down, for just so long is the mind in bondage, like a calf (in bondage) to mother’s milk.
interlinear_notes: This is a play on the word vanatha, which also occurs in the previous verse, and means both a thicket and in metaphorical usage the thicket of desire.

pali_mahasangiti: Ucchinda sinehamattano, Kumudaṁ sāradikaṁva pāṇinā; Santimaggameva brūhaya, Nibbānaṁ sugatena desitaṁ.
english_sujato: Cut out affection for oneself, like plucking an autumn lotus. Foster only the path to peace, the extinguishment the Holy One taught.
interlinear_pali: Ucchinda sineham-attano, kumudaṁ sāradikaṁ va pāṇinā, santimaggam-eva brūhaya Nibbānaṁ Sugatena desitaṁ.
interlinear_english: Cut off (any) affection for one’s self, like an autumn lotus (plucked) with the hand, develop fully the path to peace and Nibbāna taught by the Happy One.

pali_mahasangiti: Idha vassaṁ vasissāmi, idha hemantagimhisu; Iti bālo vicinteti, antarāyaṁ na bujjhati.
english_sujato: “Here I will stay for the rains; here for winter, here the summer”; thus the fool thinks, not realizing the danger.
interlinear_pali: “Idha vassaṁ vasissāmi, idha hemantagimhisu”, iti bālo vicinteti, antarāyaṁ na bujjhati.
interlinear_english: “Here I will dwell during the rains, here during winter and summer”, in just such a way a fool thinks, not understanding the danger.

pali_mahasangiti: Taṁ puttapasusammattaṁ, byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ; Suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahoghova, maccu ādāya gacchati.
english_sujato: As a mighty flood sweeps away a sleeping village, death steals away a man who dotes on children and cattle, his mind caught up in them.
interlinear_pali: Taṁ puttapasusammattaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahogho va maccu ādāya gacchati.
interlinear_english: That person whose mind is attached and besotted by cattle and children, is snatched away by death just as a sleeping village (by) a great flood.
interlinear_notes: As we really need an instrumental here, it might have been better to write: suttaṁ gāmaṁ ogheneva.
narrative_pali: Taṁ puttapasusammattaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahogho va maccu ādāya gacchati.
narrative_english: That person whose mind is attached, besotted by cattle and children, is snatched away by death just as a sleeping village by a flood.

pali_mahasangiti: Na santi puttā tāṇāya, na pitā nāpi bandhavā; Antakenādhipannassa, natthi ñātīsu tāṇatā.
english_sujato: Children provide you no shelter, nor does father, nor relatives. When you’re seized by the terminator, there’s no shelter in family.
interlinear_pali: Na santi puttā tāṇāya, na pitā na pi bandhavā, Antakenādhipannassa natthi ñātisu tāṇatā.
interlinear_english: Children are not a refuge, nor fathers, not even kin, for one overcome by the End-Maker there is no refuge in relatives.
interlinear_notes: I.e. Māra incarnate, or death.
narrative_pali: Na santi puttā tāṇāya, na pitā na pi bandhavā, Antakenādhipannassa natthi ñātisu tāṇatā.
narrative_english: Children are not a true refuge, nor fathers, and not kin, for one overcome by the End-Maker there’s no refuge in relatives.

pali_mahasangiti: Etamatthavasaṁ ñatvā, paṇḍito sīlasaṁvuto; Nibbānagamanaṁ maggaṁ, khippameva visodhaye.
english_sujato: Knowing the reason for this, astute, and ethically restrained, one would quickly clear the path that leads to extinguishment.
interlinear_pali: Etam-atthavasaṁ ñatvā, paṇḍito sīlasaṁvuto, Nibbānagamanaṁ maggaṁ khippam-eva visodhaye.
interlinear_english: Understanding the truth of this the wise one, endowed with virtue, should quickly purify the path that is leading to Nibbāna.

pali_mahasangiti: Mattāsukhapariccāgā, passe ce vipulaṁ sukhaṁ; Caje mattāsukhaṁ dhīro, sampassaṁ vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: If by giving up material happiness one sees abundant happiness, the attentive would give up material happiness, seeing the abundant happiness.
interlinear_pali: Mattāsukhapariccāgā, passe ce vipulaṁ sukhaṁ, caje mattāsukhaṁ dhīro, sampassaṁ vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: If, by renouncing a small good, he might see a good that is large, the wise one should renounce that small good, seeing the good that is extensive.
narrative_pali: Mattāsukhapariccāgā, passe ce vipulaṁ sukhaṁ, caje mattāsukhaṁ dhīro, sampassaṁ vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.
narrative_english: If, by renouncing a small good, one might see a good that is large,

pali_mahasangiti: Paradukkhūpadhānena, attano sukhamicchati; Verasaṁsaggasaṁsaṭṭho, verā so na parimuccati.
english_sujato: Seeking their own happiness by imposing suffering on others, intimate with enmity, they’re not freed from enmity.
interlinear_pali: Paradukkhūpadānena attano sukham-icchati, verasaṁsaggasaṁsaṭṭho, verā so na parimuccati.
interlinear_english: One who desires happiness for oneself by causing suffering for another, being associated thus with hatred, is not fully released from that hatred.

pali_mahasangiti: Yañhi kiccaṁ apaviddhaṁ, akiccaṁ pana karīyati; Unnaḷānaṁ pamattānaṁ, tesaṁ vaḍḍhanti āsavā.
english_sujato: They dump what should be done, and do what should not be done. For the insolent and the negligent, their defilements only grow.
interlinear_pali: Yaṁ hi kiccaṁ tad-apaviddhaṁ, akiccaṁ pana kayirati, unnalānaṁ pamattānaṁ, tesaṁ vaḍḍhanti āsavā.
interlinear_english: That to be done is rejected, but what is not to be done is done, for the insolent, the heedless, their pollutants increase.

pali_mahasangiti: Yesañca susamāraddhā, niccaṁ kāyagatā sati; Akiccaṁ te na sevanti, kicce sātaccakārino; Satānaṁ sampajānānaṁ, atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.
english_sujato: Those that have properly undertaken constant mindfulness of the body, don’t cultivate what should not be done, but always do what should be done. Mindful and aware, their defilements come to an end.
interlinear_pali: Yesañ-ca susamāraddhā niccaṁ kāyagatā sati akiccaṁ te na sevanti, kicce sātaccakārino, satānaṁ sampajānānaṁ, atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.
interlinear_english: But for those who always properly undertake mindfulness of the body who do not practice what is not to be done, persisting in what is to be done, for those mindful ones, those fully aware, the pollutants are laid to rest.
narrative_pali: Yesañ-ca susamāraddhā niccaṁ kāyagatā sati akiccaṁ te na sevanti, kicce sātaccakārino, satānaṁ sampajānānaṁ, atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.
narrative_english: But those who always properly

pali_mahasangiti: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā, rājāno dve ca khattiye; Raṭṭhaṁ sānucaraṁ hantvā, anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.
english_sujato: Having slain mother and father, and two aristocratic kings, and having wiped out <j>the kingdom with its tax collector, the brahmin walks on untroubled.
interlinear_pali: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā, rājāno dve ca khattiye, raṭṭhaṁ sānucaraṁ hantvā, anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.
interlinear_english: Destroying mother and father, and (then) two noble kings, destroying a kingdom and its followers, the brahmin proceeds untroubled.
interlinear_notes: The commentary interprets this verse to mean: destroying craving and the conceit ‘I am’, and the two: eternalism and annihilationism, destroying passionate delight in the twelve sense spheres, the one without pollutants proceeds untroubled.
narrative_pali: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā, rājāno dve ca khattiye, raṭṭhaṁ sānucaraṁ hantvā, anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.
narrative_english: Destroying mother and father, and two noble kings, destroying a kingdom and its followers, the Brahmin proceeds untroubled.341

pali_mahasangiti: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā, rājāno dve ca sotthiye; Veyagghapañcamaṁ hantvā, anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.
english_sujato: Having slain mother and father, and two prosperous kings, and a tiger as the fifth, the brahmin walks on untroubled.
interlinear_pali: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā, rājāno dve ca sotthiye, veyyagghapañcamaṁ hantvā, anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.
interlinear_english: Destroying mother and father, and two prosperous kings, destroying a tiger as the fifth, the brahmin proceeds untroubled.
interlinear_notes: This is often interpreted as being equal to sottiye, learned; but there is no reason why we can’t translate it according to how it is written as sotthiye, prosperous, blessed. The commentary says two prosperous kings here means two brahmin kings.

The commentary interprets this verse to mean: destroying craving and the conceit ‘I am’, and the two: eternalism and annihilationism, destroying the five hindrances having doubt as the fifth, the one without pollutants proceeds untroubled.

pali_mahasangiti: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti, sadā gotamasāvakā; Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca, niccaṁ buddhagatā sati.
english_sujato: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the Buddha.
interlinear_pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ Buddhagatā sati.
interlinear_english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Buddha.
narrative_pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ Buddhagatā sati. Gotama’s disciples always
narrative_english: awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Buddha.

pali_mahasangiti: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti, sadā gotamasāvakā; Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca, niccaṁ dhammagatā sati.
english_sujato: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the teaching.
interlinear_pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ Dhammagatā sati.
interlinear_english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Dhamma.

pali_mahasangiti: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti, sadā gotamasāvakā; Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca, niccaṁ saṅghagatā sati.
english_sujato: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the Saṅgha.
interlinear_pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ Saṅghagatā sati.
interlinear_english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Saṅgha.

pali_mahasangiti: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti, sadā gotamasāvakā; Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca, niccaṁ kāyagatā sati.
english_sujato: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night are constantly mindful of the body.
interlinear_pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ kāyagatā sati.
interlinear_english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the body.

pali_mahasangiti: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti, sadā gotamasāvakā; Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca, ahiṁsāya rato mano.
english_sujato: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, whose minds day and night delight in harmlessness.
interlinear_pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca ahiṁsāya rato mano.
interlinear_english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night have a mind that delights in non-violence.

pali_mahasangiti: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti, sadā gotamasāvakā; Yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca, bhāvanāya rato mano.
english_sujato: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, whose minds day and night delight in meditation.
interlinear_pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca bhāvanāya rato mano.
interlinear_english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night have a mind that delights in cultivation.

pali_mahasangiti: Duppabbajjaṁ durabhiramaṁ, Durāvāsā gharā dukhā; Dukkhosamānasaṁvāso, Dukkhānupatitaddhagū; Tasmā na caddhagū siyā, Na ca dukkhānupatito siyā.
english_sujato: Going forth is hard, it’s hard to be happy; life at home is hard too, and painful, it’s painful to stay when you’ve nothing in common. A traveler is a prey to pain, so don’t be a traveler, don’t be prey to pain.
interlinear_pali: Duppabbajjaṁ durabhiramaṁ, durāvāsā gharā dukhā, dukkhosamānasaṁvāso, dukkhānupatitaddhagū, tasmā na caddhagū siyā, na ca dukkhānupatito siyā.
interlinear_english: The going forth is hard, it is hard to find delight (therein), (but) it is (also) hard to dwell in households that are suffering, dwelling together with those different is suffering, travellers (in the round of births) are affected by suffering, therefore do not be a traveller, do not be affected by suffering.
narrative_pali: Duppabbajjaṁ durabhiramaṁ, durāvāsā gharā dukhā, dukkhosamānasaṁvāso, dukkhānupatitaddhagū, tasmā na caddhagū siyā, na ca dukkhānupatito siyā.
narrative_english: The going-forth is hard, it is hard to find real delight therein,

pali_mahasangiti: Saddho sīlena sampanno, yasobhogasamappito; Yaṁ yaṁ padesaṁ bhajati, tattha tattheva pūjito.
english_sujato: One who is faithful, accomplished in ethics, blessed with fame and wealth, is honored in whatever place they frequent.
interlinear_pali: Saddho sīlena sampanno yasobhogasamappito, yaṁ yaṁ padesaṁ bhajati, tattha tattheva pūjito.
interlinear_english: The faithful one who is endowed with virtue, and has wealth and fame, whatever district he resorts to, right there and then he is worshipped.

pali_mahasangiti: Dūre santo pakāsenti, himavantova pabbato; Asantettha na dissanti, rattiṁ khittā yathā sarā.
english_sujato: The good shine from afar, like the Himalayan peaks, but the wicked are not seen, like arrows scattered in the night.
interlinear_pali: Dūre santo pakāsenti, himavanto va pabbato, asantettha na dissanti, rattiṁ khittā yathā sarā.
interlinear_english: The good are visible from far, like a mountain covered in snow, (but) the wicked are not seen here, just like arrows shot in the night.
interlinear_notes: The commentary says visible means coming within the range of knowledge of the Buddhas; and the wicked are those who have set their sight on material rewards.

pali_mahasangiti: Ekāsanaṁ ekaseyyaṁ, eko caramatandito; Eko damayamattānaṁ, vanante ramito siyā.
english_sujato: Sitting alone, sleeping alone, tirelessly wandering alone; one who tames themselves alone would delight within a forest.
interlinear_pali: Ekāsanaṁ ekaseyyaṁ, eko caram-atandito, eko damayam-attānaṁ vanante ramito siyā.
interlinear_english: Sitting alone, lying down alone, walking alone, diligent, the solitary one who trains himself will delight in the edge of a forest.

pali_mahasangiti: Abhūtavādī nirayaṁ upeti, Yo vāpi katvā na karomi cāha; Ubhopi te pecca samā bhavanti, Nihīnakammā manujā parattha.
english_sujato: A liar goes to hell, as does one who denies what they did. Both are equal in the hereafter, those men of base deeds.
interlinear_pali: Abhūtavādī nirayaṁ upeti, yo vāpi katvā ‘Na karomī’ ti cāha, ubho pi te pecca samā bhavanti nihīnakammā manujā parattha.
interlinear_english: The one who speaks falsely goes to the underworld, and he who says: ‘I did not do’ what he has done, both of these are just the same when they have gone to the hereafter, (they are) humans who did base deeds.
narrative_pali: Abhūtavādī Nirayaṁ upeti, yo vāpi katvā ‘Na karomī’ ti cāha, ubho pi te pecca samā bhavanti nihīnakammā manujā parattha.
narrative_english: The one who speaks falsely goes to Niraya Hell, and he who says: ‘I did not do’ what he has done, both of these are just the same when they have gone to the hereafter, they are humans who did base deeds.

pali_mahasangiti: Kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo, pāpadhammā asaññatā; Pāpā pāpehi kammehi, nirayaṁ te upapajjare.
english_sujato: Many who wear a scrap of ocher cloth are unrestrained and wicked. Being wicked, they are reborn in hell due to their bad deeds.
interlinear_pali: Kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo pāpadhammā asaññatā, pāpā pāpehi kammehi nirayaṁ te upapajjare.
interlinear_english: Many wearing the monastic robe around their necks are wicked, unrestrained, the wicked through their wicked deeds re-arisein the underworld.
narrative_pali: Kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo pāpadhammā asaññatā, pāpā pāpehi kammehi Nirayaṁ te upapajjare.
narrative_english: Many wearing the robe around their necks are wicked, unrestrained, the wicked through their wicked deeds arise in the Niraya Hell.

pali_mahasangiti: Seyyo ayoguḷo bhutto, tatto aggisikhūpamo; Yañce bhuñjeyya dussīlo, raṭṭhapiṇḍamasaññato.
english_sujato: It’d be better for the immoral and unrestrained to eat an iron ball, scorching, like a burning flame, than to eat the nation’s alms.
interlinear_pali: Seyyo ayoguḷo bhutto tatto, aggisikhūpamo, yañ-ce bhuñjeyya dussīlo raṭṭhapiṇḍaṁ asaññato.
interlinear_english: It’s better to have eaten a glowing iron ball, like a flame of fire, than that (the monastic) who is unrestrained and unvirtuous should enjoy the country’s almsfood.

pali_mahasangiti: Cattāri ṭhānāni naro pamatto, Āpajjati paradārūpasevī; Apuññalābhaṁ na nikāmaseyyaṁ, Nindaṁ tatīyaṁ nirayaṁ catutthaṁ.
english_sujato: Four things befall a heedless man who sleeps with another’s wife: wickedness, poor sleep, ill-repute, and rebirth in hell.
interlinear_pali: Cattāri ṭhānāni naro pamatto, āpajjatī paradārūpasevī: apuññalābhaṁ, nanikāmaseyyaṁ, nindaṁ tatīyaṁ, nirayaṁ catutthaṁ.
interlinear_english: There are four states the man who is heedless, the man who consorts with other man’s wives, undergoes: he gains demerit, an uncomfortable bed, blame as third, and (rebirth in) the underworld as fourth.
narrative_pali: Cattāri ṭhānāni naro pamatto, āpajjatī paradārūpasevī: apuññalābhaṁ, nanikāmaseyyaṁ, nindaṁ tatīyaṁ, Nirayaṁ catutthaṁ.
narrative_english: There are four states the man who is heedless, the man who consorts with other men’s wives, undergoes: demerit, a rough bed, blame, and rebirth in Niraya Hell as fourth.

pali_mahasangiti: Apuññalābho ca gatī ca pāpikā, Bhītassa bhītāya ratī ca thokikā; Rājā ca daṇḍaṁ garukaṁ paṇeti, Tasmā naro paradāraṁ na seve.
english_sujato: He accrues wickedness and is reborn in a bad place, all so a frightened couple <j>may snatch a moment’s pleasure, for which rulers impose a heavy punishment. That’s why a man should not <j>sleep with another’s wife.
interlinear_pali: Apuññalābho ca gatī ca pāpikā, bhītassa bhītāya ratī ca thokikā, rājā ca daṇḍaṁ garukaṁ paṇeti, tasmā naro paradāraṁ na seve.
interlinear_english: Gaining demerit and a bad destiny, and (only) the small delight of a scared man with a scared woman, and kings who apply heavy punishment, a man therefore should not consort with another’s wife.

pali_mahasangiti: Kuso yathā duggahito, hatthamevānukantati; Sāmaññaṁ dupparāmaṭṭhaṁ, nirayāyupakaḍḍhati.
english_sujato: When kusa grass is wrongly grasped it only cuts the hand. So too, the ascetic life, when wrongly taken, drags you to hell.
interlinear_pali: Kuso yathā duggahito hattham-evānukantati, sāmaññaṁ dupparāmaṭṭhaṁ nirayāyupakaḍḍhati.
interlinear_english: As jagged grass, wrongly grasped, cuts into the hand, so does the ascetic life, wrongly grasped, drag one down to the underworld.
interlinear_notes: Kusa is a particular type of grass, see Nature s.v. Kusa: A type of perennial grass with a sharp spiky leaf growing up to 0.9 m. high and with deep roots; but the commentary here defines it to mean any grass that is capable of cutting, including palm leaves, hence the translation.

pali_mahasangiti: Yaṁ kiñci sithilaṁ kammaṁ, saṅkiliṭṭhañca yaṁ vataṁ; Saṅkassaraṁ brahmacariyaṁ, na taṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english_sujato: Any lax act, any corrupt observance, or suspicious spiritual life, is not very fruitful.
interlinear_pali: Yaṁ kiñci sithilaṁ kammaṁ saṅkiliṭṭhañ-ca yaṁ vataṁ, saṅkassaraṁ brahmacariyaṁ na taṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whatever lax deed there is and that vow which is defiled, (know that) a holy life that is doubtful does not have great fruit for that one.
narrative_pali: Yaṁ kiñci sithilaṁ kammaṁ saṅkiliṭṭhañ-ca yaṁ vataṁ, saṅkassaraṁ brahmacariyaṁ na taṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
narrative_english: Whatever lax deed there is and that vow which is defiled, know that a holy life that is doubtful does not have great fruit for that one.

pali_mahasangiti: Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṁ, daḷhamenaṁ parakkame; Sithilo hi paribbājo, bhiyyo ākirate rajaṁ.
english_sujato: If one is to do what should be done, one should staunchly strive. For the life gone forth when laxly led just stirs up dust all the more.
interlinear_pali: Kayirañ-ce kayirāthenaṁ, daḷham-enaṁ parakkame, saṭhilo hi paribbājo bhiyyo ākirate rajaṁ.
interlinear_english: If he would do what should be done, he should be firm in his effort, for the wanderer who is lax spreads a lot of impurity.

pali_mahasangiti: Akataṁ dukkaṭaṁ seyyo, pacchā tappati dukkaṭaṁ; Katañca sukataṁ seyyo, yaṁ katvā nānutappati.
english_sujato: A bad deed is better left undone, for it will plague you later on. A good deed is better done, one that does not plague you.
interlinear_pali: Akataṁ dukkataṁ seyyo, pacchā tapati dukkataṁ, katañ-ca sukataṁ seyyo, yaṁ katvā nānutappati.
interlinear_english: Better undone is a wrong-doing, a wrong-doing one later regrets, better done is what is well-done, which, when done, one does not regret.
narrative_pali: Akataṁ dukkataṁ seyyo, pacchā tapati dukkataṁ, katañ-ca sukataṁ seyyo, yaṁ katvā nānutappati.
narrative_english: Better undone is wrong-doing, wrong-doing one later regrets,

pali_mahasangiti: Nagaraṁ yathā paccantaṁ, guttaṁ santarabāhiraṁ; Evaṁ gopetha attānaṁ, khaṇo vo mā upaccagā; Khaṇātītā hi socanti, nirayamhi samappitā.
english_sujato: As a frontier city is guarded inside and out, so you should ward yourselves— don’t let the moment pass you by. For if you miss your moment you’ll grieve when sent to hell.
interlinear_pali: Nagaraṁ yathā paccantaṁ guttaṁ santarabāhiraṁ, evaṁ gopetha attānaṁ, khaṇo vo mā upaccagā, khaṇātītā hi socanti nirayamhi samappitā.
interlinear_english: As a border town is guarded on the inside and the outside, so one should watch over oneself, and you should not let the moment pass, for when the chance has passed they grieve when consigned to the underworld.
