narrative_pali: Nagaraṁ yathā paccantaṁ guttaṁ santarabāhiraṁ, evaṁ gopetha attānaṁ, khaṇo vo mā upaccagā, khaṇātītā hi socanti Nirayamhi samappitā.
narrative_english: As a border town is guarded on the inside and the outside, so one should watch over oneself, and should not let the moment pass, for when the chance has passed they grieve, when consigned to Niraya Hell.

pali_mahasangiti: Alajjitāye lajjanti, lajjitāye na lajjare; Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā, sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
english_sujato: Unashamed of what is shameful, ashamed of what is not shameful; beings who uphold wrong view go to a bad place.
interlinear_pali: Alajjitāye lajjanti, lajjitāye na lajjare, micchādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
interlinear_english: They are ashamed of what is not shameful, not ashamed of what is shameful, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny.

pali_mahasangiti: Abhaye bhayadassino, bhaye cābhayadassino; Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā, sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
english_sujato: Seeing danger where there is none, and blind to the actual danger, beings who uphold wrong view go to a bad place.
interlinear_pali: Abhaye bhayadassino, bhaye cābhayadassino, micchādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
interlinear_english: Seeing fear in what is not fearful, not seeing fear in what is fearful, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny.

pali_mahasangiti: Avajje vajjamatino, vajje cāvajjadassino; Micchādiṭṭhisamādānā, sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
english_sujato: Seeing fault where there is none, and blind to the actual fault, beings who uphold wrong view go to a bad place.
interlinear_pali: Avajje vajjamatino, vajje cāvajjadassino, micchādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
interlinear_english: Finding blame in what is blameless, not seeing blame in what is blameable, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny.

pali_mahasangiti: Vajjañca vajjato ñatvā, avajjañca avajjato; Sammādiṭṭhisamādānā, sattā gacchanti suggatiṁ.
english_sujato: Knowing a fault as a fault and the faultless as faultless, beings who uphold right view go to a good place.
interlinear_pali: Vajjañ-ca vajjato ñatvā, avajjañ-ca avajjato, sammādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti suggatiṁ.
interlinear_english: Knowing blame in what is blameable, and no blame in what is blameless, undertaking right views, beings go to a good destiny.
narrative_pali: Vajjañ-ca vajjato ñatvā, avajjañ-ca avajjato, sammādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti suggatiṁ.
narrative_english: Knowing blame in the blameable, and no blame in what is blameless,

pali_mahasangiti: Ahaṁ nāgova saṅgāme, cāpato patitaṁ saraṁ; Ativākyaṁ titikkhissaṁ, dussīlo hi bahujjano.
english_sujato: Like an elephant struck with arrows in battle, I shall endure abuse, for so many folk are badly behaved.
interlinear_pali: Ahaṁ nāgo va saṅgāme cāpāto patitaṁ saraṁ ativākyaṁ titikkhissaṁ, dussīlo hi bahujjano.
interlinear_english: Like an elephant in battle (endures) an arrow shot from bow (so) will I endure abuse, for many people are unvirtuous.
narrative_pali: Ahaṁ nāgo va saṅgāme cāpāto patitaṁ saraṁ ativākyaṁ titikkhissaṁ, dussīlo hi bahujjano.
narrative_english: Like an elephant in battle endures an arrow shot from bow so will I endure abuse, for many people are unvirtuous.

pali_mahasangiti: Dantaṁ nayanti samitiṁ, dantaṁ rājābhirūhati; Danto seṭṭho manussesu, yotivākyaṁ titikkhati.
english_sujato: The well-tamed beast is the one led to the crowd; the tamed elephant’s the one the king mounts; the tamed person who endures abuse is the best of human beings.
interlinear_pali: Dantaṁ nayanti samitiṁ, dantaṁ rājābhirūhati, danto seṭṭho manussesu, yotivākyaṁ titikkhati.
interlinear_english: They lead one trained into a crowd, a king mounts one who has been trained, amongst humans one trained is best, the one who can endure abuse.

pali_mahasangiti: Varamassatarā dantā, ājānīyā ca sindhavā; Kuñjarā ca mahānāgā, attadanto tato varaṁ.
english_sujato: Those who have tamed themselves are better than fine tamed mules, thoroughbreds from Sindh, or giant tuskers.
interlinear_pali: Varam-assatarā dantā, ājānīyā ca Sindhavā, kuñjarā ca mahānāgā, attadanto tato varaṁ.
interlinear_english: Noble are the well-trained horses, the well-bred horses from Sindh, and the great tusker elephants, (and even) more noble than that is the one who has trained himself.

pali_mahasangiti: Na hi etehi yānehi, gaccheyya agataṁ disaṁ; Yathāttanā sudantena, danto dantena gacchati.
english_sujato: For not on those mounts would you go to the untrodden place, whereas, with the help of one <j>whose self is well tamed, you go there, tamed by the tamed.
interlinear_pali: Na hi etehi yānehi gaccheyya agataṁ disaṁ, yathattanā sudantena, danto dantena gacchati.
interlinear_english: Not by these vehicles can one go to the place beyond destinations, as one through training himself well, being trained by the training, goes.
interlinear_notes: I.e. Nibbāna.

pali_mahasangiti: Dhanapālo nāma kuñjaro, Kaṭukabhedano dunnivārayo; Baddho kabaḷaṁ na bhuñjati, Sumarati nāgavanassa kuñjaro.
english_sujato: The tusker named Dhanapāla is musky in rut, hard to control. Bound, he eats not a morsel, for he misses the elephant forest.
interlinear_pali: Dhanapālakŏ nāma kuñjaro kaṭukappabhedano dunnivārayo, baddho kabalaṁ na bhuñjati, sumarati nāgavanassa kuñjaro.
interlinear_english: The tusker named Dhanapālaka musty in rut, difficult to restrain, bound, he doesn’t eat (even) a morsel, the tusker remembers the elephant forest.
interlinear_notes: The verse is unusual in that it has no moral outside of the story which is attached to it.
narrative_pali: Dhanapālakŏ nāma kuñjaro kaṭukappabhedano dunnivārayo, baddho kabalaṁ na bhuñjati, sumarati nāgavanassa kuñjaro.
narrative_english: The tusker Dhanapālaka in rut, difficult to restrain, bound, he doesn’t eat a morsel, the tusker remembers the forest.356

pali_mahasangiti: Middhī yadā hoti mahagghaso ca, Niddāyitā samparivattasāyī; Mahāvarāhova nivāpapuṭṭho, Punappunaṁ gabbhamupeti mando.
english_sujato: One who gets drowsy from overeating, fond of sleep, rolling round the bed like a great hog stuffed with grain: that dullard returns to the womb again and again.
interlinear_pali: Middhī yadā hoti mahagghaso ca, niddāyitā samparivattasāyī, mahāvarāho va nivāpapuṭṭho, punappunaṁ gabbham-upeti mando.
interlinear_english: When one is torpid and overeats, sleepy and rolling on the bed, like a great pig fed on fodder, that fool comes to the womb again.

pali_mahasangiti: Idaṁ pure cittamacāri cārikaṁ, Yenicchakaṁ yatthakāmaṁ yathāsukhaṁ; Tadajjahaṁ niggahessāmi yoniso, Hatthippabhinnaṁ viya aṅkusaggaho.
english_sujato: In the past my mind wandered how it wished, where it liked, as it pleased. Now I’ll carefully guide it, as a trainer with a hook guides a rutting elephant.
interlinear_pali: Idaṁ pure cittam-acāri cārikaṁ yenicchakaṁ yatthakāmaṁ yathāsukhaṁ, tad-ajjahaṁ niggahessāmi yoniso, hatthim-pabhinnaṁ viya aṅkusaggaho.
interlinear_english: Formerly this wandering mind wandered through desire, pleasure and happiness, (but) today I will control it wisely, like one with goad an elephant in rut.
narrative_pali: Idaṁ pure cittam-acāri cārikaṁ yenicchakaṁ yatthakāmaṁ yathāsukhaṁ, tad-ajjahaṁ niggahessāmi yoniso, hatthim-pabhinnaṁ viya aṅkusaggaho.
narrative_english: Formerly this wandering mind wandered through desire, pleasure, happiness, but today I will control it wisely, like one with goad an elephant.

pali_mahasangiti: Appamādaratā hotha, sacittamanurakkhatha; Duggā uddharathattānaṁ, paṅke sannova kuñjaro.
english_sujato: Delight in diligence! Take good care of your mind! Pull yourself out of this pit, like an elephant sunk in a bog.
interlinear_pali: Appamādaratā hotha, sacittam-anurakkhatha, duggā uddharathattānaṁ paṅke sanno va kuñjaro.
interlinear_english: You should delight in heedfulness, you should always protect your mind, you should raise yourself from this pit like the tusker sunk in the mud.

pali_mahasangiti: Sace labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ, Saddhiṁ caraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ; Abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni, Careyya tenattamano satīmā.
english_sujato: If you find an alert companion, an attentive friend to live happily together, then, overcoming all adversities, wander with them, joyful and mindful.
interlinear_pali: Sace labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ saddhiṁcaraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ, abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni careyya tenattamano satīmā.
interlinear_english: If you should find a prudent friend or companion, one who lives well, a wise one, overcoming all your troubles you should live with that one, glad and mindful.
narrative_pali: Sace labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ saddhiṁcaraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ, abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni careyya tenattamano satīmā.
narrative_english: If you find a prudent, wise friend or companion who lives well, overcoming all your troubles, live with that one, glad and mindful. 329. No ce labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ

pali_mahasangiti: No ce labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ, Saddhiṁ caraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ; Rājāva raṭṭhaṁ vijitaṁ pahāya, Eko care mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.
english_sujato: If you find no alert companion, no attentive friend to live happily together, then, like a king who flees his conquered realm, wander alone like a tusker in the wilds.
interlinear_pali: No ce labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ saddhiṁcaraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ, rājā va raṭṭhaṁ vijitaṁ pahāya eko care mātaṅgaraññe va nāgo.
interlinear_english: If you do not find a prudent friend or companion, one who lives well, a wise one, like a king who abandons his conquered kingdom one should live alone like a solitary elephant in the forest.

pali_mahasangiti: Ekassa caritaṁ seyyo, Natthi bāle sahāyatā; Eko care na ca pāpāni kayirā, Appossukko mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.
english_sujato: It’s better to wander alone, there’s no fellowship with fools. Wander alone and do no wrong, at ease like a tusker in the wilds.
interlinear_pali: Ekassa caritaṁ seyyo, natthi bāle sahāyatā, eko care na ca pāpāni kayirā, appossukko mātaṅgaraññe va nāgo.
interlinear_english: It is better to live alone, there can be no friendship with a fool, one should live alone and not do anything bad, unconcerned like a solitary elephant in the forest.

pali_mahasangiti: Atthamhi jātamhi sukhā sahāyā, Tuṭṭhī sukhā yā itarītarena; Puññaṁ sukhaṁ jīvitasaṅkhayamhi, Sabbassa dukkhassa sukhaṁ pahānaṁ.
english_sujato: A friend in need is a blessing; it’s a blessing to be content with whatever; good deeds are a blessing at the end of life, and giving up all suffering is a blessing.
interlinear_pali: Atthamhi jātamhi sukhā sahāyā, tuṭṭhī sukhā yā itarītarena, puññaṁ sukhaṁ jīvitasaṅkhayamhi, sabbassa dukkhassa sukhaṁ pahāṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Friends are good whenever need arises, being content with everything is good, at the break-up of life merit is good, the abandoning of all suffering is good.
narrative_pali: Atthamhi jātamhi sukhā sahāyā, tuṭṭhī sukhā yā itarītarena, puññaṁ sukhaṁ jīvitasaṅkhayamhi, sabbassa dukkhassa sukhaṁ pahāṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Friends are good whenever need arises, being content with everything is good, at the break-up of life merit is good, abandoning of suffering is good.

pali_mahasangiti: Sukhā matteyyatā loke, atho petteyyatā sukhā; Sukhā sāmaññatā loke, atho brahmaññatā sukhā.
english_sujato: In this world it’s a blessing to serve one’s mother and one’s father. And it’s a blessing also to serve ascetics and brahmins.
interlinear_pali: Sukhā matteyyatā loke, atho petteyyatā sukhā, sukhā sāmaññatā loke, atho brahmaññatā sukhā.
interlinear_english: Respecting one’s mother is good in the world, also respecting one’s father is good, respecting ascetics is good in the world, also respecting (true) brahmins is good.

pali_mahasangiti: Sukhaṁ yāva jarā sīlaṁ, sukhā saddhā patiṭṭhitā; Sukho paññāya paṭilābho, pāpānaṁ akaraṇaṁ sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: It’s a blessing to keep precepts until you grow old; a blessing to be grounded in faith; the getting of wisdom’s a blessing; and it’s a blessing to avoid doing wrong.
interlinear_pali: Sukhaṁ yāva jarā sīlaṁ, sukhā saddhā patiṭṭhitā, sukho paññāya paṭilābho, pāpānaṁ akaraṇaṁ sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: Virtuous conduct till old age is good, the establishing of faith is good, the acquisition of wisdom is good, doing nothing wicked is good.

pali_mahasangiti: Manujassa pamattacārino, Taṇhā vaḍḍhati māluvā viya; So plavatī hurā huraṁ, Phalamicchaṁva vanasmi vānaro.
english_sujato: When a man lives heedlessly, craving grows in them like a camel’s foot creeper. They jump from one thing to the next, like a langur greedy for fruit in a forest grove.
interlinear_pali: Manujassa pamattacārino taṇhā vaḍḍhati māluvā viya, so palavatī hurāhuraṁ phalam-icchaṁ va vanasmi’ vānaro.
interlinear_english: For a human who lives life heedlessly craving increases like a clinging creeper, he rushes from one place to another like a monkey desiring fruit in the forest.

pali_mahasangiti: Yaṁ esā sahate jammī, taṇhā loke visattikā; Sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti, abhivaṭṭhaṁva bīraṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Whoever is beaten by this wretched craving, this attachment to the world, their sorrow grows, like grass in the rain.
interlinear_pali: Yaṁ esā sahatī jammī taṇhā loke visattikā, sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti abhivaṭṭhaṁ va bīraṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: That one who is overcome by these low cravings and attachments in the world, for him griefs increase like grass that has had heavy rain.
narrative_pali: Yaṁ esā sahatī jammī taṇhā loke visattikā, sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti abhivaṭṭhaṁ va bīraṇaṁ.
narrative_english: That one who is overcome by these low cravings and attachments in the world, for him griefs increase like grass that has had heavy rain.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo cetaṁ sahate jammiṁ, taṇhaṁ loke duraccayaṁ; Sokā tamhā papatanti, udabinduva pokkharā.
english_sujato: But whoever prevails over this wretched craving, so hard to get over in the world, their sorrows fall from them, like a drop from a lotus-leaf.
interlinear_pali: Yo cetaṁ sahatī jammiṁ taṇhaṁ loke duraccayaṁ, sokā tamhā papatanti udabindu va pokkharā.
interlinear_english: Whoever overcomes this low craving in the world, which is difficult to get past, griefs fall from him like a drop of water from a lotus.

pali_mahasangiti: Taṁ vo vadāmi bhaddaṁ vo, yāvantettha samāgatā; Taṇhāya mūlaṁ khaṇatha, usīratthova bīraṇaṁ; Mā vo naḷaṁva sotova, māro bhañji punappunaṁ.
english_sujato: I say this to you, good people, all those who have gathered here: dig up the root of craving, as you’d dig up grass in search of roots. Don’t let Māra break you again and again, like a stream breaking a reed.
interlinear_pali: Taṁ vo vadāmi: “Bhaddaṁ vo yāvantettha samāgatā”, taṇhāya mūlaṁ khaṇatha, usīrattho va bīraṇaṁ, mā vo naḷaṁ va soto va Māro bhañji punappunaṁ.
interlinear_english: This I say to you: “Good luck to as many as have assembled here”, dig up the root of craving, like one seeking the root (digs up) grass, do not let Māra push you down again like a stream (pushes down) the reed.
interlinear_notes: The commentary paraphrases with: usīrena atthiko.

pali_mahasangiti: Yathāpi mūle anupaddave daḷhe, Chinnopi rukkho punareva rūhati; Evampi taṇhānusaye anūhate, Nibbattatī dukkhamidaṁ punappunaṁ.
english_sujato: A tree grows back even when cut down, so long as its roots are strong and undamaged; suffering springs up again and again, so long as the tendency to craving is not pulled out.
interlinear_pali: Yathā pi mūle anupaddave daḷhe chinno pi rukkho, punar-eva rūhati, evam-pi taṇhānusaye anūhate nibbattatī dukkham-idaṁ punappunaṁ.
interlinear_english: Just as when the root remains firm and untroubled though the tree was cut down, it grows again, so when the tendency to craving is not rooted out this suffering appears again and again.
interlinear_notes: A locative absolutive construction.
narrative_pali: Yathā pi mūle anupaddave daḷhe chinno pi rukkho, punar-eva rūhati, evam-pi taṇhānusaye anūhate nibbattatī dukkham-idaṁ punappunaṁ.
narrative_english: Just as when the root remains untroubled though the tree was cut down, it grows again, so when craving is not rooted out, this suffering appears again and again.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa chattiṁsati sotā, manāpasavanā bhusā; Mahāvahanti duddiṭṭhiṁ, saṅkappā rāganissitā.
english_sujato: A person of low views in whom the thirty-six streams that flow to pleasure are mighty, is swept away by lustful thoughts.
interlinear_pali: Yassa chattiṁsatī sotā manāpassavanā bhusā, vāhā vahanti duddiṭṭhiṁ saṅkappā rāganissitā.
interlinear_english: He in whom the thirty-six streams flow pleasantly and strong, the one with wrong view, is carried away by his passionate intentions.
interlinear_notes: The number is arrived at by multiplying the types of craving (for pleasure, continuity and discontinuity) by the six internal and external sense spheres.

pali_mahasangiti: Savanti sabbadhi sotā, latā uppajja tiṭṭhati; Tañca disvā lataṁ jātaṁ, mūlaṁ paññāya chindatha.
english_sujato: The streams flow everywhere; a weed springs up and remains. Seeing this weed that has been born, cut the root with wisdom.
interlinear_pali: Savanti sabbadhī sotā, latā ubbhijja tiṭṭhati, tañ-ca disvā lataṁ jātaṁ mūlaṁ paññāya chindatha.
interlinear_english: Streams are flowing everywhere, the creepers remain where they grow, seeing this, cut the creeper’s root that has arisen with wisdom.

pali_mahasangiti: Saritāni sinehitāni ca, Somanassāni bhavanti jantuno; Te sātasitā sukhesino, Te ve jātijarūpagā narā.
english_sujato: A personage’s joys flow from senses and cravings. Seekers of happiness, bent on pleasure, continue to be reborn and grow old.
interlinear_pali: Saritāni sinehitāni ca sŏmanassāni bhavanti jantuno, te sātasitā sukhesino, te ve jātijarūpagā narā.
interlinear_english: * There are flowing streams of affection and mental happinesses for a person, pleasure-dependent they seek happiness, those people undergo both birth and old age.

pali_mahasangiti: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā, Parisappanti sasova bandhito; Saṁyojanasaṅgasattakā, Dukkhamupenti punappunaṁ cirāya.
english_sujato: People governed by thirst, crawl about like a trapped rabbit. Bound and fettered, for a long time they return to pain time and again.
interlinear_pali: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā parisappanti saso va bādhito, saṁyojanasaṅgasattakā dukkham-upenti punappunaṁ cirāya.
interlinear_english: People surrounded by craving crawl round like a hare in a trap, attached and clinging to fetters they come back again and again to suffering for a long time.
interlinear_notes: Often translated as runs around, but a hare in a trap isn’t running anywhere. Commentary paraphrases with saṁsappanti.

pali_mahasangiti: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā, Parisappanti sasova bandhito; Tasmā tasiṇaṁ vinodaye, Ākaṅkhanta virāgamattano.
english_sujato: People governed by thirst, crawl about like a trapped rabbit. That’s why one who longs for dispassion should dispel thirst.
interlinear_pali: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā parisappanti saso va bādhito, tasmā tasiṇaṁ vinodaye – bhikkhu ākaṅkha’ virāgam-attano.
interlinear_english: People surrounded by craving crawl round like a hare in a trap, therefore he should remove craving – the monk who longs for dispassion for himself.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo nibbanatho vanādhimutto, Vanamutto vanameva dhāvati; Taṁ puggalametha passatha, Mutto bandhanameva dhāvati.
english_sujato: Unsnarled, they set out for the jungle, then they run right back to the jungle they left behind. Just look at this individual! Freed, they run to bondage.
interlinear_pali: Yo nibbanatho vanādhimutto, vanamutto vanam-eva dhāvati, taṁ puggalam-etha passatha, mutto bandhanam-eva dhāvati.
interlinear_english: The one who is free from desires, who is intent on the forest, (though) free from the forest, runs back to the forest, come here and look at that person, (though) free, he runs back to bondage.
interlinear_notes: It is hard to get the meaning across without greatly expanding the translation, the forest is the forest of desires.

pali_mahasangiti: Na taṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanamāhu dhīrā, Yadāyasaṁ dārujapabbajañca; Sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu, Puttesu dāresu ca yā apekkhā.
english_sujato: The attentive say that shackle is not strong that’s made of iron, wood, or knots. But obsession with jeweled earrings, concern for your partners and children:
interlinear_pali: Na taṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanam-āhu dhīrā, yad-āyasaṁ dārujaṁ pabbajañ-ca, sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu puttesu dāresu ca yā apekhā –
interlinear_english: That bondage is not so strong say the wise, that is made of iron or wood or reeds, * impassioned and excited they seek out jewels and earrings and children and wives –

pali_mahasangiti: Etaṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanamāhu dhīrā, Ohārinaṁ sithilaṁ duppamuñcaṁ; Etampi chetvāna paribbajanti, Anapekkhino kāmasukhaṁ pahāya.
english_sujato: this, say the attentive, is a strong shackle dragging the indulgent down, hard to escape. Having cut this one too they go forth, unconcerned, having given up sensual pleasures.
interlinear_pali: etaṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanam-āhu dhīrā, ohārinaṁ sithilaṁ, duppamuñcaṁ, etam-pi chetvāna paribbajanti anapekkhino, kāmasukhaṁ pahāya.
interlinear_english: that bondage is strong say the wise, dragging down the lax, hard to get free from, having cut this down they wander about seeking nothing, abandoning the happiness in pleasure.

pali_mahasangiti: Ye rāgarattānupatanti sotaṁ, Sayaṅkataṁ makkaṭakova jālaṁ; Etampi chetvāna vajanti dhīrā, Anapekkhino sabbadukkhaṁ pahāya.
english_sujato: Besotted by lust they fall into the stream, like a spider caught in the web she wove. The attentive proceed, having cut this one too, unconcerned, having given up all suffering.
interlinear_pali: Ye rāgarattānupatanti sotaṁ sayaṁkataṁ makkaṭako va jālaṁ, etam-pi chetvāna vajanti dhīrā, anapekkhino sabbadukkhaṁ pahāya.
interlinear_english: Those who are impassioned by passion follow the stream like a spider a web made by itself, having cut this away the wise proceed, seeking nothing, abandoning all suffering.
narrative_pali: Ye rāgarattānupatanti sotaṁ sayaṁkataṁ makkaṭako va jālaṁ,

pali_mahasangiti: Muñca pure muñca pacchato, Majjhe muñca bhavassa pāragū; Sabbattha vimuttamānaso, Na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.
english_sujato: Let go of the past, let go of the future, let go of the present, having gone beyond rebirth. With your heart freed in every respect, you’ll not come again to rebirth and old age.
interlinear_pali: Muñca pure, muñca pacchato, majjhe muñca, bhavassa pāragū, sabbattha vimuttamānaso, na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.
interlinear_english: Be free of the past, be free of the future, be free of the present, after crossing over (all) existence, with mind liberated in every way, you will not return to birth and old age.

pali_mahasangiti: Vitakkamathitassa jantuno, Tibbarāgassa subhānupassino; Bhiyyo taṇhā pavaḍḍhati, Esa kho daḷhaṁ karoti bandhanaṁ.
english_sujato: For a personage churned by thoughts, very lustful, focusing on beauty, their craving grows and grows, tying them with a stout bond.
interlinear_pali: Vitakkapamathitassa jantuno tibbarāgassa, subhānupassino, bhiyyo taṇhā pavaḍḍhati, esa kho daḷhaṁ karoti bandhanaṁ.
interlinear_english: For a person crushed by thoughts and pierced by passion, contemplating the attractive, craving increases much more, this surely makes the bond more firm.

pali_mahasangiti: Vitakkūpasame ca yo rato, Asubhaṁ bhāvayate sadā sato; Esa kho byanti kāhiti, Esa checchati mārabandhanaṁ.
english_sujato: But one who loves to calm their thoughts, developing perception of ugliness, ever mindful, will surely eliminate that craving, cutting off the bonds of Māra.
interlinear_pali: Vitakkupasame ca yo rato asubhaṁ bhāvayatī sadā sato, esa kho vyantikāhiti, esacchecchati Mārabandhanaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever has delight in the calming of thoughts, who always mindfully cultivates what is unattractive, will surely abolish this (craving), he will cut off the bond of Māra.

pali_mahasangiti: Niṭṭhaṅgato asantāsī, vītataṇho anaṅgaṇo; Acchindi bhavasallāni, antimoyaṁ samussayo.
english_sujato: One who is confident, unafraid, rid of craving, free of blemish, having struck down the arrows flying to future lives, this bag of bones is their last.
interlinear_pali: Niṭṭhaṁ gato asantāsī, vītataṇho anaṅgaṇo, acchindi bhavasallāni, antimoyaṁ samussayo.
interlinear_english: Having gone to the end, without trembling, without craving, without impurity, cutting off the darts of existence, this one is his final body.
narrative_pali: Niṭṭhaṁ gato asantāsī, vītataṇho anaṅgaṇo, acchindi bhavasallāni, antimoyaṁ samussayo.
narrative_english: Having gone to the end, without

pali_mahasangiti: Vītataṇho anādāno, Niruttipadakovido; Akkharānaṁ sannipātaṁ, Jaññā pubbāparāni ca; Sa ve “antimasārīro, Mahāpañño mahāpuriso”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: Rid of craving, free of grasping, expert in the definition of terms, knowing the correct structure and sequence of syllables, they are said to be one who bears their final body, one of great wisdom, a great person.
interlinear_pali: Vītataṇho anādāno, niruttipadakovido, akkharānaṁ sannipātaṁ jaññā pubbaparāni ca, sa ve antimasārīro mahāpañño (mahāpuriso) ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: Without craving, without attachment, skilled in words and their explanation, knowing how syllables are arranged, which come before and which after, the one in his final body is said to be (a great person), one of great wisdom.

pali_mahasangiti: Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūhamasmi, Sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto; Sabbañjaho taṇhakkhaye vimutto, Sayaṁ abhiññāya kamuddiseyyaṁ.
english_sujato: I am the vanquisher of all, the knower of all, unsullied in the midst of all things. I’ve given up all, freed in the ending of craving. Since I know for myself, whose follower should I be?
interlinear_pali: Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūham-asmi, sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto, sabbañjaho taṇhakkhaye vimutto, sayaṁ abhiññāya, kam-uddiseyyaṁ.
interlinear_english: All-Conquering, All-Wise am I, undefiled regarding all things, having given up everything, liberated through craving’s destruction, when having deep knowledge myself, who should I point to (as Teacher)?
narrative_pali: Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūham-asmi, sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto, sabbañjaho taṇhakkhaye vimutto, sayaṁ abhiññāya, kam-uddiseyyaṁ.
narrative_english: All-Conquering, All-Wise am I, undefiled regarding all things,

pali_mahasangiti: Sabbadānaṁ dhammadānaṁ jināti, Sabbarasaṁ dhammaraso jināti; Sabbaratiṁ dhammarati jināti, Taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṁ jināti.
english_sujato: The gift of the teaching surmounts all other gifts; the taste of the teaching surmounts all other tastes; the joy of the teaching surmounts all other joys; the ending of craving surmounts all suffering.
interlinear_pali: Sabbadānaṁ Dhammadānaṁ jināti, sabbaṁ rasaṁ Dhammaraso jināti, sabbaṁ ratiṁ Dhammaratiṁ jināti, taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṁ jināti.
interlinear_english: The gift of the Dhamma surpasses all other gifts, the taste of the Dhamma surpasses all other tastes, the love of the Dhamma surpasses all other loves, destruction of craving overcomes all suffering.
narrative_pali: Sabbadānaṁ Dhammadānaṁ jināti, sabbaṁ rasaṁ Dhammaraso jināti, sabbaṁ ratiṁ Dhammaratiṁ jināti, taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṁ jināti.
narrative_english: The gift of the Dhamma surpasses other gifts, the taste of the Dhamma surpasses other tastes,

pali_mahasangiti: Hananti bhogā dummedhaṁ, no ca pāragavesino; Bhogataṇhāya dummedho, hanti aññeva attanaṁ.
english_sujato: Riches ruin a simpleton, but not a seeker of the far shore. From craving for wealth, a simpleton ruins themselves and others.
interlinear_pali: Hananti bhogā dummedhaṁ no ve pāragavesino, bhogataṇhāya dummedho hanti aññe va attanaṁ.
interlinear_english: Riches destroy the stupid one who does not seek the way beyond, through his craving for riches the stupid one destroys others and himself.

pali_mahasangiti: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, rāgadosā ayaṁ pajā; Tasmā hi vītarāgesu, dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english_sujato: Weeds are the bane of crops, but greed is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of greed is so very fruitful.
interlinear_pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, rāgadosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vītarāgesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
interlinear_english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by passion, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without passion.
narrative_pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, rāgadosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vītarāgesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
narrative_english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, people are ruined by passion, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without passion.

pali_mahasangiti: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, dosadosā ayaṁ pajā; Tasmā hi vītadosesu, dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english_sujato: Weeds are the bane of crops, but hate is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of hate is so very fruitful.
interlinear_pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, dosadosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vītadosesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
interlinear_english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by hatred, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without hatred.

pali_mahasangiti: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, mohadosā ayaṁ pajā; Tasmā hi vītamohesu, dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english_sujato: Weeds are the bane of crops, but delusion is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of delusion is so very fruitful.
interlinear_pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, mohadosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vītamohesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
interlinear_english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by delusion, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without delusion.

pali_mahasangiti: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, icchādosā ayaṁ pajā; Tasmā hi vigaticchesu, dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english_sujato: Weeds are the bane of crops, but desire is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of desire is so very fruitful.
interlinear_pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, icchādosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vigaticchesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
interlinear_english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by desire, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without desire.

pali_mahasangiti: Cakkhunā saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu sotena saṁvaro; Ghānena saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu jivhāya saṁvaro.
english_sujato: Restraint of the eye is good; good is restraint of the ear; restraint of the nose is good; good is restraint of the tongue.
interlinear_pali: Cakkhunā saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu sotena saṁvaro, ghāṇena saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu jivhāya saṁvaro,
interlinear_english: Restraint of eye is good, restraint of ear is good, restraint of nose is good, restraint of tongue is good,

pali_mahasangiti: Kāyena saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu vācāya saṁvaro; Manasā saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu sabbattha saṁvaro; Sabbattha saṁvuto bhikkhu, sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
english_sujato: Restraint of the body is good; good is restraint of speech; restraint of mind is good; everywhere, restraint is good. The mendicant restrained everywhere is released from all suffering.
interlinear_pali: kāyena saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu vācāya saṁvaro, manasā saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu sabbattha saṁvaro, sabbattha saṁvuto bhikkhu sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
interlinear_english: restraint of body is good, restraint of speech is good, restraint of mind is good, restraint is everywhere good, a monastic who is restrained everywhere is liberated from all suffering.
interlinear_notes: Note that restraint of body at this point forms a bridge between categories, on the one hand it is the last of the five-fold sense-spheres; and on the other it is the first of the three courses of action.

pali_mahasangiti: Hatthasaṁyato pādasaṁyato, Vācāsaṁyato saṁyatuttamo; Ajjhattarato samāhito, Eko santusito tamāhu bhikkhuṁ.
english_sujato: One restrained in hand and foot, and in speech, the supreme restraint; happy inside, serene, solitary, content, I call a mendicant.
interlinear_pali: Hatthasaṁyatŏ pādasaṁyato, vācāya saṁyatŏ saṁyatuttamo, ajjhattarato samāhito, eko santusito: tam-āhu bhikkhuṁ.
interlinear_english: One who controls his hands, controls his feet, controls his speech, controls the (mind) supreme, with inner delight and composure, solitary, content: that one is called a monastic.
interlinear_notes: The comm. explains it to mean one who personally delights in cultivating his meditation object.
narrative_pali: Hatthasaṁyatŏ pādasaṁyato, vācāya saṁyatŏ saṁyatuttamo, ajjhattarato samāhito, eko santusito: tam-āhu bhikkhuṁ.
narrative_english: One who controls his hands, controls his feet, controls his speech, controls the mind supreme, with delight, composure, solitary, content: that one do they call a bhikkhu.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo mukhasaṁyato bhikkhu, mantabhāṇī anuddhato; Atthaṁ dhammañca dīpeti, madhuraṁ tassa bhāsitaṁ.
english_sujato: When a mendicant of restrained mouth, thoughtful in counsel, not restless, explains the text and its meaning, their words are sweet.
interlinear_pali: Yo mukhasaṁyato bhikkhu, mantabhāṇī anuddhato, atthaṁ Dhammañ-ca dīpeti, madhuraṁ tassa bhāsitaṁ.
interlinear_english: That monastic who restrains the mouth, who speaks well, and who is modest, who explains the meaning of the Dhamma, his speech is sweet.

pali_mahasangiti: Dhammārāmo dhammarato, dhammaṁ anuvicintayaṁ; Dhammaṁ anussaraṁ bhikkhu, saddhammā na parihāyati.
english_sujato: Delighting in the teaching, enjoying the teaching, contemplating the teaching, a mendicant who recollects the teaching doesn’t fall away from the true teaching.
interlinear_pali: Dhammārāmo Dhammarato, Dhammaṁ anuvicintayaṁ, Dhammaṁ anussaraṁ bhikkhu, Saddhammā na parihāyati.
interlinear_english: The one who finds pleasure in the Dhamma, delights in Dhamma, reflects on Dhamma, the monastic who remembers Dhamma, does not abandon the Good Dhamma.

pali_mahasangiti: Salābhaṁ nātimaññeyya, nāññesaṁ pihayaṁ care; Aññesaṁ pihayaṁ bhikkhu, samādhiṁ nādhigacchati.
english_sujato: A well-off mendicant ought not look down on others, nor should they be envious. A mendicant who envies others does not achieve immersion.
interlinear_pali: Salābhaṁ nātimaññeyya, nāññesaṁ pihayaṁ care, aññesaṁ pihayaṁ bhikkhu samādhiṁ nādhigacchati.
interlinear_english: One should not despise one’s own gains, one should not live envious of others, the monastic who is envious of others does not attain concentration.
narrative_pali: Salābhaṁ nātimaññeyya, nāññesaṁ pihayaṁ care, aññesaṁ pihayaṁ bhikkhu samādhiṁ nādhigacchati.
narrative_english: One should not despise one’s own gains, don’t live envious of others, the bhikkhu who is envious does not attain concentration.

pali_mahasangiti: Appalābhopi ce bhikkhu, salābhaṁ nātimaññati; Taṁ ve devā pasaṁsanti, suddhājīviṁ atanditaṁ.
english_sujato: If a mendicant is poor in offerings, the well-to-do ought not look down on them. For the gods indeed praise them, who are tireless and pure of livelihood.
interlinear_pali: Appalābho pi ce bhikkhu salābhaṁ nātimaññati, taṁ ve devā pasaṁsanti suddhājīviṁ atanditaṁ.
interlinear_english: Even if a monastic gains little he should not despise his gains, even the very gods praise the one of pure life who is diligent.

pali_mahasangiti: Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṁ, yassa natthi mamāyitaṁ; Asatā ca na socati, sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: One who has no sense of ownership in the whole realm of name and form, who does not grieve for that which is not, is said to be a mendicant.
interlinear_pali: Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṁ yassa natthi mamāyitaṁ, asatā ca na socati, sa ve bhikkhū ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: The one who does not have fondness at all for mind and body, and who grieves not for what does not exist, is surely called a monastic.
narrative_pali: Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṁ yassa natthi mamāyitaṁ, asatā ca na socati, sa ve bhikkhū ti vuccati.
narrative_english: The one who does not have fondness at all for mind and body, who grieves not for what does not exist, he is surely called a bhikkhu.

pali_mahasangiti: Mettāvihārī yo bhikkhu, pasanno buddhasāsane; Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: A mendicant who meditates on love, devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, would realize the peaceful state, the blissful stilling of conditions.
interlinear_pali: Mettāvihārī yo bhikkhu, pasanno Buddhasāsane, adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: That monastic who dwells in loving-kindness, with faith in Buddha’s dispensation, should attain the state of peace, the joy in stilling of (all) conditions.
narrative_pali: Mettāvihārī yo bhikkhu, pasanno Buddhasāsane, adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.
narrative_english: That bhikkhu who lives with loving-kindness, with faith in the Buddha’s dispensation, should surely attain to the state of peace, the joy in the stilling of conditions.

pali_mahasangiti: Siñca bhikkhu imaṁ nāvaṁ, sittā te lahumessati; Chetvā rāgañca dosañca, tato nibbānamehisi.
english_sujato: Bail out this boat, mendicant! When bailed out it will float lightly. Having cut off desire and hate, you shall reach extinguishment.
interlinear_pali: Siñca bhikkhu imaṁ nāvaṁ, sittā te lahum-essati, chetvā rāgañ-ca dosañ-ca, tato Nibbānam-ehisi.
interlinear_english: Please bail out this boat, monastic, when bailed out it will go lightly, cutting off passion and hatred, from here one will go to Nibbāna.

pali_mahasangiti: Pañca chinde pañca jahe, pañca cuttari bhāvaye; Pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu, “oghatiṇṇo”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: Five to cut, five to drop, and five more to develop. When a mendicant slips five chains they’re said to have crossed the flood.
interlinear_pali: Pañca chinde, pañca jahe, pañca cuttaribhāvaye, pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu oghatiṇṇo ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: One should cut off five, one should abandon five, one should cultivate five more, the monastic who surmounts five attachments is called a flood-crosser.
interlinear_notes: The comm. explains it thus: one should cut off the five lower destinations, abandon the five lower fetters, cultivate five spiritual faculties; the five attachments are through passion, hatred, delusion, conceit and views.

pali_mahasangiti: Jhāya bhikkhu mā pamādo, Mā te kāmaguṇe ramessu cittaṁ; Mā lohaguḷaṁ gilī pamatto, Mā kandi “dukkhamidan”ti dayhamāno.
english_sujato: Practice absorption, don’t be negligent! Don’t let the mind delight in the senses! Don’t heedlessly swallow a hot iron ball! And when it burns, don’t cry, “Oh, the pain!”
interlinear_pali: Jhāya, bhikkhu, mā ca pāmado, mā te kāmaguṇe bhamassu cittaṁ, mā lohaguḷaṁ gilī, pamatto, mā kandi: ‘Dukkham-idan’-ti ḍayhamāno.
interlinear_english: Meditate, monastic, do not be heedless, do not let your mind swirl around in strands of desire, do not, heedless, swallow a (hot) iron ball, do not, while burning, cry: ‘This is suffering.’

pali_mahasangiti: Natthi jhānaṁ apaññassa, paññā natthi ajhāyato; Yamhi jhānañca paññā ca, sa ve nibbānasantike.
english_sujato: No absorption for one without wisdom, no wisdom for one without absorption. But one with absorption and wisdom— they have truly drawn near to extinguishment.
interlinear_pali: Natthi jhānaṁ apaññassa, paññā natthi ajhāyato, yamhi jhānañ-ca paññā ca sa ve Nibbānasantike.
interlinear_english: There is no concentration for one without wisdom, there is no wisdom for one without concentration, the one who has both concentration and wisdom is indeed in the presence of Nibbāna.

pali_mahasangiti: Suññāgāraṁ paviṭṭhassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno; Amānusī rati hoti, sammā dhammaṁ vipassato.
english_sujato: A mendicant who enters an empty hut with mind at peace finds a superhuman delight as they rightly discern the Dhamma.
interlinear_pali: Suññāgāraṁ paviṭṭhassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno, amānusī ratī hoti sammā Dhammaṁ vipassato.
interlinear_english: For the one who has entered an empty place, a monastic with a peaceful mind, there is superhuman delight from insight into true Dhamma.

pali_mahasangiti: Yato yato sammasati, khandhānaṁ udayabbayaṁ; Labhatī pītipāmojjaṁ, amataṁ taṁ vijānataṁ.
english_sujato: Whenever they are mindful of the rise and fall of the aggregates, they feel rapture and joy: that is freedom from death for one who knows.
interlinear_pali: Yato yato sammasati khandhānaṁ udayabbayaṁ labhatī pītipāmojjaṁ, amataṁ taṁ vijānataṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever has right mindfulness regarding the rise and fall of the components (of mind and body) gains joy and happiness, that is the deathless state for the one who knows.

pali_mahasangiti: Tatrāyamādi bhavati, idha paññassa bhikkhuno; Indriyagutti santuṭṭhi, pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro.
english_sujato: This is the very start of the path for a wise mendicant here: guarding the senses, contentment, and restraint in the monastic code.
interlinear_pali: Tatrāyam-ādi bhavati idha paññassa bhikkhuno: indriyagutti santuṭṭhī: pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro.
interlinear_english: This is the very beginning for the wise monastic here: contentment, guarding the senses, and restraint in the regulations.

pali_mahasangiti: Mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe, suddhājīve atandite; Paṭisanthāravutyassa, ācārakusalo siyā; Tato pāmojjabahulo, dukkhassantaṁ karissati.
english_sujato: Mix with spiritual friends, who are tireless and pure of livelihood. Share what you have with others, being skillful in your conduct. And when you’re full of joy, you’ll make an end to suffering.
interlinear_pali: Mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe suddhājīve atandite, paṭisanthāravuttassa ācārakusalo siyā, tato pāmojjabahulo, dukkhassantaṁ karissati.
interlinear_english: One should resort to spiritual friends, ones of pure life, ones who are diligent, one should be of friendly disposition, one who will be skilful in his conduct, rejoicing frequently because of that, one will make an end to suffering.

pali_mahasangiti: Vassikā viya pupphāni, maddavāni pamuñcati; Evaṁ rāgañca dosañca, vippamuñcetha bhikkhavo.
english_sujato: As a jasmine sheds its withered flowers, O mendicants, shed greed and hate.
interlinear_pali: Vassikā viya pupphāni maddavāni pamuñcati, evaṁ rāgañ-ca dosañ-ca vippamuñcetha bhikkhavo.
interlinear_english: Just as striped jasmine casts off its withered flowers, so, monastics, cast off (all) passion and hatred.
narrative_pali: Vassikā viya pupphāni maddavāni pamuñcati, evaṁ rāgañ-ca dosañ-ca vippamuñcetha bhikkhavo.
narrative_english: Just as striped jasmine casts off its withered flowers, just so, bhikkhus, cast off all passion and hatred.

pali_mahasangiti: Santakāyo santavāco, santavā susamāhito; Vantalokāmiso bhikkhu, “upasanto”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: Calm in body, calm in speech, peaceful and serene; a mendicant who’s spat out the world’s bait is said to be one at peace.
interlinear_pali: Santakāyo santavāco, santavā susamāhito, vantalokāmiso bhikkhu upasanto ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: Calm in body and calm in speech, having calmness and composure, having thrown off worldly gain the monastic is called one at peace.
narrative_pali: Santakāyo santavāco, santavā susamāhito, vantalokāmiso bhikkhu upasanto ti vuccati.
narrative_english: Calm in body and calm in speech, having calmness and composure,

pali_mahasangiti: Attanā codayattānaṁ, paṭimaṁsetha attanā; So attagutto satimā, sukhaṁ bhikkhu vihāhisi.
english_sujato: Urge yourself on, reflect on yourself. A mendicant self-controlled and mindful will always dwell in happiness.
interlinear_pali: Attanā codayattānaṁ, paṭimāsettam-attanā, so attagutto satimā sukhaṁ bhikkhu vihāhisi.
interlinear_english: By oneself one should censure self, by oneself one should be controlled, he who guards himself, mindful, will live happily, monastic.
narrative_pali: Attanā codayattānaṁ, paṭimāsettam-attanā,
narrative_english: so attagutto satimā sukhaṁ bhikkhu vihāhisi. By oneself one should censure self, by oneself one should be controlled, the one who guards himself, mindful, that bhikkhu will live happily.

pali_mahasangiti: Attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā; Attā hi attano gati, tasmā saṁyamamattānaṁ; Assaṁ bhadraṁva vāṇijo.
english_sujato: Self is indeed the lord of self, for who else would be one’s lord? Self is indeed the home of self, so restrain yourself, as a merchant his thoroughbred steed.
interlinear_pali: Attā hi attano nātho, attā hi attano gati, tasmā saṁyamayattānaṁ assaṁ bhadraṁ va vāṇijo.
interlinear_english: Self is the protector of self, self is the refuge of self, therefore one should restrain oneself, as a merchant his noble horse.
interlinear_notes: Not given in this meaning in PED, it is noticed by DP.

pali_mahasangiti: Pāmojjabahulo bhikkhu, pasanno buddhasāsane; Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.
english_sujato: A monk full of joy trusting in the Buddha’s teaching, would realize the peaceful state, the blissful stilling of conditions.
interlinear_pali: Pāmojjabahulo bhikkhu, pasanno Buddhasāsane, adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.
interlinear_english: The monastic, having much happiness, with faith in the dispensation of the Buddha, could attain to the state of peace, happy in the stilling of (all) conditions.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo have daharo bhikkhu, yuñjati buddhasāsane; Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.
english_sujato: A young mendicant devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, lights up the world, like the moon freed from clouds.
interlinear_pali: Yo have daharo bhikkhu yuñjati Buddhasāsane, sŏ imaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti, abbhā mutto va candimā.
interlinear_english: That young monastic who is devoted to the Buddha’s dispensation, shines forth in this world, like the moon freed from a cloud.

pali_mahasangiti: Chinda sotaṁ parakkamma, kāme panuda brāhmaṇa; Saṅkhārānaṁ khayaṁ ñatvā, akataññūsi brāhmaṇa.
english_sujato: Cut the stream, striving! Cast aside sensual pleasures, brahmin. Knowing the ending of conditions, know the uncreated, brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Chinda sotaṁ parakkamma, kāme panuda, brāhmaṇa, saṅkhārānaṁ khayaṁ ñatvā, akataññūsi, brāhmaṇa.
interlinear_english: Strive and cut off the stream, remove desire, brahmin, knowing the destruction of the conditioned, be one who knows that which is not made, brahmin.
interlinear_notes: What is not made is Nibbāna.
narrative_pali: Chinda sotaṁ parakkamma, kāme panuda, brāhmaṇa, saṅkhārānaṁ khayaṁ ñatvā, akataññūsi, brāhmaṇa.
narrative_english: Strive and cut off the stream, remove desire, Brahmin, knowing the destruction of the conditioned, know that which is not made, Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yadā dvayesu dhammesu, pāragū hoti brāhmaṇo; Athassa sabbe saṁyogā, atthaṁ gacchanti jānato.
english_sujato: When a brahmin has gone beyond dualistic phenomena, then they consciously make an end of all fetters.
interlinear_pali: Yadā dvayesu dhammesu pāragū hoti brāhmaṇo, athassa sabbe saṁyogā atthaṁ gacchanti jānato.
interlinear_english: When a brahmin has, through two things, crossed over, then, for one who knows, all the fetters are laid to rest.
interlinear_notes: I.e. calmness (samatha) and insight (vipassanā).
narrative_pali: Yadā dvayesu dhammesu pāragū hoti brāhmaṇo, athassa sabbe saṁyogā atthaṁ gacchanti jānato.
narrative_english: When a Brahmin has, through two states, crossed over, then for one who knows, all his fetters are laid to rest.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa pāraṁ apāraṁ vā, pārāpāraṁ na vijjati; Vītaddaraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: One for whom there is no crossing over or crossing back, or crossing over and back; stress-free, detached, that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yassa pāraṁ apāraṁ vā pārāpāraṁ na vijjati, vītaddaraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: For whom the near shore, the far shore or both do not exist, free of anxiety, being detached, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Yassa pāraṁ apāraṁ vā pārāpāraṁ na vijjati, vītaddaraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: For whom the near shore, the far shore, or both do not exist, free of

pali_mahasangiti: Jhāyiṁ virajamāsīnaṁ, katakiccamanāsavaṁ; Uttamatthamanuppattaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Absorbed, rid of hopes, their task completed, without defilements, arrived at the highest goal: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Jhāyiṁ virajam-āsīnaṁ, katakiccaṁ anāsavaṁ, uttamatthaṁ anuppattaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: The meditator sitting down, the one who is dustless, who has done his duty, without pollutants, who has reached the ultimate good, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Jhāyiṁ virajam-āsīnaṁ, katakiccaṁ anāsavaṁ, uttamatthaṁ anuppattaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: The meditator sitting down, dustless, who has done his duty, without pollutants, who has reached the supreme good, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Divā tapati ādicco, rattimābhāti candimā; Sannaddho khattiyo tapati, jhāyī tapati brāhmaṇo; Atha sabbamahorattiṁ, buddho tapati tejasā.
english_sujato: The sun blazes by day, the moon radiates at night, the aristocrat shines in armor, and the brahmin shines in absorption. But all day and all night, the Buddha blazes with glory.
interlinear_pali: Divā tapati ādicco, rattiṁābhāti candimā, sannaddho khattiyo tapati, jhāyī tapati brāhmaṇo, atha sabbam-ahorattiṁ Buddho tapati tejasā.
interlinear_english: The sun is radiant by day, the moon shines by night, the accoutred noble is radiant, the meditating brahmin is radiant, yet every day and night the Buddha is radiant through his power.
narrative_pali: Divā tapati ādicco, rattiṁ ābhāti candimā, sannaddho khattiyo tapati, jhāyī tapati brāhmaṇo, atha sabbam-ahorattiṁ Buddho tapati tejasā.
narrative_english: The sun shines by day, the moon shines by night, the accoutred noble is radiant, the meditating Brahmin’s radiant, then every day and night the Buddha is radiant through his shining power.

pali_mahasangiti: Bāhitapāpoti brāhmaṇo, Samacariyā samaṇoti vuccati; Pabbājayamattano malaṁ, Tasmā “pabbajito”ti vuccati.
english_sujato: A brahmin’s so-called <j>since they’ve banished evil, an ascetic’s so-called <j>since they live a serene life. One who has renounced all stains is said to be a “renunciant”.
interlinear_pali: Bāhitapāpo ti brāhmaṇo, samacariyā samaṇo ti vuccati, pabbājayam-attano malaṁ tasmā pabbajito ti vuccati.
interlinear_english: Warding off wickedness one is called a brahmin, one living austerely is said to be an ascetic, * because of driving forth (all) stain from oneself one is said to be one who has gone forth.
interlinear_notes: It is difficult to make the puns in this verse, which rely on similarity of sound, rather than etymology, work in English.
narrative_pali: Bāhitapāpo ti brāhmaṇo, samacariyā samaṇo ti vuccati, pabbājayam-attano malaṁ tasmā pabbajito ti vuccati.
narrative_english: Warding wickedness one’s called a Brahmin, an austere one is called an ascetic,

pali_mahasangiti: Na brāhmaṇassa pahareyya, nāssa muñcetha brāhmaṇo; Dhī brāhmaṇassa hantāraṁ, tato dhī yassa muñcati.
english_sujato: One should never strike a brahmin, nor should a brahmin retaliate. Woe to the one who hurts a brahmin, and woe for the one who retaliates.
interlinear_pali: Na brāhmaṇassa pahareyya, nāssa muñcetha brāhmaṇo, dhī brāhmaṇassa hantāraṁ, tato: dhī yassa muñcati.
interlinear_english: A brahmin should not hit a brahmin, nor should he abandon him, woe to the one who strikes a brahmin, further: woe to the one who abandons him.
narrative_pali: Na brāhmaṇassa pahareyya, nāssa muñcetha brāhmaṇo, dhī brāhmaṇassa hantāraṁ, tato: dhī yassa muñcati.
narrative_english: A Brahmin shouldn’t hit a Brahmin and nor should he abandon him,

pali_mahasangiti: Na brāhmaṇassetadakiñci seyyo, Yadā nisedho manaso piyehi; Yato yato hiṁsamano nivattati, Tato tato sammatimeva dukkhaṁ.
english_sujato: Nothing is better for a brahmin than to hold their mind back from attachment. From wherever a cruel wish recoils, right there suffering subsides.
interlinear_pali: Na brāhmaṇass’ etad-akiñci seyyo: yadā nisedho manaso piyehi, yato yato hiṁsamano nivattati, tato tato sammati-m-eva dukkhaṁ.
interlinear_english: It is no little good for the brahmin: when the mind is held back from what is dear, whenever his mind turns back from violence, then there is a calming of suffering.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa kāyena vācāya, manasā natthi dukkaṭaṁ; Saṁvutaṁ tīhi ṭhānehi, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Who does nothing wrong by body, speech or mind, restrained in these three respects, that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yassa kāyena vācāya manasā natthi dukkataṁ, saṁvutaṁ tīhi ṭhānehi, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: For whom there is no wrong-doing bodily, verbally or mentally, being restrained in (these) three things, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Yassa kāyena vācāya manasā natthi dukkataṁ, saṁvutaṁ tīhi ṭhānehi, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: For whom there is no wrong-doing by body, by voice or by mind, being restrained in these three things, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yamhā dhammaṁ vijāneyya, sammāsambuddhadesitaṁ; Sakkaccaṁ taṁ namasseyya, aggihuttaṁva brāhmaṇo.
english_sujato: You should graciously honor the one from whom you learn the Dhamma taught by the awakened Buddha, as a brahmin honors the sacred flame.
interlinear_pali: Yamhā Dhammaṁ vijāneyya Sammāsambuddhadesitaṁ, sakkaccaṁ taṁ namasseyya, aggihuttaṁ va brāhmaṇo.
interlinear_english: That one from whom one learned Dhamma taught by the Perfect Sambuddha, with respect bow down to him, like brahmin (bows) at fire-sacrifice.
narrative_pali: Yamhā Dhammaṁ vijāneyya Sammāsambuddhadesitaṁ, sakkaccaṁ taṁ namasseyya, aggihuttaṁ va brāhmaṇo.
narrative_english: That one from whom one learned Dhamma taught by the Perfect Sambuddha, with respect you should honour him, like Brahmin at fire-sacrifice.

pali_mahasangiti: Na jaṭāhi na gottena, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo; Yamhi saccañca dhammo ca, so sucī so ca brāhmaṇo.
english_sujato: Not by matted hair or family, or birth is one a brahmin. Those who are  truthful and principled: they are pure, they are brahmins.
interlinear_pali: Na jaṭāhi na gottena, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo, yamhi saccañ-ca Dhammo ca, so sucī so va brāhmaṇo.
interlinear_english: Not because of matted hair, family or birth is one a true brahmin, in whom there is truth and Dhamma, that one is pure, that one is surely a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Na jaṭāhi na gottena, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo,
narrative_english: yamhi saccañ-ca Dhammo ca, so sucī so va brāhmaṇo. Not because of matted hair, family or birth is one a true Brahmin, in whom there is truth and Dhamma, that one is pure, and a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Kiṁ te jaṭāhi dummedha, kiṁ te ajinasāṭiyā; Abbhantaraṁ te gahanaṁ, bāhiraṁ parimajjasi.
english_sujato: Why the matted hair, you simpleton, and why the skin of deer? The tangle is inside you, yet you polish up your outsides.
interlinear_pali: Kiṁ te jaṭāhi dummedha, kiṁ te ajinasāṭiyā? Abbhantaraṁ te gahanaṁ, bāhiraṁ parimajjasi.
interlinear_english: Why do you have your hair matted, stupid one, and why your deer-skin? Within you there is a jungle, you (only) polish the outside.
interlinear_notes: Comm: a jungle of defilements.
narrative_pali: Kiṁ te jaṭāhi dummedha, kiṁ te ajinasāṭiyā? Abbhantaraṁ te gahanaṁ, bāhiraṁ parimajjasi.
narrative_english: Why do you have your hair matted, stupid one, and why your deer-skin? Within you there is a jungle, you only polish the outside.

pali_mahasangiti: Paṁsukūladharaṁ jantuṁ, kisaṁ dhamanisanthataṁ; Ekaṁ vanasmiṁ jhāyantaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: A personage who wears robes of rags, lean, their limbs showing veins, meditating alone in the forest, that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Paṁsukūladharaṁ jantuṁ, kisaṁ dhamanisanthataṁ, ekaṁ vanasmiṁ jhāyantaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: That one who wears discarded clothes, who is lean with protruding veins, who meditates alone in the forest, that one I say is a brahmin.
interlinear_notes: Her name means the lean (Kisā) Gotamī.
This statement, which occurred also in vs. 385, 386 & 391 now becomes the refrain in all the remaining verses.
narrative_pali: Paṁsukūladharaṁ jantuṁ, kisaṁ dhamanisanthataṁ, ekaṁ vanasmiṁ jhāyantaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: That one who wears discarded clothes, who is lean with protruding veins, who meditates in the forest, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Na cāhaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ brūmi, yonijaṁ mattisambhavaṁ; Bhovādi nāma so hoti, sace hoti sakiñcano; Akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: I don’t call someone a brahmin after the mother’s womb they’re born from. If they still have attachments, they’re just someone who says “worthy”. Having nothing, taking nothing: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Na cāhaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ brūmi yonijaṁ mattisambhavaṁ, bhovādī nāma so hoti sace hoti sakiñcano; akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: I do not call one a brahmin simply because of being born from a (certain) womb, that one is just one who says ‘bho’ if he is attached; having nothing and unattached, that one I say is a brahmin.
interlinear_notes: From here to the end all the verses are drawn from Vāseṭṭhasutta (MN 98 and Sn 3.9); it is worth noting that this chapter is exceptionally long, and the parallel collections are much shorter.
It was a way for brahmins to address non-brahmins, implying their inferiority.
narrative_pali: Na cāhaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ brūmi yonijaṁ mattisambhavaṁ,
narrative_english: bhovādī nāma so hoti sace hoti sakiñcano;

pali_mahasangiti: Sabbasaṁyojanaṁ chetvā, yo ve na paritassati; Saṅgātigaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Having cut off all fetters they have no anxiety. They’ve slipped their chains and are detached: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Sabbasaṁyojanaṁ chetvā yo ve na paritassati, saṅgātigaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever has cut off all the fetters surely does not tremble, surmounting attachments, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Chetvā naddhiṁ varattañca, sandānaṁ sahanukkamaṁ; Ukkhittapalighaṁ buddhaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They’ve cut the strap and harness, the halter and bridle too, with cross-bar lifted, they’re awakened: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Chetvā naddhiṁ varattañ-ca, sandānaṁ sahanukkamaṁ, ukkhittapalighaṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: (Whoever) has cut off the thong, the strap, the rope, together with the bridle, who has thrown off the obstacle and is awakened, that one I say is a brahmin.
interlinear_notes: The commentary interprets the meaning as follows: Whoever has cut off hatred, craving, the sixty-two views together with the latent tendencies, and thrown off ignorance, that one I call a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Chetvā naddhiṁ varattañ-ca, sandānaṁ sahanukkamaṁ, ukkhittapalighaṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever has cut off the thong, the strap, the rope, together with

pali_mahasangiti: Akkosaṁ vadhabandhañca, aduṭṭho yo titikkhati; Khantībalaṁ balānīkaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Abuse, killing, caging: they endure these without anger. Patience is their powerful army: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Akkosaṁ vadhabandhañ-ca aduṭṭho yo titikkhati, khantībalaṁ balānīkaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever, being pure, forbears with punishment, bondage and abuse, having the strength of endurance, having an army of strengths,, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Akkodhanaṁ vatavantaṁ, sīlavantaṁ anussadaṁ; Dantaṁ antimasārīraṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Not irritable or pretentious, dutiful in precepts and observances, tamed, bearing their final body: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Akkodhanaṁ vatavantaṁ, sīlavantaṁ anussutaṁ, dantaṁ antimasārīraṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: (Whoever is) controlled of mind, dutiful, virtuous, taint-free, well-trained and in his last body, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Vāri pokkharapatteva, āraggeriva sāsapo; Yo na limpati kāmesu, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Like water from a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed off the point of a pin, sensual pleasures slip off them: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Vāri pokkharapatte va, āragge-r-iva sāsapo, yo na lippati kāmesu, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Like water on the lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on a needle, he who is unsmeared by desires, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yo dukkhassa pajānāti, idheva khayamattano; Pannabhāraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They understand for themselves the end of suffering in this life; with burden put down, detached: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yo dukkhassa pajānāti idheva khayam-attano, pannabhāraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever knows right here the destruction of his suffering, putting down the burden, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Gambhīrapaññaṁ medhāviṁ, maggāmaggassa kovidaṁ; Uttamatthamanuppattaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Deep in wisdom, intelligent, expert in the path and what is not the path; arrived at the highest goal: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Gambhīrapaññaṁ medhāviṁ, maggāmaggassa kovidaṁ, uttamatthaṁ anuppattaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: The deeply wise sagacious one, skilled in what is path and not path, who has reached the ultimate good, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Gambhīrapaññaṁ medhāviṁ, maggāmaggassa kovidaṁ,

pali_mahasangiti: Asaṁsaṭṭhaṁ gahaṭṭhehi, anāgārehi cūbhayaṁ; Anokasārimappicchaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Mixing with neither householders nor the homeless; a migrant with no bastion, few in wishes: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Asaṁsaṭṭhaṁ gahaṭṭhehi anāgārehi cūbhayaṁ, anokasāriṁ appicchaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: (Whoever) doesn’t mix with either householders or the houseless, wandering homeless, with few desires, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Asaṁsaṭṭhaṁ gahaṭṭhehi anāgārehi cūbhayaṁ, anokasāriṁ appicchaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever does not mix with the householders or the houseless, wand’ring homeless, with few desires, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Nidhāya daṇḍaṁ bhūtesu, tasesu thāvaresu ca; Yo na hanti na ghāteti, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They’ve laid aside violence against creatures firm and frail; not killing or making others kill: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Nidhāya daṇḍaṁ bhūtesu tasesu thāvaresu ca, yo na hanti na ghāteti, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: * Whoever has laid down the stick (used) against fearful and fearless beings, who neither hurts nor kills, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Nidhāya daṇḍaṁ bhūtesu tasesu thāvaresu ca, yo na hanti na ghāteti, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever has laid down the stick used against fearful and fearless beings, who neither hurts nor kills, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Aviruddhaṁ viruddhesu, attadaṇḍesu nibbutaṁ; Sādānesu anādānaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Not fighting among those who fight, quenched among those who have taken up arms, not grasping among those who grasp: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Aviruddhaṁ viruddhesu, attadaṇḍesu nibbutaṁ, sādānesu anādānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Being friendly with the hostile, calm amongst those holding a stick, not attached amongst those attached, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Aviruddhaṁ viruddhesu, attadaṇḍesu nibbutaṁ, sādānesu anādānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Being friendly with the hostile, calm amongst those holding a stick,

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa rāgo ca doso ca, māno makkho ca pātito; Sāsaporiva āraggā, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They’ve discarded greed and hate, along with conceit and contempt, like a mustard seed off the point of a pin: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yassa rāgo ca doso ca māno makkho ca pātito, sāsapo-r-iva āraggā, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever has dropped off passion and hatred, conceit and anger, like a mustard seed from a needle, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Akakkasaṁ viññāpaniṁ, giraṁ saccamudīraye; Yāya nābhisaje kañci, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: The words they utter are polished, informative, and true, and don’t offend anyone: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Akakkasaṁ viññapaniṁ giraṁ saccaṁ udīraye, yāya nābhisaje kañci, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: (Whoever) speaks a word of truth that is informed and is not coarse, through which no one would be angry, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Akakkasaṁ viññapaniṁ giraṁ saccaṁ udīraye, yāya nābhisaje kañci, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever speaks a word of truth that is informed and is not coarse, through which no one would be angry, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yodha dīghaṁ va rassaṁ vā, aṇuṁ thūlaṁ subhāsubhaṁ; Loke adinnaṁ nādiyati, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They don’t steal anything in the world, long or short, tiny or huge, beautiful or ugly: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yodha dīghaṁ va rassaṁ vā aṇuṁ-thūlaṁ subhāsubhaṁ, loke adinnaṁ nādiyati, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: * Whoever in the world does not take what is not given, long, short, small, large, attractive or unattractive, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Yodha dīghaṁ va rassaṁ vā aṇuṁ-thūlaṁ subhāsubhaṁ, loke adinnaṁ nādiyati, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever here does not take what is not given, long, short, small, large, attractive or unattractive, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Āsā yassa na vijjanti, asmiṁ loke paramhi ca; Nirāsāsaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They have no hope in this world or the next; with no need for hope, detached: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Āsā yassa na vijjanti asmiṁ loke paramhi ca, nirāsayaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: For the one who has no longings in this world or in the next world, being without longings, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassālayā na vijjanti, aññāya akathaṅkathī; Amatogadhamanuppattaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They have no clinging, knowledge has freed them of indecision, they’ve arrived at the objective, freedom from death: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yassālayā na vijjanti, aññāya akathaṅkathī, amatogadhaṁ anuppattaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: For the one who has no desires, who, through knowledge, is without doubt, who has reached immersion in the deathless, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Yassālayā na vijjanti, aññāya akathaṅkathī, amatogadhaṁ anuppattaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: For the one who has no desires, who, through knowledge, is without doubt, who has reached unto the deathless, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yodha puññañca pāpañca, ubho saṅgamupaccagā; Asokaṁ virajaṁ suddhaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They’ve escaped the chain of both good and bad deeds; sorrowless, stainless, pure: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yodha puññañ-ca pāpañ-ca ubho saṅgaṁ upaccagā, asokaṁ virajaṁ suddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever here has overcome clinging to both merit and demerit, who is griefless, dustless and pure, that one I say is a brahmin.
interlinear_notes: In the Majjhima commentary to Vāseṭṭhasuttaṁ pāpaṁ here is defined as apuññaṁ, which I follow in the translation.
narrative_pali: Yodha puññañ-ca pāpañ-ca ubho saṅgaṁ upaccagā, asokaṁ virajaṁ suddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever here has overcome clinging to merit, demerit, who is griefless, dustless and pure, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Candaṁva vimalaṁ suddhaṁ, vippasannamanāvilaṁ; Nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Pure as the spotless moon, clear and undisturbed, they’ve ended relish for rebirth: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Candaṁ va vimalaṁ suddhaṁ, vippasannam-anāvilaṁ, nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: (Whoever) just like the moon is stainless, pure, clear and undisturbed, has destroyed joy in existence, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Candaṁ va vimalaṁ suddhaṁ, vippasannam-anāvilaṁ, nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever, just like the moon, is stainless, pure, clear, undisturbed, and has destroyed joy in existence, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yomaṁ palipathaṁ duggaṁ, saṁsāraṁ mohamaccagā; Tiṇṇo pāraṅgato jhāyī, anejo akathaṅkathī; Anupādāya nibbuto, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They’ve got past this grueling swamp of delusion, transmigration. Meditating in stillness, free of indecision, they have crossed over to the far shore. They’re quenched by not grasping: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yo imaṁ palipathaṁ duggaṁ saṁsāraṁ moham-accagā, tiṇṇo pāragato jhāyī, anejo akathaṅkathī, anupādāya nibbuto, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: He who has crossed the difficult and dangerous path through births and deaths and delusion, the meditator who has crossed over to the further shore, free of lust and free of doubt, unattached and cooled down, that one I say is a brahmin.
interlinear_notes: The commentary says: Whoever has overcome the difficult path of passions and so forth, the inaccessible defilements, the round of births and deaths, the delusion of not having penetrated the four noble truths.
narrative_pali: Yo imaṁ palipathaṁ duggaṁ saṁsāraṁ moham-accagā, tiṇṇo pāragato jhāyī, anejo akathaṅkathī, anupādāya nibbuto, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: He who has crossed the difficult path through births, deaths and delusion, the meditator, crossed over to the further shore, free of lust and doubt, unattached and cooled down, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yodha kāme pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje; Kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They’ve given up sensual pleasures, and have gone forth from lay life; they’ve ended rebirth in the sensual realm: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yodha kāme pahatvāna anāgāro paribbaje, kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever, giving up sensual desires, would wander homeless here, destroying desires and existence, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Yodha kāme pahatvāna anāgāro paribbaje, kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ. Whoever, giving up desires,
narrative_english: would wander homeless in the world,

pali_mahasangiti: Yodha taṇhaṁ pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje; Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ. Yodha taṇhaṁ pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje; Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They’ve given up craving, and have gone forth from lay life; they’ve ended craving to be reborn: that’s who I declare a brahmin. They’ve given up craving, and have gone forth from lay life; they’ve ended craving to be reborn: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yodha taṇhaṁ pahatvāna, anāgāro paribbaje, taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever, giving up craving, would wander homeless here, destroying craving and existence, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Yodha taṇhaṁ pahatvāna, anāgāro paribbaje, taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ. Whoever, giving up craving,
narrative_english: would wander homeless in this world,

pali_mahasangiti: Hitvā mānusakaṁ yogaṁ, dibbaṁ yogaṁ upaccagā; Sabbayogavisaṁyuttaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They’ve thrown off the human yoke, and slipped out of the heavenly yoke; unyoked from all yokes: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Hitvā mānusakaṁ yogaṁ, dibbaṁ yogaṁ upaccagā, sabbayogavisaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Abandoning the human yoke, overcoming the divine yoke, being unattached to all yokes, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Hitvā mānusakaṁ yogaṁ, dibbaṁ yogaṁ upaccagā, sabbayogavisaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Abandoning the human yoke, overcoming the divine yoke, being unattached to all yokes, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Hitvā ratiñca aratiñca, sītibhūtaṁ nirūpadhiṁ; Sabbalokābhibhuṁ vīraṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Giving up desire and discontent, they’re cooled and free of attachments; a hero, master of the whole world: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Hitvā ratiñ-ca aratiñ-ca, sītibhūtaṁ nirūpadhiṁ, sabbalokābhibhuṁ vīraṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Abandoning delight and aversion, cooled off and free from cleaving, a hero who vanquished the whole world, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Hitvā ratiñ-ca aratiñ-ca, sītibhūtaṁ nirūpadhiṁ, sabbalokābhibhuṁ vīraṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Abandoning delight and hate, cooled off and free from all cleaving, a hero who vanquished the world, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Cutiṁ yo vedi sattānaṁ, upapattiñca sabbaso; Asattaṁ sugataṁ buddhaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They know the passing away and rebirth of all beings; unattached, holy, awakened: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Cutiṁ yo vedi sattānaṁ upapattiñ-ca sabbaso, asattaṁ sugataṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever knows in every way beings’ passing and their rebirth, unattached, fortunate, awake, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Cutiṁ yo vedi sattānaṁ upapattiñ-ca sabbaso, asattaṁ sugataṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever knows in ev’ry way beings’ passing and their rebirth, unattached, happy and awake, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa gatiṁ na jānanti, devā gandhabbamānusā; Khīṇāsavaṁ arahantaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Gods, centaurs, and humans don’t know their destiny; the perfected ones with defilements ended: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yassa gatiṁ na jānanti devā gandhabbamānusā – khīṇāsavaṁ Arahantaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: For the one whose destiny is unknown to gods, gandhabbas and men – being pollutant-free, an Arahat, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Yassa pure ca pacchā ca, majjhe ca natthi kiñcanaṁ; Akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: They have nothing before or after, or even in between. Having nothing, taking nothing: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Yassa pure ca pacchā ca majjhe ca natthi kiñcanaṁ, akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: For whom there is nothing in the past, the future or the present, having nothing and unattached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Usabhaṁ pavaraṁ vīraṁ, mahesiṁ vijitāvinaṁ; Anejaṁ nhātakaṁ buddhaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: Captain of the herd, excellent hero, great seer and victor; unstirred, washed, awakened: that’s who I declare a brahmin.
interlinear_pali: Usabhaṁ pavaraṁ vīraṁ, mahesiṁ vijitāvinaṁ, anejaṁ nhātakaṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: A noble leader, heroic, a great seer, victorious, free of lust, cleansed and awakened, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Usabhaṁ pavaraṁ vīraṁ, mahesiṁ vijitāvinaṁ, anejaṁ nhātakaṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: A noble leader, heroic, a great seer, victorious, free of lust, cleansed and awakened, that one I say is a Brahmin.

pali_mahasangiti: Pubbenivāsaṁ yo vedi, saggāpāyañca passati; Atho jātikkhayaṁ patto, abhiññāvosito muni; Sabbavositavosānaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english_sujato: One who knows their past lives, sees heaven and places of loss, and has attained the end of rebirth; a sage of perfect insight at the summit of spiritual perfection: that’s who I declare a brahmin.  The Sayings of the Dhamma are complete.
interlinear_pali: Pubbenivāsaṁ yo vedī, saggāpāyañ-ca passati, atho jātikkhayaṁ patto, abhiññāvosito muni, sabbavositavosānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
interlinear_english: Whoever knows their former lives, and sees heaven and the downfall, and has attained birth’s destruction, the sage, accomplished in deep knowledge, who is accomplished in all accomplishments, that one I say is a brahmin.
narrative_pali: Pubbenivāsaṁ yo vedī, saggāpāyañ-ca passati, atho jātikkhayaṁ patto, abhiññāvosito muni, sabbavositavosānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
narrative_english: Whoever knows their former lives, and sees heaven and Apāya, and has attained birth’s destruction, the sage, accomplished in knowledge, who is accomplished in all things, that one I say is a Brahmin.
